# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation
# for comparing rates in cluster-randomized trials
# Reference: Hayes & Moulton, or Eldridge & Kerry textbooks
# Additive one-cluster correction applied

# Study parameters
p1 <- 0.005     # treatment rate per child-week
p0 <- 0.010     # control rate per child-week
E <- 2500       # exposure (child-weeks) per cluster
cv <- 0.15      # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05   # significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90

# Two-sided critical values
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # for two-sided test
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   # power side

cat("========== DESIGN PARAMETERS ==========\n")
cat("Treatment rate (p1):", p1, "per child-week\n")
cat("Control rate (p0):", p0, "per child-week\n")
cat("Exposure per cluster (E):", E, "child-weeks\n")
cat("Between-cluster CV:", cv, "\n")
cat("Two-sided alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Critical value z_alpha:", round(z_alpha, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical value z_beta:", round(z_beta, 4), "\n\n")

# Expected counts per cluster and arm
mu1 <- p1 * E   # treatment: expected events per cluster
mu0 <- p0 * E   # control: expected events per cluster

cat("========== EXPECTED COUNTS ==========\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (treatment, μ1):", mu1, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (control, μ0):", mu0, "\n")
cat("Rate difference (p1 - p0):", p1 - p0, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV approximation:
# For comparing two rates with Poisson distribution within clusters
# and log-normal variation between clusters:
# 
# Sample size per arm: n = (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/μ1 + 1/μ0) / (p1 - p0)²
#
# This formula treats the rate difference on the natural scale with CV inflation

cat("========== SAMPLE SIZE CALCULATION ==========\n")

numerator <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)
denominator <- (p1 - p0)^2

cat("Numerator: (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/μ1 + 1/μ0)\n")
cat("  = (", z_alpha, "+", z_beta, ")² × ", cv, "² × (1/", mu1, "+ 1/", mu0, ")\n")
cat("  = ", round(numerator, 6), "\n\n")

cat("Denominator: (p1 - p0)²\n")
cat("  = (", p1, "-", p0, ")²\n")
cat("  = ", round(denominator, 8), "\n\n")

n_continuous <- numerator / denominator

cat("Continuous solution: n = ", numerator, " / ", denominator, "\n")
cat("                    n = ", round(n_continuous, 3), " clusters per arm\n\n")

# Additive one-cluster correction
n_corrected <- n_continuous + 1
cat("With additive one-cluster correction: n = ", round(n_corrected, 3), "\n\n")

# Round to integer
n_per_arm <- ceiling(n_corrected)

cat("Integer clusters per arm (rounded up):", n_per_arm, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at different sample sizes
power_at_n <- function(n) {
  # For cluster-rate CV approximation:
  # Power ∝ sqrt(n) × (p1 - p0) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  # More precisely:
  z_stat <- sqrt(n) * (p1 - p0) / (cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  z_power_stat <- z_stat - z_alpha
  pnorm(z_power_stat)
}

power_continuous <- power_at_n(n_continuous)
power_corrected <- power_at_n(n_corrected)
power_integer <- power_at_n(n_per_arm)
power_preceding <- power_at_n(n_per_arm - 1)

cat("========== POWER VERIFICATION ==========\n")
cat("Power at n =", round(n_continuous, 3), "(continuous):", round(power_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", round(n_corrected, 3), "(with correction):", round(power_corrected, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_per_arm, "(selected integer):", round(power_integer, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_per_arm - 1, "(preceding design):", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n\n")

# Check if selected design meets power requirement
meets_power <- power_integer >= power_target

cat("========== FINAL ANSWER ==========\n")
cat("Clusters per arm:", n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Total clusters (both arms):", 2 * n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_integer, 4), "\n")
cat("Meets target power (", power_target, "):", meets_power, "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_per_arm - 1, "):", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_arm, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
    list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * n_per_arm, unit = "clusters"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_integer, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(n_continuous, 3), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
  )
)

library(jsonlite)
result_json_str <- toJSON(result_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)
cat("Result JSON:", result_json_str, "\n")

# Proper POWER_AGENT_RESULT format
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", result_json_str, "\n", sep="")

# The test statistic should follow standard normal under the null

p1 <- 0.005     
p0 <- 0.010     
E <- 2500       
cv <- 0.15      
alpha <- 0.05   
power_target <- 0.90

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   

mu1 <- p1 * E   
mu0 <- p0 * E   

cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("p1 =", p1, ", p0 =", p0, ", E =", E, ", cv =", cv, "\n")
cat("μ1 =", mu1, ", μ0 =", mu0, "\n")
cat("z_alpha =", z_alpha, ", z_beta =", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV formula
numerator <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)
denominator <- (p1 - p0)^2

n_continuous <- numerator / denominator
n_corrected <- n_continuous + 1
n_integer <- ceiling(n_corrected)

cat("Sample size calculation:\n")
cat("n_continuous =", round(n_continuous, 3), "\n")
cat("n_with_correction =", round(n_corrected, 3), "\n")
cat("n_integer =", n_integer, "\n\n")

# Power verification using correct formula:
# Under the cluster-rate CV approximation, the standardized test statistic is:
# Z = (p1 - p0) × sqrt(n) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
# 
# Under the null hypothesis (p1 = p0), Z ~ N(0,1)
# Under the alternative, Z has expectation (p1 - p0) × sqrt(n) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha | H1)

power_at_n <- function(n) {
  # Standardized effect size
  se_diff <- cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / sqrt(n)
  # Effect: p1 - p0
  effect <- p1 - p0
  # Standardized test statistic under H1
  z_noncentrality <- abs(effect) / se_diff  # abs because we care about magnitude
  # Power: P(|Z| > z_alpha)
  # For two-sided test: power = P(Z > z_alpha) + P(Z < -z_alpha)
  # When effect is in expected direction:
  power <- pnorm(z_noncentrality - z_alpha) + pnorm(-z_noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power
}

# Actually, let me reconsider. For a two-sided test with noncentrality parameter λ:
# Power = P(|Z| > z_alpha under H1)
# where the noncentrality is λ = |effect| / SE

power_at_n_v2 <- function(n) {
  se_diff <- cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / sqrt(n)
  noncentrality <- abs(p1 - p0) / se_diff
  
  # For two-sided test with noncentrality λ
  # Power = Φ(λ - z_alpha) + Φ(-λ - z_alpha)
  # But the second term is negligible when λ is positive
  # Standard approach: Power = Φ(λ - z_alpha)
  
  # Actually for two-sided:
  power_right <- pnorm(noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power_left <- pnorm(-noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power <- power_right + power_left
  power
}

# Let's use a simpler verification:
# At the sample size that solves the equation, by definition we achieve target power
# Check: (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 = [sqrt(n) × |p1-p0| / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1+1/mu0))]^2

verify_power <- function(n) {
  # Right-hand side of the power equation
  rhs_squared <- n * (p1 - p0)^2 / (cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  
  # At power_target, LHS = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
  lhs_target <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
  
  cat("For n =", n, ":\n")
  cat("  LHS (at power_target):", lhs_target, "\n")
  cat("  RHS (from n):", rhs_squared, "\n")
  cat("  Ratio RHS/LHS:", rhs_squared / lhs_target, "\n")
  
  # Power equation: Φ(sqrt(RHS) - z_alpha) = power_target
  implied_power <- pnorm(sqrt(rhs_squared) - z_alpha)
  cat("  Implied power:", round(implied_power, 4), "\n\n")
  
  implied_power
}

power_corrected <- verify_power(n_corrected)

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation
# for comparing rates in cluster-randomized trials
# with additive one-cluster correction

# Study parameters
p1 <- 0.005     # treatment rate per child-week
p0 <- 0.010     # control rate per child-week
E <- 2500       # exposure (child-weeks) per cluster
cv <- 0.15      # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05   # significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90

# Two-sided critical value
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # for two-sided test
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   # power side (one-sided critical value for power)

# Expected counts per cluster and arm
mu1 <- p1 * E   # treatment: expected events per cluster
mu0 <- p0 * E   # control: expected events per cluster

cat("Treatment rate:", p1, "per child-week\n")
cat("Control rate:", p0, "per child-week\n")
cat("Exposure per cluster:", E, "child-weeks\n")
cat("Between-cluster CV:", cv, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (treatment):", mu1, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (control):", mu0, "\n")
cat("Rate difference (p1 - p0):", p1 - p0, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV approximation formula:
# Under Poisson variation within clusters and log-normal heterogeneity between clusters,
# the variance of the log rate difference is approximately:
# Var(log(p1) - log(p0)) ≈ cv² * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)

# Variance of rate difference on the log scale
var_log_rd <- cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)

cat("Variance of log(rate difference):", var_log_rd, "\n")
cat("SE of log(rate difference):", sqrt(var_log_rd), "\n\n")

# For comparing means/rates with equal sample sizes n per arm,
# the test statistic on log scale has variance multiplied by 2/n
# (because we estimate separate log rates from n clusters per arm)

# Sample size calculation (continuous):
# (z_alpha + z_beta)² × 2 × var_log_rd = (log(p1/p0))² 
# But we work with rate difference on natural scale.
# 
# More directly for cluster-rate CV approximation:
# Sample size n per arm satisfies:
# (z_alpha + z_beta)² × [cv²/mu1 + cv²/mu0] / n = (p1 - p0)² / (p1 × p0)
# 
# Rearranged: n = (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / [(p1-p0)²/(p1×p0)]

numerator <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)
denominator <- (p1 - p0)^2 / (p1 * p0)

n_continuous <- numerator / denominator

cat("Numerator (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/μ1 + 1/μ0):", numerator, "\n")
cat("Denominator (Δp)²/(p1×p0):", denominator, "\n")
cat("Sample size (continuous):", n_continuous, "\n")

# Additive one-cluster correction: n_adj = n + 1
n_adj <- n_continuous + 1
cat("Sample size with one-cluster correction:", n_adj, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer
n_per_arm <- ceiling(n_continuous)
n_per_arm_corrected <- ceiling(n_adj)

cat("Integer clusters per arm (from continuous, no correction):", n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Integer clusters per arm (with one-cluster correction applied):", n_per_arm_corrected, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at selected design
# For a given n, power ∝ to the ratio:
# (p1 - p0)² × n / (cv² × (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))

power_achieved_continuous <- function(n) {
  test_stat_sq <- (p1 - p0)^2 * n / (cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  # Standard normal approximate power
  z_power <- sqrt(test_stat_sq) - z_alpha
  pnorm(z_power)
}

power_n_continuous <- power_achieved_continuous(n_continuous)
power_n_integer <- power_achieved_continuous(n_per_arm)
power_n_corrected <- power_achieved_continuous(n_per_arm_corrected)
power_preceding <- power_achieved_continuous(n_per_arm_corrected - 1)

cat("Verification of achieved power:\n")
cat("Power at continuous solution n =", round(n_continuous, 3), ":", round(power_n_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at integer solution n =", n_per_arm, ":", round(power_n_integer, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_per_arm_corrected, "(with one-cluster correction):", round(power_n_corrected, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design n =", n_per_arm_corrected - 1, ":", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n\n")

# Report final answer
cat("========================================\n")
cat("FINAL SAMPLE SIZE CALCULATION\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Design method: cluster_rate_cv (with additive one-cluster correction)\n")
cat("Clusters per arm (minimum integer):", n_per_arm_corrected, "\n")
cat("Total clusters (both arms):", 2 * n_per_arm_corrected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at selected design:", round(power_n_corrected, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")

# Structure for output
results <- list(
  sample_size = n_per_arm_corrected,
  sample_size_per_arm = n_per_arm_corrected,
  total_clusters = 2 * n_per_arm_corrected,
  continuous_solution = round(n_continuous, 3),
  power_achieved = round(power_n_corrected, 4),
  power_preceding = round(power_preceding, 4),
  target_power = power_target
)

cat("\nJSON output for result:\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_arm_corrected, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * n_per_arm_corrected, unit = "clusters"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_n_corrected, 4), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(n_continuous, 3), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation
# for comparing rates in cluster-randomized trials
# Reference: Hayes & Moulton, or Eldridge & Kerry textbooks
# Additive one-cluster correction applied

# Study parameters
p1 <- 0.005     # treatment rate per child-week
p0 <- 0.010     # control rate per child-week
E <- 2500       # exposure (child-weeks) per cluster
cv <- 0.15      # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05   # significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90

# Two-sided critical values
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # for two-sided test
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   # power side

cat("========== DESIGN PARAMETERS ==========\n")
cat("Treatment rate (p1):", p1, "per child-week\n")
cat("Control rate (p0):", p0, "per child-week\n")
cat("Exposure per cluster (E):", E, "child-weeks\n")
cat("Between-cluster CV:", cv, "\n")
cat("Two-sided alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Critical value z_alpha:", round(z_alpha, 4), "\n")
cat("Critical value z_beta:", round(z_beta, 4), "\n\n")

# Expected counts per cluster and arm
mu1 <- p1 * E   # treatment: expected events per cluster
mu0 <- p0 * E   # control: expected events per cluster

cat("========== EXPECTED COUNTS ==========\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (treatment, μ1):", mu1, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (control, μ0):", mu0, "\n")
cat("Rate difference (p1 - p0):", p1 - p0, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV approximation:
# For comparing two rates with Poisson distribution within clusters
# and log-normal variation between clusters:
# 
# Sample size per arm: n = (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/μ1 + 1/μ0) / (p1 - p0)²
#
# This formula treats the rate difference on the natural scale with CV inflation

cat("========== SAMPLE SIZE CALCULATION ==========\n")

numerator <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)
denominator <- (p1 - p0)^2

cat("Numerator: (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/μ1 + 1/μ0)\n")
cat("  = (", z_alpha, "+", z_beta, ")² × ", cv, "² × (1/", mu1, "+ 1/", mu0, ")\n")
cat("  = ", round(numerator, 6), "\n\n")

cat("Denominator: (p1 - p0)²\n")
cat("  = (", p1, "-", p0, ")²\n")
cat("  = ", round(denominator, 8), "\n\n")

n_continuous <- numerator / denominator

cat("Continuous solution: n = ", numerator, " / ", denominator, "\n")
cat("                    n = ", round(n_continuous, 3), " clusters per arm\n\n")

# Additive one-cluster correction
n_corrected <- n_continuous + 1
cat("With additive one-cluster correction: n = ", round(n_corrected, 3), "\n\n")

# Round to integer
n_per_arm <- ceiling(n_corrected)

cat("Integer clusters per arm (rounded up):", n_per_arm, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at different sample sizes
power_at_n <- function(n) {
  # For cluster-rate CV approximation:
  # Power ∝ sqrt(n) × (p1 - p0) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  # More precisely:
  z_stat <- sqrt(n) * (p1 - p0) / (cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  z_power_stat <- z_stat - z_alpha
  pnorm(z_power_stat)
}

power_continuous <- power_at_n(n_continuous)
power_corrected <- power_at_n(n_corrected)
power_integer <- power_at_n(n_per_arm)
power_preceding <- power_at_n(n_per_arm - 1)

cat("========== POWER VERIFICATION ==========\n")
cat("Power at n =", round(n_continuous, 3), "(continuous):", round(power_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", round(n_corrected, 3), "(with correction):", round(power_corrected, 4), "\n")

cat("Power at n =", n_per_arm - 1, "(preceding design):", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n\n")

# Check if selected design meets power requirement
meets_power <- power_integer >= power_target

cat("========== FINAL ANSWER ==========\n")
cat("Clusters per arm:", n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Total clusters (both arms):", 2 * n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_integer, 4), "\n")
cat("Meets target power (", power_target, "):", meets_power, "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_per_arm - 1, "):", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_arm, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
    list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * n_per_arm, unit = "clusters"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_integer, 4), unit = "probability"),

)

# Cluster-rate CV approximation with corrected power verification
# The test statistic should follow standard normal under the null

p1 <- 0.005     
p0 <- 0.010     
E <- 2500       
cv <- 0.15      
alpha <- 0.05   
power_target <- 0.90

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   

mu1 <- p1 * E   
mu0 <- p0 * E   

cat("Design Parameters:\n")
cat("p1 =", p1, ", p0 =", p0, ", E =", E, ", cv =", cv, "\n")
cat("μ1 =", mu1, ", μ0 =", mu0, "\n")
cat("z_alpha =", z_alpha, ", z_beta =", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV formula
numerator <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)
denominator <- (p1 - p0)^2

n_continuous <- numerator / denominator
n_corrected <- n_continuous + 1
n_integer <- ceiling(n_corrected)

cat("Sample size calculation:\n")
cat("n_continuous =", round(n_continuous, 3), "\n")
cat("n_with_correction =", round(n_corrected, 3), "\n")
cat("n_integer =", n_integer, "\n\n")

# Power verification using correct formula:
# Under the cluster-rate CV approximation, the standardized test statistic is:
# Z = (p1 - p0) × sqrt(n) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
# 
# Under the null hypothesis (p1 = p0), Z ~ N(0,1)
# Under the alternative, Z has expectation (p1 - p0) × sqrt(n) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha | H1)

power_at_n <- function(n) {
  # Standardized effect size
  se_diff <- cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / sqrt(n)
  # Effect: p1 - p0
  effect <- p1 - p0
  # Standardized test statistic under H1
  z_noncentrality <- abs(effect) / se_diff  # abs because we care about magnitude
  # Power: P(|Z| > z_alpha)
  # For two-sided test: power = P(Z > z_alpha) + P(Z < -z_alpha)
  # When effect is in expected direction:
  power <- pnorm(z_noncentrality - z_alpha) + pnorm(-z_noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power
}

# Actually, let me reconsider. For a two-sided test with noncentrality parameter λ:
# Power = P(|Z| > z_alpha under H1)
# where the noncentrality is λ = |effect| / SE

power_at_n_v2 <- function(n) {
  se_diff <- cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / sqrt(n)
  noncentrality <- abs(p1 - p0) / se_diff
  
  # For two-sided test with noncentrality λ
  # Power = Φ(λ - z_alpha) + Φ(-λ - z_alpha)
  # But the second term is negligible when λ is positive
  # Standard approach: Power = Φ(λ - z_alpha)
  
  # Actually for two-sided:
  power_right <- pnorm(noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power_left <- pnorm(-noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power <- power_right + power_left
  power
}

# Let's use a simpler verification:
# At the sample size that solves the equation, by definition we achieve target power
# Check: (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 = [sqrt(n) × |p1-p0| / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1+1/mu0))]^2

verify_power <- function(n) {
  # Right-hand side of the power equation
  rhs_squared <- n * (p1 - p0)^2 / (cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  
  # At power_target, LHS = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
  lhs_target <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
  
  cat("For n =", n, ":\n")
  cat("  LHS (at power_target):", lhs_target, "\n")
  cat("  RHS (from n):", rhs_squared, "\n")
  cat("  Ratio RHS/LHS:", rhs_squared / lhs_target, "\n")
  
  # Power equation: Φ(sqrt(RHS) - z_alpha) = power_target
  implied_power <- pnorm(sqrt(rhs_squared) - z_alpha)
  cat("  Implied power:", round(implied_power, 4), "\n\n")
  
  implied_power
}

power_continuous <- verify_power(n_continuous)
power_corrected <- verify_power(n_corrected)
power_integer <- verify_power(n_integer)
power_preceding <- verify_power(n_integer - 1)

cat("========== SUMMARY ==========\n")
cat("Selected design: n =", n_integer, "clusters per arm\n")
cat("Total clusters: ", 2 * n_integer, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_integer, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")

# Evidence e1; success=false

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation
# for comparing rates in cluster-randomized trials
# with additive one-cluster correction

# Study parameters
p1 <- 0.005     # treatment rate per child-week
p0 <- 0.010     # control rate per child-week
E <- 2500       # exposure (child-weeks) per cluster
cv <- 0.15      # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05   # significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90

# Two-sided critical value
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # for two-sided test
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   # power side (one-sided critical value for power)

# Expected counts per cluster and arm
mu1 <- p1 * E   # treatment: expected events per cluster
mu0 <- p0 * E   # control: expected events per cluster

cat("Treatment rate:", p1, "per child-week\n")
cat("Control rate:", p0, "per child-week\n")
cat("Exposure per cluster:", E, "child-weeks\n")
cat("Between-cluster CV:", cv, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (treatment):", mu1, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (control):", mu0, "\n")
cat("Rate difference (p1 - p0):", p1 - p0, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV approximation formula:
# Under Poisson variation within clusters and log-normal heterogeneity between clusters,
# the variance of the log rate difference is approximately:
# Var(log(p1) - log(p0)) ≈ cv² * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)

# Variance of rate difference on the log scale
var_log_rd <- cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)

cat("Variance of log(rate difference):", var_log_rd, "\n")
cat("SE of log(rate difference):", sqrt(var_log_rd), "\n\n")

# For comparing means/rates with equal sample sizes n per arm,
# the test statistic on log scale has variance multiplied by 2/n
# (because we estimate separate log rates from n clusters per arm)

# Sample size calculation (continuous):
# (z_alpha + z_beta)² × 2 × var_log_rd = (log(p1/p0))² 
# But we work with rate difference on natural scale.
# 
# More directly for cluster-rate CV approximation:
# Sample size n per arm satisfies:
# (z_alpha + z_beta)² × [cv²/mu1 + cv²/mu0] / n = (p1 - p0)² / (p1 × p0)
# 
# Rearranged: n = (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / [(p1-p0)²/(p1×p0)]

numerator <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)
denominator <- (p1 - p0)^2 / (p1 * p0)

n_continuous <- numerator / denominator

cat("Numerator (z_alpha + z_beta)² × cv² × (1/μ1 + 1/μ0):", numerator, "\n")
cat("Denominator (Δp)²/(p1×p0):", denominator, "\n")
cat("Sample size (continuous):", n_continuous, "\n")

# Additive one-cluster correction: n_adj = n + 1
n_adj <- n_continuous + 1
cat("Sample size with one-cluster correction:", n_adj, "\n\n")

# Round up to nearest integer
n_per_arm <- ceiling(n_continuous)
n_per_arm_corrected <- ceiling(n_adj)

cat("Integer clusters per arm (from continuous, no correction):", n_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Integer clusters per arm (with one-cluster correction applied):", n_per_arm_corrected, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at selected design
# For a given n, power ∝ to the ratio:
# (p1 - p0)² × n / (cv² × (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))

power_achieved_continuous <- function(n) {
  test_stat_sq <- (p1 - p0)^2 * n / (cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  # Standard normal approximate power
  z_power <- sqrt(test_stat_sq) - z_alpha
  pnorm(z_power)
}

power_n_continuous <- power_achieved_continuous(n_continuous)
power_n_integer <- power_achieved_continuous(n_per_arm)
power_n_corrected <- power_achieved_continuous(n_per_arm_corrected)
power_preceding <- power_achieved_continuous(n_per_arm_corrected - 1)

cat("Verification of achieved power:\n")
cat("Power at continuous solution n =", round(n_continuous, 3), ":", round(power_n_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at integer solution n =", n_per_arm, ":", round(power_n_integer, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", n_per_arm_corrected, "(with one-cluster correction):", round(power_n_corrected, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design n =", n_per_arm_corrected - 1, ":", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n\n")

# Report final answer
cat("========================================\n")
cat("FINAL SAMPLE SIZE CALCULATION\n")
cat("========================================\n")
cat("Design method: cluster_rate_cv (with additive one-cluster correction)\n")
cat("Clusters per arm (minimum integer):", n_per_arm_corrected, "\n")
cat("Total clusters (both arms):", 2 * n_per_arm_corrected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at selected design:", round(power_n_corrected, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")

# Structure for output
results <- list(
  sample_size = n_per_arm_corrected,
  sample_size_per_arm = n_per_arm_corrected,
  total_clusters = 2 * n_per_arm_corrected,
  continuous_solution = round(n_continuous, 3),
  power_achieved = round(power_n_corrected, 4),
  power_preceding = round(power_preceding, 4),
  target_power = power_target
)

cat("\nJSON output for result:\n")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_arm_corrected, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * n_per_arm_corrected, unit = "clusters"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_n_corrected, 4), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "probability"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(n_continuous, 3), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
)), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

cat("n_integer =", n_integer, "\n\n")

# Power verification using correct formula:
# Under the cluster-rate CV approximation, the standardized test statistic is:
# Z = (p1 - p0) × sqrt(n) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
# 
# Under the null hypothesis (p1 = p0), Z ~ N(0,1)
# Under the alternative, Z has expectation (p1 - p0) × sqrt(n) / (cv × sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha | H1)

power_at_n <- function(n) {
  # Standardized effect size
  se_diff <- cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / sqrt(n)
  # Effect: p1 - p0
  effect <- p1 - p0
  # Standardized test statistic under H1
  z_noncentrality <- abs(effect) / se_diff  # abs because we care about magnitude
  # Power: P(|Z| > z_alpha)
  # For two-sided test: power = P(Z > z_alpha) + P(Z < -z_alpha)
  # When effect is in expected direction:
  power <- pnorm(z_noncentrality - z_alpha) + pnorm(-z_noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power
}

# Actually, let me reconsider. For a two-sided test with noncentrality parameter λ:
# Power = P(|Z| > z_alpha under H1)
# where the noncentrality is λ = |effect| / SE

power_at_n_v2 <- function(n) {
  se_diff <- cv * sqrt(1/mu1 + 1/mu0) / sqrt(n)
  noncentrality <- abs(p1 - p0) / se_diff
  
  # For two-sided test with noncentrality λ
  # Power = Φ(λ - z_alpha) + Φ(-λ - z_alpha)
  # But the second term is negligible when λ is positive
  # Standard approach: Power = Φ(λ - z_alpha)
  
  # Actually for two-sided:
  power_right <- pnorm(noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power_left <- pnorm(-noncentrality - z_alpha)
  power <- power_right + power_left
  power
}

# At the sample size that solves the equation, by definition we achieve target power

verify_power <- function(n) {
  # Right-hand side of the power equation
  rhs_squared <- n * (p1 - p0)^2 / (cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  
  # At power_target, LHS = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
  lhs_target <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
  
  cat("For n =", n, ":\n")
  cat("  LHS (at power_target):", lhs_target, "\n")
  cat("  RHS (from n):", rhs_squared, "\n")
  cat("  Ratio RHS/LHS:", rhs_squared / lhs_target, "\n")
  
  # Power equation: Φ(sqrt(RHS) - z_alpha) = power_target
  implied_power <- pnorm(sqrt(rhs_squared) - z_alpha)
  cat("  Implied power:", round(implied_power, 4), "\n\n")

cat("Total clusters: ", 2 * n_integer, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_integer, 4), "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Meets target:", power_integer >= power_target, "\n")
cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_integer - 1, "):", round(power_preceding, 4), "\n")

# Output JSON
library(jsonlite)
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
    list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * n_integer, unit = "clusters"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_integer, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(n_continuous, 3), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
  )
)

result_json_str <- toJSON(result_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", result_json_str, "\n", sep="")


# Evidence e4; success=true

# Final verification with high precision
p1 <- 0.005     
p0 <- 0.010     
E <- 2500       
cv <- 0.15      
alpha <- 0.05   
power_target <- 0.90

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   

mu1 <- p1 * E   
mu0 <- p0 * E   

cat("FINAL VERIFICATION\n")
cat("=================\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV formula
numerator <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0)
denominator <- (p1 - p0)^2

n_continuous <- numerator / denominator
n_corrected <- n_continuous + 1

cat("Continuous solution: n =", format(n_continuous, digits = 10), "\n")
cat("With one-cluster correction: n =", format(n_corrected, digits = 10), "\n\n")

# Rounding: take ceiling of the corrected value
n_integer <- ceiling(n_corrected)
cat("Integer clusters per arm: n =", n_integer, "\n")
cat("(ceiling of", format(n_corrected, digits = 6), ")\n\n")

# Power at each relevant design
power_formula <- function(n) {
  rhs_squared <- n * (p1 - p0)^2 / (cv^2 * (1/mu1 + 1/mu0))
  pnorm(sqrt(rhs_squared) - z_alpha)
}

design_points <- c(n_integer - 1, n_integer, n_continuous, n_corrected)
names(design_points) <- c("preceding (n-1)", "selected (n)", "continuous", "corrected")

cat("Power at design points:\n")
for (i in seq_along(design_points)) {
  n <- design_points[i]
  power <- power_formula(n)
  meets <- ifelse(power >= power_target, "✓", "✗")
  cat("  n =", format(n, width=10, digits=8), 
      "  power =", format(power, digits=6), "  ", meets, "\n")
}

cat("\n")
cat("Selected design: n =", n_integer, "clusters per arm\n")
cat("Total clusters: ", 2 * n_integer, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", format(power_formula(n_integer), digits = 6), "\n")
cat("Target power:  ", power_target, "\n")

power_at_selected <- power_formula(n_integer)
power_at_preceding <- power_formula(n_integer - 1)

cat("\nPower comparison:\n")
cat("  Preceding design (n =", n_integer - 1, "): ", 
    format(power_at_preceding, digits = 6), "\n")
cat("  Selected design  (n =", n_integer, "): ", 
    format(power_at_selected, digits = 6), "\n")

# Final JSON output
library(jsonlite)
result_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_integer, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
    list(metric = "total_clusters", value = 2 * n_integer, unit = "clusters"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_selected, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_preceding, 4), unit = "probability"),
    list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(n_continuous, 3), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
    list(metric = "corrected_continuous", value = round(n_corrected, 3), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
  )
)

result_json_str <- toJSON(result_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15)
cat("\n\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", result_json_str, "\n", sep="")

plan.estimand: Probability of rejecting the null hypothesis of equal survival in a two-sample log-rank test
plan.hypothesis: H₀: λ_treatment = λ_control (equal hazard rates); H₁: λ_treatment ≠ λ_control
assumptions: Freedman approximation to the log-rank test
Two-sided hypothesis test at significance level α = 0.05
Equal allocation (1:1 treatment:control)
No loss to follow-up or censoring beyond specified event probabilities
Event probabilities represent the marginal probability of observing an event over the study period
Proportional hazards assumption holds
scientific_notes: The Freedman approximation for the log-rank test uses the event probabilities to estimate the variance under the null and alternative hypotheses
powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default implements this approximation; the function signature is powerCT(nEvents, hr, p0, p1, alpha, sided)
The user specifies event probabilities p0 (control) and p1 (treatment) rather than follow-up time and event rate parameters

answer.summary: Power for a two-sided log-rank comparison using the Freedman approximation with 200 participants per group, hazard ratio 0.7, and event probabilities of 0.3707 (treatment) and 0.4890 (control) is 0.6383 (63.83%).
answer.method: Freedman (1982) approximation to the log-rank test, implemented via powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default. The function computes power for the hypothesis H₀: HR = 1 versus H₁: HR ≠ 1 using the closed-form expression: power = Φ(√(k·m)·|HR−1|/(k·HR+1) − z₁₋α/₂), where m = nₑ·pₑ + nᴄ·pᴄ is the total expected number of events, k = nₑ/nᴄ is the allocation ratio, and Φ is the standard normal CDF.
assumptions: Freedman approximation valid for this sample size (large-sample approximation via central limit theorem)
Proportional hazards assumption holds
Event probabilities (0.3707 for treatment, 0.4890 for control) represent marginal cumulative probabilities over the study period
No loss to follow-up or censoring beyond what is captured by the event probabilities
Equal allocation (1:1 ratio) between treatment and control groups
Two-sided hypothesis test at α = 0.05
Hazard ratio of 0.7 represents the true underlying treatment effect
limitations: The Freedman approximation assumes large sample sizes and relies on normal approximation; with 200 per arm (~172 total expected events) this is generally adequate but not exact
Method requires event probabilities rather than time-to-event survival functions; does not directly account for specific follow-up duration or heterogeneous censoring patterns
Power is calculated assuming fixed event probabilities and does not account for design refinements such as adaptive sample size adjustment
No attrition adjustments included; assumes all enrolled participants contribute to follow-up

# Install and load powerSurvEpi package
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters
n_per_arm <- 200
allocation_ratio <- 1
hr <- 0.7  # Hazard ratio (treatment vs. control)
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # Event probability in treatment
p_control <- 0.4890    # Event probability in control
alpha <- 0.05
sided <- 2  # Two-sided test

# Expected number of events in each group
# Since we have equal allocation with 200 per arm:
# Total participants = 200 + 200 = 400
# Expected events in treatment arm = 200 * 0.3707
# Expected events in control arm = 200 * 0.4890

n_events_treatment <- n_per_arm * p_treatment
n_events_control <- n_per_arm * p_control
total_events <- n_events_treatment + n_events_control

cat("Study Design Summary:\n")
cat("=====================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size per arm: %d participants\n", n_per_arm))
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio: 1:1 (equal)\n"))
cat(sprintf("Total participants: %d\n", n_per_arm * 2))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (treatment): %.4f\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (control): %.4f\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("Expected events (treatment): %.2f\n", n_events_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Expected events (control): %.2f\n", n_events_control))
cat(sprintf("Total expected events: %.2f\n", total_events))
cat(sprintf("Hazard ratio: %.2f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Test: Two-sided log-rank (Freedman approximation)\n"))
cat("\n")

# Calculate power using powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default
# Function signature: powerCT(nEvents, hr, p0, p1, alpha, sided)
# nEvents: total number of events
# hr: hazard ratio
# p0: event probability in control group
# p1: event probability in treatment group
# alpha: significance level
# sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided

power_result <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT(
  nEvents = total_events,
  hr = hr,
  p0 = p_control,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  alpha = alpha,
  sided = sided
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("==========================\n")
cat(sprintf("Power: %.6f\n", power_result))
cat(sprintf("Power (percentage): %.2f%%\n", power_result * 100))

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power_result,
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("\nStructured Output:\n")
print(results)

============================
powerCT              package:powerSurvEpi              R Documentation

_ P_ o_ w_ e_ r _ C_ a_ l_ c_ u_ l_ a_ t_ i_ o_ n _ i_ n _ t_ h_ e _ A_ n_ a_ l_ y_ s_ i_ s _ o_ f _ S_ u_ r_ v_ i_ v_ a_ l _ D_ a_ t_ a _ f_ o_ r _ C_ l_ i_ n_ i_ c_ a_ l _ T_ r_ i_ a_ l_ s

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     Power calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves Between
     Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for clinical
     trials. Some parameters will be estimated based on a pilot data
     set.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     powerCT(formula, 
             dat, 
             nE, 
             nC, 
             RR, 
             alpha = 0.05)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

 formula: A formula object, e.g. ‘Surv(time, status) ~ x’, where ‘time’
          is a vector of survival/censoring time, ‘status’ is a vector
          of censoring indicator, ‘x’ is the group indicator, which is
          a factor object in R and takes only two possible values (‘C’
          for control group and ‘E’ for experimental group). See also
          the documentation of the function ‘survfit’ in the library
          ‘survival’.

     dat: a data frame representing the pilot data set and containing
          at least 3 columns: (1) survival/censoring time; (2)
          censoring indicator; (3) group indicator which is a factor
          object in R and takes only two possible values (‘C’ for
          control group and ‘E’ for experimental group).

      nE: integer. number of participants in the experimental group.

      nC: integer. number of participants in the control group.

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

   alpha: numeric. type I error rate.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     The movitation of this function is that some times we do not have
     information about m or p_E and p_C available, but we have a pilot
     data set that can be used to estimate p_E and p_C hence m, where
     m=n_E p_E + n_C p_C is the expected total number of events over
     both groups, n_E and n_C are numbers of participants in group E
     (experimental group) and group C (control group), respectively.
     p_E is the probability of failure in group E (experimental group)
     over the maximum time period of the study (t years).  p_C is the
     probability of failure in group C (control group) over the maximum
     time period of the study (t years).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the power of the test is

             power=Phi(sqrt{k*m}*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1)-z_{1-alpha/2}),        
     
     where

                             m=n_E p_E+n_C p_C,                         
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1), Phi is the cumulative
     distribution function (CDF) of N(0, 1).

     p_C and p_E can be calculated from the following formulaes:

                 p_C=sum_{i=1}^{t}D_i, p_E=sum_{i=1}^{t}E_i,            
     
     where D_i=lambda_i A_i C_i, E_i=RRlambda_i B_i C_i,
     A_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-lambda_j),
     B_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-RRlambda_j),
     C_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-delta_j).  And lambda_i is the probability
     of failure at time ‘i’ among participants in the control group,
     given that a participant has survived to time i-1 and is not
     censored at time i-1, i.e., the approximate hazard time i in the
     control group, i=1,...,t; RRlambda_i is the probability of failure
     at time ‘i’ among participants in the experimental group, given
     that a participant has survived to time i-1 and is not censored at
     time i-1, i.e., the approximate hazard time i in the experimental
     group, i=1,...,t; delta is the prbability that a participant is
     censored at time i given that he was followed up to time i and has
     not failed, i=0, 1, ..., t, which is assumed the same in each
     group.

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

mat.lambda: a matrix with 9 columns and ‘nTimes+1’ rows, where ‘nTimes’
          is the number of observed time points for the control group
          in the data set. The 9 columns are (1) ‘time’ - observed time
          point for the control group; (2) ‘lambda’; (3) ‘RRlambda’;
          (4) ‘delta’; (5) ‘A’; (6) ‘B’; (7) ‘C’; (8) ‘D’; (9) ‘E’.
          Please refer to the Details section for the definitions of
          elements of these quantities. See also Table 14.24 on page
          809 of Rosner (2006).

mat.event: a matrix with 5 columns and ‘nTimes+1’ rows, where ‘nTimes’
          is the number of observed time points for control group in
          the data set. The 5 columns are (1) ‘time’ - observed time
          point for the control group; (2) ‘nEvent.C’ - number of
          events in the control group at each time point; (3)
          ‘nCensored.C’ - number of censorings in the control group at
          each time point; (4) ‘nSurvive.C’ - number of alived in the
          control group at each time point; (5) ‘nRisk.C’ - number of
          participants at risk in the control group at each time point.
          Please refer to Table 14.12 on page 787 of Rosner (2006).

      pC: estimated probability of failure in group C (control group)
          over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pE: estimated probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

   power: the power of the test.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     (1) The estimates of RRlambda_i=RR*lambda_i. That is, ‘RRlambda’
     is not directly estimated based on data from the experimental
     group; (2) The power formula assumes that the central-limit
     theorem is valid and hence is appropriate for large samples.

_ R_ e_ f_ e_ r_ e_ n_ c_ e_ s:

     in clinical trials using the log-rank test.  _Statistics in

# Verify power calculation using Freedman approximation formula
# Reference: Freedman (1982), Rosner (2006)

# Study parameters
n_per_arm <- 200
hr <- 0.7
p_treatment <- 0.3707
p_control <- 0.4890
alpha <- 0.05
sided <- 2

cat("=== Manual Calculation of Power Using Freedman Approximation ===\n\n")

# Step 1: Calculate total expected events
n_events_treatment <- n_per_arm * p_treatment
n_events_control <- n_per_arm * p_control
total_events <- n_events_treatment + n_events_control

cat(sprintf("Expected events (treatment): %.6f\n", n_events_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Expected events (control): %.6f\n", n_events_control))
cat(sprintf("Total expected events (m): %.6f\n", total_events))
cat("\n")

# Step 2: Calculate allocation ratio k
k <- n_per_arm / n_per_arm  # should be 1.0
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio (k = nE/nC): %.6f\n", k))
cat("\n")

# Step 3: Calculate the test statistic component
# Formula: sqrt(k*m) * |RR - 1| / (k*RR + 1)
numerator_component <- sqrt(k * total_events) * abs(hr - 1)
denominator_component <- k * hr + 1
test_stat_component <- numerator_component / denominator_component

cat(sprintf("sqrt(k*m) = sqrt(%.6f * %.6f) = %.6f\n", k, total_events, sqrt(k * total_events)))
cat(sprintf("|HR - 1| = |%.6f - 1| = %.6f\n", hr, abs(hr - 1)))
cat(sprintf("k*HR + 1 = %.6f * %.6f + 1 = %.6f\n", k, hr, denominator_component))
cat(sprintf("Test statistic component: %.6f\n", test_stat_component))
cat("\n")

# Step 4: Calculate critical value for two-sided test
z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
cat(sprintf("Critical value z_{1-α/2} = z_{%.6f} = %.6f\n", 1 - alpha / 2, z_critical))
cat("\n")

# Step 5: Calculate the argument for the normal CDF
cdf_argument <- test_stat_component - z_critical
cat(sprintf("Argument for Φ: %.6f - %.6f = %.6f\n", test_stat_component, z_critical, cdf_argument))
cat("\n")

# Step 6: Calculate power
power_manual <- pnorm(cdf_argument)
cat(sprintf("Power = Φ(%.6f) = %.15f\n", cdf_argument, power_manual))
cat(sprintf("Power (percentage): %.2f%%\n", power_manual * 100))
cat("\n")

# Verify against powerSurvEpi result
library(powerSurvEpi)
power_package <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  nE = n_per_arm,
  nC = n_per_arm,
  pE = p_treatment,
  pC = p_control,
  RR = hr,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("=== Verification Against powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default ===\n\n")
cat(sprintf("Manual calculation: %.15f\n", power_manual))
cat(sprintf("Package result:     %.15f\n", power_package))
cat(sprintf("Difference:         %.2e\n", abs(power_manual - power_package)))
cat("\n")

if (abs(power_manual - power_package) < 1e-10) {
  cat("✓ Manual calculation matches package result (difference < 1e-10)\n")
} else {
  cat("⚠ Results differ slightly\n")
}

plan.hypothesis: H₀: λ_treatment = λ_control (equal hazard rates); H₁: λ_treatment ≠ λ_control
assumptions: Freedman approximation to the log-rank test
Two-sided hypothesis test at significance level α = 0.05
Equal allocation (1:1 treatment:control)
No loss to follow-up or censoring beyond specified event probabilities
Event probabilities represent the marginal probability of observing an event over the study period
Proportional hazards assumption holds
scientific_notes: The Freedman approximation for the log-rank test uses the event probabilities to estimate the variance under the null and alternative hypotheses
powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default implements this approximation; the function signature is powerCT(nEvents, hr, p0, p1, alpha, sided)
The user specifies event probabilities p0 (control) and p1 (treatment) rather than follow-up time and event rate parameters

# Install and load powerSurvEpi package
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters
n_per_arm <- 200
allocation_ratio <- 1
hr <- 0.7  # Hazard ratio (treatment vs. control)
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # Event probability in treatment
p_control <- 0.4890    # Event probability in control
alpha <- 0.05
sided <- 2  # Two-sided test

# Expected number of events in each group
# Since we have equal allocation with 200 per arm:
# Total participants = 200 + 200 = 400
# Expected events in treatment arm = 200 * 0.3707
# Expected events in control arm = 200 * 0.4890

n_events_treatment <- n_per_arm * p_treatment
n_events_control <- n_per_arm * p_control
total_events <- n_events_treatment + n_events_control

cat("Study Design Summary:\n")
cat("=====================\n")
cat(sprintf("Sample size per arm: %d participants\n", n_per_arm))
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio: 1:1 (equal)\n"))
cat(sprintf("Total participants: %d\n", n_per_arm * 2))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (treatment): %.4f\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (control): %.4f\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("Expected events (treatment): %.2f\n", n_events_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Expected events (control): %.2f\n", n_events_control))
cat(sprintf("Total expected events: %.2f\n", total_events))
cat(sprintf("Hazard ratio: %.2f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("Significance level (α): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Test: Two-sided log-rank (Freedman approximation)\n"))
cat("\n")

# Calculate power using powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default
# Function signature: powerCT(nEvents, hr, p0, p1, alpha, sided)
# nEvents: total number of events
# hr: hazard ratio
# p0: event probability in control group
# p1: event probability in treatment group
# alpha: significance level
# sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided

power_result <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT(
  nEvents = total_events,
  hr = hr,
  p0 = p_control,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  alpha = alpha,
  sided = sided
)

cat("Power Calculation Results:\n")
cat("==========================\n")
cat(sprintf("Power: %.6f\n", power_result))
cat(sprintf("Power (percentage): %.2f%%\n", power_result * 100))

# Output for structured reporting
results <- data.frame(
  metric = "power",
  value = power_result,
  unit = "probability"
)

cat("\nStructured Output:\n")
print(results)

     Power calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves Between
     Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for clinical

_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

 formula: A formula object, e.g. ‘Surv(time, status) ~ x’, where ‘time’
          is a vector of survival/censoring time, ‘status’ is a vector
          of censoring indicator, ‘x’ is the group indicator, which is
          a factor object in R and takes only two possible values (‘C’

          ‘survival’.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     The movitation of this function is that some times we do not have
     information about m or p_E and p_C available, but we have a pilot
     data set that can be used to estimate p_E and p_C hence m, where
     m=n_E p_E + n_C p_C is the expected total number of events over
     both groups, n_E and n_C are numbers of participants in group E
     (experimental group) and group C (control group), respectively.
     p_E is the probability of failure in group E (experimental group)
     over the maximum time period of the study (t years).  p_C is the
     probability of failure in group C (control group) over the maximum
     time period of the study (t years).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the power of the test is

             power=Phi(sqrt{k*m}*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1)-z_{1-alpha/2}),        
     
     where

                             m=n_E p_E+n_C p_C,                         
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1), Phi is the cumulative
     distribution function (CDF) of N(0, 1).

     p_C and p_E can be calculated from the following formulaes:

                 p_C=sum_{i=1}^{t}D_i, p_E=sum_{i=1}^{t}E_i,            
     
     where D_i=lambda_i A_i C_i, E_i=RRlambda_i B_i C_i,
     A_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-lambda_j),
     B_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-RRlambda_j),
     C_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-delta_j).  And lambda_i is the probability
     of failure at time ‘i’ among participants in the control group,
     given that a participant has survived to time i-1 and is not
     censored at time i-1, i.e., the approximate hazard time i in the
     control group, i=1,...,t; RRlambda_i is the probability of failure
     at time ‘i’ among participants in the experimental group, given
     that a participant has survived to time i-1 and is not censored at
     time i-1, i.e., the approximate hazard time i in the experimental
     group, i=1,...,t; delta is the prbability that a participant is
     censored at time i given that he was followed up to time i and has
     not failed, i=0, 1, ..., t, which is assumed the same in each
     group.

mat.lambda: a matrix with 9 columns and ‘nTimes+1’ rows, where ‘nTimes’

          (4) ‘delta’; (5) ‘A’; (6) ‘B’; (7) ‘C’; (8) ‘D’; (9) ‘E’.
          Please refer to the Details section for the definitions of
          elements of these quantities. See also Table 14.24 on page
          809 of Rosner (2006).

mat.event: a matrix with 5 columns and ‘nTimes+1’ rows, where ‘nTimes’

          the data set. The 5 columns are (1) ‘time’ - observed time
          point for the control group; (2) ‘nEvent.C’ - number of
          events in the control group at each time point; (3)
          ‘nCensored.C’ - number of censorings in the control group at
          each time point; (4) ‘nSurvive.C’ - number of alived in the
          control group at each time point; (5) ‘nRisk.C’ - number of
          participants at risk in the control group at each time point.
          Please refer to Table 14.12 on page 787 of Rosner (2006).

          over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pE: estimated probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

# Verify power calculation using Freedman approximation formula
# Reference: Freedman (1982), Rosner (2006)

# Study parameters
n_per_arm <- 200
hr <- 0.7
p_treatment <- 0.3707
p_control <- 0.4890
alpha <- 0.05
sided <- 2

cat("=== Manual Calculation of Power Using Freedman Approximation ===\n\n")

# Step 1: Calculate total expected events
n_events_treatment <- n_per_arm * p_treatment
n_events_control <- n_per_arm * p_control
total_events <- n_events_treatment + n_events_control

cat(sprintf("Expected events (treatment): %.6f\n", n_events_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Expected events (control): %.6f\n", n_events_control))
cat(sprintf("Total expected events (m): %.6f\n", total_events))
cat("\n")

# Step 2: Calculate allocation ratio k
k <- n_per_arm / n_per_arm  # should be 1.0
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio (k = nE/nC): %.6f\n", k))
cat("\n")

# Step 3: Calculate the test statistic component
# Formula: sqrt(k*m) * |RR - 1| / (k*RR + 1)
numerator_component <- sqrt(k * total_events) * abs(hr - 1)
denominator_component <- k * hr + 1
test_stat_component <- numerator_component / denominator_component

cat(sprintf("sqrt(k*m) = sqrt(%.6f * %.6f) = %.6f\n", k, total_events, sqrt(k * total_events)))
cat(sprintf("|HR - 1| = |%.6f - 1| = %.6f\n", hr, abs(hr - 1)))
cat(sprintf("k*HR + 1 = %.6f * %.6f + 1 = %.6f\n", k, hr, denominator_component))
cat(sprintf("Test statistic component: %.6f\n", test_stat_component))
cat("\n")

# Step 4: Calculate critical value for two-sided test
z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)
cat(sprintf("Critical value z_{1-α/2} = z_{%.6f} = %.6f\n", 1 - alpha / 2, z_critical))
cat("\n")

# Step 5: Calculate the argument for the normal CDF
cdf_argument <- test_stat_component - z_critical
cat(sprintf("Argument for Φ: %.6f - %.6f = %.6f\n", test_stat_component, z_critical, cdf_argument))
cat("\n")

# Step 6: Calculate power
power_manual <- pnorm(cdf_argument)
cat(sprintf("Power = Φ(%.6f) = %.15f\n", cdf_argument, power_manual))
cat(sprintf("Power (percentage): %.2f%%\n", power_manual * 100))
cat("\n")

# Verify against powerSurvEpi result
library(powerSurvEpi)
power_package <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  nE = n_per_arm,
  nC = n_per_arm,
  pE = p_treatment,
  pC = p_control,
  RR = hr,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("=== Verification Against powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default ===\n\n")
cat(sprintf("Manual calculation: %.15f\n", power_manual))
cat(sprintf("Package result:     %.15f\n", power_package))
cat(sprintf("Difference:         %.2e\n", abs(power_manual - power_package)))
cat("\n")

if (abs(power_manual - power_package) < 1e-10) {
  cat("✓ Manual calculation matches package result (difference < 1e-10)\n")
} else {
  cat("⚠ Results differ slightly\n")
}

  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     Power calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves Between
     Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for clinical
     trials. Some parameters will be estimated based on a pilot data

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     powerCT(formula, 
             dat, 
             nE, 
             nC, 
             RR, 
             alpha = 0.05)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

 formula: A formula object, e.g. ‘Surv(time, status) ~ x’, where ‘time’
          is a vector of survival/censoring time, ‘status’ is a vector
          of censoring indicator, ‘x’ is the group indicator, which is
          a factor object in R and takes only two possible values (‘C’
          for control group and ‘E’ for experimental group). See also
          the documentation of the function ‘survfit’ in the library
          ‘survival’.

     dat: a data frame representing the pilot data set and containing
          at least 3 columns: (1) survival/censoring time; (2)
          censoring indicator; (3) group indicator which is a factor
          object in R and takes only two possible values (‘C’ for
          control group and ‘E’ for experimental group).

      nC: integer. number of participants in the control group.

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     The movitation of this function is that some times we do not have
     information about m or p_E and p_C available, but we have a pilot
     data set that can be used to estimate p_E and p_C hence m, where
     m=n_E p_E + n_C p_C is the expected total number of events over
     both groups, n_E and n_C are numbers of participants in group E
     (experimental group) and group C (control group), respectively.
     p_E is the probability of failure in group E (experimental group)
     over the maximum time period of the study (t years).  p_C is the
     probability of failure in group C (control group) over the maximum
     time period of the study (t years).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the power of the test is

             power=Phi(sqrt{k*m}*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1)-z_{1-alpha/2}),        
     
     where

                             m=n_E p_E+n_C p_C,                         
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1), Phi is the cumulative
     distribution function (CDF) of N(0, 1).

     p_C and p_E can be calculated from the following formulaes:

                 p_C=sum_{i=1}^{t}D_i, p_E=sum_{i=1}^{t}E_i,            
     
     where D_i=lambda_i A_i C_i, E_i=RRlambda_i B_i C_i,
     A_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-lambda_j),
     B_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-RRlambda_j),
     C_i=prod_{j=0}^{i-1}(1-delta_j).  And lambda_i is the probability
     of failure at time ‘i’ among participants in the control group,
     given that a participant has survived to time i-1 and is not
     censored at time i-1, i.e., the approximate hazard time i in the
     control group, i=1,...,t; RRlambda_i is the probability of failure
     at time ‘i’ among participants in the experimental group, given
     that a participant has survived to time i-1 and is not censored at
     time i-1, i.e., the approximate hazard time i in the experimental
     group, i=1,...,t; delta is the prbability that a participant is
     censored at time i given that he was followed up to time i and has
     not failed, i=0, 1, ..., t, which is assumed the same in each
     group.

          participants at risk in the control group at each time point.
          Please refer to Table 14.12 on page 787 of Rosner (2006).

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation
# Field Trials of Health Interventions, Chapter 5, Section 6.1
# With additive one-cluster correction

# Input parameters
p_control <- 0.010      # Control event rate per child-week
p_treatment <- 0.005    # Treatment event rate per child-week
m_cluster <- 2500       # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.25           # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05           # Two-sided significance level
target_power <- 0.90    # Target power
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # Two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)   # Power parameter (one-sided)

cat("=== Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation Sample Size Calculation ===\n")
cat("Control rate (per child-week):", p_control, "\n")
cat("Treatment rate (per child-week):", p_treatment, "\n")
cat("Exposure per cluster (child-weeks):", m_cluster, "\n")
cat("Between-cluster CV (κ):", kappa, "\n")
cat("Two-sided alpha:", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("z_alpha (two-sided):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("z_beta (power):", z_beta, "\n\n")

# The approximation formula (without one-cluster correction):
# n = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * [κ^2 * (p_0 + p_1) + (p_0 + p_1)/(m_cluster)] / (p_0 - p_1)^2
# 
# With additive one-cluster correction:
# n_corrected = n + 1

# Difference in rates
delta_p <- p_control - p_treatment
cat("Difference in rates (p_0 - p_1):", delta_p, "\n\n")

# Average rate
p_avg <- (p_control + p_treatment) / 2
cat("Average rate (p_0 + p_1)/2:", p_avg, "\n")
cat("Sum of rates (p_0 + p_1):", p_control + p_treatment, "\n\n")

# Variance inflation term from CV approximation
# The cluster-rate CV method accounts for:
# 1. Between-cluster heterogeneity in rates: κ^2 * (p_0 + p_1)
# 2. Within-cluster Poisson variation: (p_0 + p_1) / m_cluster

variance_term_cv <- kappa^2 * (p_control + p_treatment)
variance_term_poisson <- (p_control + p_treatment) / m_cluster
total_variance_term <- variance_term_cv + variance_term_poisson

cat("Variance term from between-cluster CV: κ^2 * (p_0 + p_1) =", variance_term_cv, "\n")
cat("Variance term from Poisson variation: (p_0 + p_1) / m =", variance_term_poisson, "\n")
cat("Total variance term:", total_variance_term, "\n\n")

# Sample size per arm (before one-cluster correction)
z_sum_squared <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
numerator <- z_sum_squared * total_variance_term
denominator <- delta_p^2

n_uncorrected <- numerator / denominator

cat("(z_alpha + z_beta)^2 =", z_sum_squared, "\n")
cat("Numerator:", numerator, "\n")
cat("Denominator:", denominator, "\n")
cat("Uncorrected clusters per arm: n =", n_uncorrected, "\n\n")

# Apply additive one-cluster correction
n_corrected <- n_uncorrected + 1
cat("After one-cluster correction: n + 1 =", n_corrected, "\n\n")

# Round upward to next integer
n_final <- ceiling(n_corrected)
cat("Final clusters per arm (rounded upward):", n_final, "\n\n")

# Verification: compute achieved power at the final sample size
# We can verify by computing power backward using the formula
# Rearranging: power = P(Z > z_crit - (effect size * sqrt(n)))

# For the two-sided test:
# Effect size per cluster = delta_p / sqrt(variance_term)
se_per_cluster <- sqrt(total_variance_term / n_final)
z_critical_one_sided <- z_alpha  # For one-sided test at two-sided alpha/2
effect_size_standardized <- delta_p / sqrt(total_variance_term)
z_power_achieved <- sqrt(n_final) * effect_size_standardized

# For two-sided test, power = P(|Z| > z_alpha) under H1
# This is approximately P(Z > z_alpha - effect_size_standardized * sqrt(n))
power_achieved <- pnorm(z_power_achieved - z_alpha)

cat("=== Verification of Achieved Power ===\n")
cat("Standard error per cluster:", se_per_cluster, "\n")
cat("Standardized effect size:", effect_size_standardized, "\n")
cat("Z-statistic for power (noncentrality):", z_power_achieved, "\n")
cat("Achieved power (approximate):", power_achieved, "\n\n")

# More precise power calculation for two-sided test:
# Under H1, the test statistic sqrt(n) * delta_p / sqrt(total_variance_term) follows N(delta_p*sqrt(n)/sqrt(variance), 1)
# Power = P(|Z| > z_alpha | H1) where Z ~ N(sqrt(n)*delta_p/sqrt(variance), 1)
# = P(Z > z_alpha) + P(Z < -z_alpha) where Z ~ N(noncentrality, 1)

noncentrality <- sqrt(n_final) * delta_p / sqrt(total_variance_term)
power_upper <- 1 - pnorm(z_alpha - noncentrality)
power_lower <- pnorm(-z_alpha - noncentrality)
power_two_sided <- power_upper + power_lower

cat("=== Refined Power Calculation (Two-Sided) ===\n")
cat("Noncentrality parameter:", noncentrality, "\n")
cat("P(Z > z_alpha | H1):", power_upper, "\n")
cat("P(Z < -z_alpha | H1):", power_lower, "\n")
cat("Total two-sided power:", power_two_sided, "\n\n")

# Final results
cat("=== FINAL RESULTS ===\n")
cat("Sample size (clusters per arm):", n_final, "\n")
cat("Method: cluster_rate_cv (with one-cluster correction)\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_two_sided, 4), "\n")

# Independent implementation of cluster-rate CV approximation
# Reference: Field Trials of Health Interventions, Chapter 5, Section 6.1

# Study parameters
p0 <- 0.010      # Control rate per child-week
p1 <- 0.005      # Treatment rate per child-week
m <- 2500        # Exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.25    # Between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05    # Two-sided alpha
beta <- 0.10     # One minus target power
target_power <- 0.90

# Critical values (two-sided test)
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)      # Two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - beta)           # One-sided power critical value

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Input parameters:\n")
cat("  p0 (control, per child-week):", p0, "\n")
cat("  p1 (treatment, per child-week):", p1, "\n")
cat("  m (exposure per cluster):", m, "\n")
cat("  κ (between-cluster CV):", kappa, "\n")
cat("  α (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("  z_α (two-sided, α/2 =", alpha/2, "):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("  z_β (one-sided, β =", beta, "):", z_beta, "\n\n")

# The cluster-rate CV approximation formula:
# Var(rate_difference_per_cluster) = κ²(p₀ + p₁) + (p₀ + p₁)/m
# 
# Sample size formula (per arm):
# n = (z_α + z_β)² × Var / (p₀ - p₁)²

# Variance components
var_cv <- kappa^2 * (p0 + p1)       # Between-cluster variation
var_poisson <- (p0 + p1) / m        # Poisson variation (binomial approximation)
var_total <- var_cv + var_poisson

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  κ² × (p₀ + p₁):", var_cv, "\n")
cat("  (p₀ + p₁)/m:", var_poisson, "\n")
cat("  Total variance:", var_total, "\n\n")

# Effect size
delta_p <- p0 - p1
cat("Effect size (p₀ - p₁):", delta_p, "\n\n")

# Sample size calculation (uncorrected)
z_sum <- z_alpha + z_beta
n_uncorr <- (z_sum^2 * var_total) / (delta_p^2)

cat("Sample size calculation:\n")
cat("  (z_α + z_β)²:", z_sum^2, "\n")
cat("  n_uncorrected = (z_α + z_β)² × Var / (Δp)²\n")
cat("  n_uncorrected:", n_uncorr, "\n\n")

# Additive one-cluster correction
n_corrected <- n_uncorr + 1
cat("After one-cluster correction: n + 1 =", n_corrected, "\n")

# Final rounding (upward)
n_final <- ceiling(n_corrected)
cat("After ceiling rounding: n_final =", n_final, "\n\n")

# ==================================================
# Power verification at the final sample size
# ==================================================

compute_power_at_n <- function(n_per_arm, p0, p1, m, kappa, alpha) {
  # Variance per cluster
  var_total <- kappa^2 * (p0 + p1) + (p0 + p1) / m
  
  # Standard error of rate difference
  se <- sqrt(var_total / n_per_arm)
  
  # Effect size
  delta_p <- p0 - p1
  
  # Noncentrality parameter (for one-sided test)
  z_alpha_two <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
  noncentrality <- delta_p / se
  
  # Power for two-sided test
  # P(reject H0 | H1) = P(|Z| > z_alpha | Z ~ N(noncentrality, 1))
  # = P(Z > z_alpha - noncentrality) + P(Z < -z_alpha - noncentrality)
  
  power_right <- 1 - pnorm(z_alpha_two - noncentrality)
  power_left <- pnorm(-z_alpha_two - noncentrality)
  power_total <- power_right + power_left
  
  return(list(power = power_total, se = se, noncentrality = noncentrality))
}

# Check power at final sample size
result_final <- compute_power_at_n(n_final, p0, p1, m, kappa, alpha)
cat("Power verification at n =", n_final, ":\n")
cat("  Standard error:", result_final$se, "\n")
cat("  Noncentrality parameter:", result_final$noncentrality, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", result_final$power, "\n\n")

# Check power at preceding design (n - 1)
result_preceding <- compute_power_at_n(n_final - 1, p0, p1, m, kappa, alpha)
cat("Power at n =", n_final - 1, ":\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", result_preceding$power, "\n\n")

# Verify that n_final is the smallest design meeting target
cat("=== Validation ===\n")
cat("n =", n_final - 1, ": power =", format(result_preceding$power, digits=6), 
    "(target 0.90):", result_preceding$power >= 0.90, "\n")
cat("n =", n_final, ": power =", format(result_final$power, digits=6), 
    "(target 0.90):", result_final$power >= 0.90, "\n\n")

cat("=== CONCLUSION ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm (target power 90%): ", n_final, "\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", format(result_final$power, digits=6), "\n")

# The "additive one-cluster correction" in cluster-randomized trial design
# typically refers to adding 1 to the uncorrected sample size to account
# for the discrete nature of clusters (rather than treating clusters as
# infinitely divisible).
#
# However, the question is: at what stage is this +1 applied?
# And what is the rounding convention?

cat("=== CLARIFICATION OF ADDITIVE ONE-CLUSTER CORRECTION ===\n\n")

cat("In cluster-randomized trial literature, the 'one-cluster correction'\n")
cat("has been used in different ways:\n\n")

cat("Standard Interpretation 1 (Hayes & Moulton, 2009):\n")
cat("  For designs with very few clusters, add 1 to account for the\n")
cat("  discrete nature of the clustering and to ensure conservative\n")
cat("  estimation. This is typically applied BEFORE rounding.\n\n")

cat("Standard Interpretation 2 (Donner & Klar):\n")
cat("  The 'one-cluster correction' is specific to matched-pair designs\n")
cat("  or certain structures. Not universally applied.\n\n")

cat("In the context of the Field Trials reference (Chapter 5, Section 6.1),\n")
cat("the cluster-rate CV method is an APPROXIMATION for:\n")
cat("  - Clustered count outcomes\n")
cat("  - With between-cluster heterogeneity (quantified by κ)\n\n")

# The user's request explicitly mentions:
# "Use the cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation in 
#  Field Trials of Health Interventions Chapter 5, Section 6.1,
#  INCLUDING ITS ADDITIVE ONE-CLUSTER CORRECTION."

# This suggests the correction is part of the method AS DESCRIBED IN THAT REFERENCE.

cat("=== AMBIGUITY IN ROUNDING SEQUENCE ===\n\n")

cat("Option A: Apply correction BEFORE rounding\n")
cat("  1. Compute n_formula = 396.5501\n")
cat("  2. Add 1: n_adj = 397.5501\n")
cat("  3. ceiling(397.5501) = 398\n\n")

cat("Option B: Apply correction AFTER rounding\n")
cat("  1. Compute n_formula = 396.5501\n")
cat("  2. ceiling(396.5501) = 397\n")
cat("  3. Add 1: 397 + 1 = 398\n\n")

cat("Option C: Apply correction as threshold adjustment\n")
cat("  1. Compute n_formula = 396.5501\n")
cat("  2. ceiling(396.5501) = 397\n")
cat("  3. This is the 'corrected' minimum sample size\n\n")

cat("=== ANALYSIS OF USER INTENT ===\n\n")

cat("The user request says: 'rounding upward'\n")
cat("This suggests: apply ceiling operation as the final step.\n\n")

cat("The candidate's approach (Option A):\n")
cat("  ceiling(n_uncorrected + 1) = ceiling(397.5501) = 398\n")
cat("  Power achieved: 90.10%\n")
cat("  MEETS target of 90%? YES\n\n")

cat("Alternative approach (Option C - ceiling first, add 1 second):\n")
cat("  ceiling(396.5501) + 1 = 397 + 1 = 398\n")
cat("  Power achieved: 90.10%\n")
cat("  MEETS target of 90%? YES\n\n")

cat("Both standard applications of the correction yield n=398.\n\n")

cat("=== KEY FINDING ===\n\n")

cat("The candidate answer of 398 is CONSISTENT WITH the formula prescription:\n")
cat("  - Apply the uncorrected formula: 396.5501\n")
cat("  - Add 1 for one-cluster correction: 397.5501\n")
cat("  - Round upward: ceiling(397.5501) = 398\n\n")

cat("The fact that n=397 also meets the 90% target is NOT a flaw in the answer,\n")
cat("because the method does not prescribe searching for the minimum n;\n")
cat("it prescribes a specific formula-based procedure.\n\n")

cat("However, there IS a question about interpretation:\n")
cat("Is 'additive one-cluster correction' a CORRECTION to the formula,\n")
cat("or is it part of the formula itself?\n\n")

cat("If it is a standard correction (as suggested by the user's explicit mention),\n")
cat("then n=398 is correct per the method.\n\n")

cat("If the user intended 'rounding upward' to mean 'find smallest n meeting target',\n")
cat("then n=397 would be the answer.\n\n")

cat("ceiling(396.5501) =", n_ceiling_uncorr, "\n")

cat("Meets 90% target?", power_ceiling_uncorr >= 0.90, "\n\n")

cat("This shows that the uncorrected formula's ceiling (n=397) ALREADY meets\n")
cat("the 90% power target. The one-cluster correction adds a buffer.\n\n")

cat("=== CONCLUSION ===\n\n")
cat("The candidate's answer of n=398 is METHODOLOGICALLY CORRECT per the\n")

# the typical variance of the rate difference is:
#   Var(ρ₀ - ρ₁) = Var(ρ₀) + Var(ρ₁)
#
# When each cluster has exposure m and event rate p:
#   - Within-cluster: E[count] = mp, Var[count] ~ mp (Poisson)
#   - Cluster rate: ρ = count/m, so Var[ρ] ~ p/m (within-cluster variation)
#   - Between-cluster heterogeneity modeled by κ: Var[ρ] ~ κ²p²
#   - Total: Var[ρ] ~ κ²p² + p/m
#
# For the DIFFERENCE ρ₀ - ρ₁:
#   Var(ρ₀ - ρ₁) = Var(ρ₀) + Var(ρ₁) = κ²p₀² + p₀/m + κ²p₁² + p₁/m

cat("Standard cluster-rate variance (heterogeneity + Poisson):\n")
cat("  Var(ρ) = κ²p² + p/m  [per cluster]\n\n")

cat("For the difference between two clusters:\n")

Additive one-cluster correction applied

Two-sided hypothesis test with alpha = 0.05
Event rates are constant within study period
