# Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation Approximation
# Field Trials of Health Interventions, Chapter 5, Section 5.1
# with additive one-cluster correction

# Input parameters
lambda0 <- 0.010  # control event rate per child-week
lambda1 <- 0.005  # treatment event rate per child-week
m <- 2500         # exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.25     # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05     # significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90  # target power

# Critical values
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided, α = 0.05 → z = 1.96
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   # one-sided, power = 0.90 → z = 1.282

cat("Critical values:\n")
cat("  z_alpha (two-sided, α=0.05):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("  z_beta (power=0.90):", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu0 <- m * lambda0  # control: 2500 * 0.010 = 25
mu1 <- m * lambda1  # treatment: 2500 * 0.005 = 12.5

cat("Expected event counts per cluster:\n")
cat("  Control (μ₀):", mu0, "\n")
cat("  Treatment (μ₁):", mu1, "\n")
cat("  Difference (μ₀ - μ₁):", mu0 - mu1, "\n\n")

# Variance components under the cluster-rate CV model
# The design effect for rate is: 1 + κ²(m - 1)
# where κ is the coefficient of variation and m is exposure per cluster
design_effect <- 1 + (kappa^2) * (m - 1)

cat("Design effect calculation:\n")
cat("  κ² =", kappa^2, "\n")
cat("  m - 1 =", m - 1, "\n")
cat("  Design effect = 1 + κ²(m-1) =", design_effect, "\n\n")

# Variance of rate difference under cluster design
# Var(λ₀ - λ₁) ≈ design_effect * (λ₀/m + λ₁/m)
# Standard error of the rate difference
var_rate_diff <- design_effect * (lambda0/m + lambda1/m)
se_rate_diff <- sqrt(var_rate_diff)

cat("Variance and SE of rate difference:\n")
cat("  λ₀/m + λ₁/m =", lambda0/m + lambda1/m, "\n")
cat("  Var(λ₀ - λ₁) =", var_rate_diff, "\n")
cat("  SE(λ₀ - λ₁) =", se_rate_diff, "\n\n")

# Rate difference (effect size)
delta <- lambda0 - lambda1

cat("Effect size:\n")
cat("  Rate difference (Δ) = λ₀ - λ₁ =", delta, "\n\n")

# Sample size formula (clusters per arm)
# n = (z_alpha + z_beta)² * Var(λ₀ - λ₁) / Δ²
# Which can be rewritten as:
# n = (z_alpha + z_beta)² * SE² / Δ²

n_continuous <- ((z_alpha + z_beta)^2) * var_rate_diff / (delta^2)

cat("Continuous sample size (clusters per arm, before correction):\n")
cat("  n = (z_α + z_β)² * Var(Δ) / Δ²\n")
cat("  n = (", z_alpha, "+", z_beta, ")² *", var_rate_diff, "/", delta^2, "\n")
cat("  n =", n_continuous, "\n\n")

# Additive one-cluster correction
# This accounts for discreteness in cluster counts
n_with_correction <- n_continuous + 1

cat("With additive one-cluster correction:\n")
cat("  n = ", n_continuous, "+ 1 =", n_with_correction, "\n\n")

# Rounding upward to nearest integer
n_rounded <- ceiling(n_with_correction)

cat("Rounded upward to nearest integer:\n")
cat("  n_per_arm =", n_rounded, "clusters per arm\n")
cat("  Total clusters = 2 ×", n_rounded, "=", 2*n_rounded, "\n\n")

# Verification: Calculate achieved power at selected sample size
z_achieved <- delta / se_rate_diff * sqrt(n_rounded)
power_achieved <- pnorm(z_achieved - z_alpha)

cat("Verification of achieved power at n =", n_rounded, ":\n")
cat("  z_achieved =", z_achieved, "\n")
cat("  Power achieved =", power_achieved, "\n\n")

# Also check power at preceding admissible design (n-1)
n_preceding <- n_rounded - 1
z_preceding <- delta / se_rate_diff * sqrt(n_preceding)
power_preceding <- pnorm(z_preceding - z_alpha)

cat("Power at preceding design (n =", n_preceding, "):\n")
cat("  z =", z_preceding, "\n")
cat("  Power =", power_preceding, "\n\n")

# Summary output
cat("="*60, "\n")
cat("SUMMARY\n")
cat("="*60, "\n")
cat("Sample size (clusters per arm):", n_rounded, "\n")
cat("Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_achieved, "\n")
cat("Power (preceding design):", power_preceding, "\n")

# JSON output
results <- list(
  sample_size = n_rounded,
  unit = "clusters_per_arm",
  continuous_solution = n_continuous,
  with_correction = n_with_correction,
  achieved_power = power_achieved,
  power_preceding = power_preceding
)

cat("\n")
print(jsonlite::toJSON(results, auto_unbox=TRUE, digits=15))

# Independent verification of the cluster-rate CV approximation
# Field Trials of Health Interventions, Hayes & Moulton, Chapter 5

# Study parameters
lambda0 <- 0.010  # control rate per child-week
lambda1 <- 0.005  # treatment rate per child-week
m <- 2500         # exposure per cluster
kappa <- 0.25     # between-cluster CV
alpha <- 0.05
power_target <- 0.90

# Critical values for two-sided test
z_crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)      # 1.96 for α=0.05
z_power <- qnorm(power_target)    # 1.282 for power=0.90

cat("INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION\n")
cat("========================\n\n")

# Step 1: Design effect
# DE = 1 + κ²(m - 1)
DE <- 1 + (kappa^2) * (m - 1)
cat("Design effect:\n")
cat("  DE = 1 + κ²(m - 1)\n")
cat("  DE = 1 + (0.25)² × (2500 - 1)\n")
cat("  DE = 1 + 0.0625 × 2499\n")
cat("  DE =", DE, "\n\n")

# Step 2: Variance of the rate difference
# Under cluster design with equal allocation (1:1):
# Var(λ₀ - λ₁) = DE × (λ₀/m + λ₁/m) / (2 × 1 × 1)
# For equal allocation, the denominator simplifies; this is variance PER ARM
# Actually, in the sample size formula context, we need:
# Var(λ₀ - λ₁) = DE × (λ₀ + λ₁) / m  [pooled variance for two-arm comparison]

# Let me verify the exact formula from Hayes & Moulton approach
# For two independent clusters (one from each arm), the variance of difference is:
# Var(λ₀ - λ₁) = DE × (λ₀/m + λ₁/m)

var_diff <- DE * (lambda0/m + lambda1/m)
se_diff <- sqrt(var_diff)

cat("Variance of rate difference:\n")
cat("  Var(λ₀ - λ₁) = DE × (λ₀/m + λ₁/m)\n")
cat("  Var(λ₀ - λ₁) =", DE, "×", (lambda0/m + lambda1/m), "\n")
cat("  Var(λ₀ - λ₁) =", var_diff, "\n")
cat("  SE(λ₀ - λ₁) =", se_diff, "\n\n")

# Step 3: Rate difference (effect size)
delta <- lambda0 - lambda1
cat("Rate difference (effect size):\n")
cat("  Δ = λ₀ - λ₁ =", delta, "\n\n")

# Step 4: Sample size formula
# For two-sided test with equal allocation:
# n = (z_α + z_β)² × Var(λ₀ - λ₁) / Δ²

n_cont <- ((z_crit + z_power)^2) * var_diff / (delta^2)
cat("Sample size (continuous, per arm):\n")
cat("  n = (z_α + z_β)² × Var(Δ) / Δ²\n")
cat("  n = (", z_crit, "+", z_power, ")² ×", var_diff, "/", delta^2, "\n")
cat("  n = (", z_crit + z_power, ")² ×", var_diff, "/", delta^2, "\n")
cat("  n =", n_cont, "\n\n")

# Step 5: Additive one-cluster correction
n_corr <- n_cont + 1
cat("With additive one-cluster correction:\n")
cat("  n = ", n_cont, "+ 1 =", n_corr, "\n\n")

# Step 6: Rounding upward
n_final <- ceiling(n_corr)
cat("Rounding upward to integer:\n")
cat("  n =", n_final, "clusters per arm\n\n")

# Step 7: Verify achieved power at n_final
# Power formula: Power = Φ(z_achieved - z_α)

cat("Total clusters:", 2 * n_final, "\n")

# - Design effect DE = 1 + κ²(m - 1) inflates variance due to clustering

# Ha: λ₀ ≠ λ₁ (two-sided)

# n = (z_α/2 + z_β)² × DE × (λ₀ + λ₁) / (λ₀ - λ₁)² / m
# OR equivalently:
# n = (z_α/2 + z_β)² × Var(λ₀ - λ₁) / (λ₀ - λ₁)²

# Let me verify both formulations give the same result

lambda0 <- 0.010
lambda1 <- 0.005
m <- 2500
kappa <- 0.25
DE <- 1 + (kappa^2) * (m - 1)
alpha <- 0.05
power_target <- 0.90

# and power calculation method

power_target <- 0.90
alpha <- 0.05

# The critical value for power calculation:
# For a one-sided rejection region in hypothesis testing power calculation
# Power = P(reject H0 | Ha true)
# = P(Z > z_α/2 | H1 true)
# = P(Z - δ/SE > z_α/2 - δ/SE | H1 true) where Z ~ N(δ/SE, 1)
# = P(Standard Normal > z_α/2 - δ/SE)
# = 1 - Φ(z_α/2 - δ/SE)
# = Φ(δ/SE - z_α/2)

# So for a given power level:
# Power = Φ(δ/SE × √n - z_α/2) = target_power
# δ/SE × √n - z_α/2 = Φ⁻¹(target_power) = z_power
# δ/SE × √n = z_α/2 + z_power

# Therefore:
# n = (z_α/2 + z_power)² × (SE/δ)²
# n = (z_α/2 + z_power)² × Var(δ) / δ²

z_alpha_onetail <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)      # 1.96 (for two-sided test)
z_power_val <- qnorm(power_target)         # 1.282 (critical value for power)

cat("Power Calculation Critical Values\n")

cat("Target power: 0.90\n")
cat("Alpha (two-sided): 0.05\n\n")

cat("  z =", z_alpha_onetail, "\n\n")

cat("z_power (critical value for power calculation):\n")
cat("  z = qnorm(power_target) = qnorm(0.90)\n")
cat("  z =", z_power_val, "\n\n")

cat("Interpretation:\n")
cat("  The sum (z_α/2 + z_power) = ", z_alpha_onetail + z_power_val, "\n")

# Cluster-Rate Coefficient-of-Variation Approximation
# Field Trials of Health Interventions, Chapter 5, Section 5.1
# with additive one-cluster correction

# Input parameters
lambda0 <- 0.010  # control event rate per child-week
lambda1 <- 0.005  # treatment event rate per child-week
m <- 2500         # exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
kappa <- 0.25     # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05     # significance level (two-sided)
power_target <- 0.90  # target power

# Critical values
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided, α = 0.05 → z = 1.96
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)   # one-sided, power = 0.90 → z = 1.282

cat("Critical values:\n")
cat("  z_alpha (two-sided, α=0.05):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("  z_beta (power=0.90):", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu0 <- m * lambda0  # control: 2500 * 0.010 = 25
mu1 <- m * lambda1  # treatment: 2500 * 0.005 = 12.5

cat("Expected event counts per cluster:\n")
cat("  Control (μ₀):", mu0, "\n")
cat("  Treatment (μ₁):", mu1, "\n")
cat("  Difference (μ₀ - μ₁):", mu0 - mu1, "\n\n")

# Variance components under the cluster-rate CV model
# The design effect for rate is: 1 + κ²(m - 1)
# where κ is the coefficient of variation and m is exposure per cluster
design_effect <- 1 + (kappa^2) * (m - 1)

cat("Design effect calculation:\n")
cat("  κ² =", kappa^2, "\n")
cat("  m - 1 =", m - 1, "\n")
cat("  Design effect = 1 + κ²(m-1) =", design_effect, "\n\n")

# Variance of rate difference under cluster design

answer.summary: Power calculation for two-sided log-rank test comparing survival curves using the Freedman approximation. With 200 participants per group (400 total), hazard ratio 0.7 (treatment vs control), event probabilities 0.3707 (treatment) and 0.4890 (control), and significance level α=0.05, the achieved power is 0.6383 (63.83%).
answer.method: Freedman approximation for log-rank test (Freedman 1982, as implemented in powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default). The formula is: power = Φ(√(km)|RR−1|/(kRR+1) − z_{1−α/2}), where k=n_E/n_C (allocation ratio), m=n_E·p_E+n_C·p_C (expected total events), RR is the hazard ratio, and Φ is the standard normal CDF.
assumptions: Two-sided log-rank test at significance level α = 0.05
Equal allocation ratio (1:1)
Hazard ratio 0.7 represents the true treatment effect
Event probabilities (0.3707 treatment, 0.4890 control) are marginal probabilities over the maximum study follow-up period
Underlying Cox proportional hazards model with constant hazard ratio
Normal approximation via Freedman method is valid (assumes sufficiently large sample size)
limitations: The Freedman approximation assumes the central limit theorem is valid; appropriateness depends on the observed number of events (171.94 expected)
The formula does not account for specific censoring distributions, only marginal event probabilities
No adjustment for multiple comparisons, interim analyses, or departures from proportional hazards assumption
Marginal event probabilities must be provided; the calculation does not derive them from survival curves or follow-up times

# Install and load powerSurvEpi
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")
}
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Study parameters
n_per_group <- 200
total_n <- n_per_group * 2
hr <- 0.7  # Hazard ratio (treatment vs control)
alpha <- 0.05
event_prob_treatment <- 0.3707
event_prob_control <- 0.4890

# Calculate expected number of events
n_events_treatment <- n_per_group * event_prob_treatment
n_events_control <- n_per_group * event_prob_control
total_events <- n_events_treatment + n_events_control

cat("Study Design:\n")
cat("  Sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("  Total sample size:", total_n, "\n")
cat("  Total expected events:", total_events, "\n")
cat("  Expected events (treatment):", n_events_treatment, "\n")
cat("  Expected events (control):", n_events_control, "\n")
cat("  Hazard ratio:", hr, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (α):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Two-sided test\n\n")

# Use powerCT.default with Freedman approximation
# Parameters:
# - type: "two.sided" for two-sided test
# - alpha: significance level
# - beta: 1 - power (we'll solve for power, so we leave as NULL and check return)
# - hr: hazard ratio
# - n: total sample size (we use n_per_group * 2 for total)
# - p_event_ctrl: event probability in control group
# - p_event_trt: event probability in treatment group

# powerCT.default uses Freedman approximation
power_result <- powerCT.default(
  type = "two.sided",
  alpha = alpha,
  beta = NULL,  # We want to compute power (1 - beta)
  hr = hr,
  n = total_n,
  p_event_ctrl = event_prob_control,
  p_event_trt = event_prob_treatment
)

cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
print(power_result)

# Extract the power value
power <- 1 - power_result$beta
cat("\nComputed Power:", power, "\n")

# Return result in required format
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", results_json, "\n")

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

answer.summary: Power calculation for a two-sided log-rank test comparing survival curves between treatment and control groups under the Freedman approximation, as implemented by powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default version 0.1.5. With 200 participants per group (400 total), an expected event probability of 0.3707 in the treatment group and 0.4890 in the control group, a postulated hazard ratio of 0.7, and significance level α = 0.05, the achieved power is 0.6383 (approximately 63.83%).
answer.method: Freedman (1982) approximation for log-rank test power, implemented by powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default. The method applies the formula: power = Φ(√(k·m)·|RR − 1|/(k·RR + 1) − z₁₋α/₂), where m = nE·pE + nC·pC, k = nE/nC, RR is the hazard ratio, and Φ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function. For two-sided test, z₁₋α/₂ = 1.96 (critical value at α = 0.05).
assumptions: Two-sided log-rank test under the Cox proportional hazards model
Equal allocation: 200 treatment (experimental), 200 control
Significance level α = 0.05
Hazard ratio HR = 0.7 (treatment vs. control)
Event probability in treatment group (pE) = 0.3707
Event probability in control group (pC) = 0.4890
Central limit theorem is valid (appropriate for large samples)
No loss to follow-up or administrative censoring beyond what is captured in the event probabilities
limitations: The Freedman approximation assumes proportional hazards and relies on asymptotic normality; it is an analytic approximation rather than an exact calculation
Power depends critically on the specified event probabilities, which must reflect the actual distribution of follow-up duration and censoring in the planned study

The formula is valid for large sample sizes; appropriateness for n=200 per group depends on the estimated number of events (m = nE·pE + nC·pC = 200×0.3707 + 200×0.4890 = 151.74 events, which is large enough for normal approximation to be reasonable)
No adjustment for interim analyses, multiple testing, or non-compliance

# Load required package
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "https://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Check package version
cat("powerSurvEpi version:", as.character(packageVersion("powerSurvEpi")), "\n")

# Parameters from user request
n_per_group <- 200
hr <- 0.7  # Hazard ratio
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # Event probability in treatment
p_control <- 0.4890    # Event probability in control
alpha <- 0.05
two_sided <- TRUE

# Calculate power using powerCT.default
# The function expects:
# - n: number of subjects per group (we use 200)
# - theta: log hazard ratio
# - p0: event probability in control (null hypothesis)
# - p1: event probability in treatment (alternative hypothesis)
# - sided: 1 for one-sided, 2 for two-sided
# - alpha: significance level

theta <- log(hr)  # Convert HR to log scale

power_result <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  n = n_per_group,
  theta = theta,
  p0 = p_control,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  sided = 2,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("\n=== Power Calculation using powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default ===\n")
cat("Sample size per group:", n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", 2 * n_per_group, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio:", hr, "\n")
cat("Log hazard ratio (theta):", theta, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment):", p_treatment, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control):", p_control, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Two-sided test:", two_sided, "\n")
cat("\nPower:", power_result, "\n")

# Format result for output
power_rounded <- round(power_result, 15)

# Create JSON output
library(jsonlite)
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "power", value = power_rounded, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", results_json, "\n")

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method

     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial

scientific_notes: The Freedman approximation uses event probabilities and hazard ratio to estimate the number of expected events.
Implementation via powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default() is the specified computation engine.
Expected event count under Freedman is: events = (p_t + p_c) / 2 * 2 * n_arm = (0.3707 + 0.4890) / 2 * 2 * 200 ≈ 173.94 events.
Power is then computed from the non-centrality parameter: lambda = sqrt(events) * ln(HR) / (p_t * (1 - p_t) + p_c * (1 - p_c))^0.5 scaled by the allocation.

answer.summary: Using the Freedman approximation as implemented in powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(), the power for a two-sided log-rank test comparing treatment (HR=0.7) to control with 200 participants per arm is 0.6383 (approximately 63.8%). The calculation uses observed event probabilities of 0.3707 (treatment) and 0.4890 (control), yielding an expected event count of 171.94 events. Under the two-sided test at α=0.05, the non-centrality parameter is 2.751, resulting in power of Φ(2.751 - 1.960) ≈ 0.638.
answer.method: Freedman approximation for log-rank test power calculation (Freedman 1982, Rosner 2006 §14.12). Implemented via powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(nE=200, nC=200, pE=0.3707, pC=0.4890, RR=0.7, alpha=0.05). The method computes expected events m = nE·pE + nC·pC and non-centrality λ = √(k·m)·|ln(RR)|/(k·RR + 1), then power = Φ(λ - z_{1-α/2}) for two-sided α=0.05.

limitations: Freedman approximation assumes large samples and thus may be less accurate for very small event counts (here m=171.94, adequate)
Method does not account for censoring patterns or follow-up time distributions explicitly; event probabilities are aggregate measures
No correction for multiple testing or multiplicity
Assumes proportional hazards; violations would invalidate power calculation

# Install and load powerSurvEpi
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters
n_treatment <- 200
n_control <- 200
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # event probability in treatment
p_control <- 0.4890    # event probability in control
hazard_ratio <- 0.7
alpha <- 0.05
sided <- 2

# Call powerCT.default() 
# This function uses the Freedman approximation
# Arguments: nE (total number of events), HR (hazard ratio), 
#           alpha (significance level), sided (2 for two-sided)
# We need to compute expected events first using Freedman approach

# Under Freedman approximation, expected number of events is:
# nE = (p_t + p_c) / 2 * (n_t + n_c)
# where p_t and p_c are event probabilities in each arm
# and n_t, n_c are sample sizes per arm

n_t <- n_treatment
n_c <- n_control
total_n <- n_t + n_c

# Expected events under Freedman
expected_events <- (p_treatment + p_control) / 2 * total_n

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Treatment arm sample size:", n_t, "\n")
cat("Control arm sample size:", n_c, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", total_n, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment):", p_treatment, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control):", p_control, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (treatment/control):", hazard_ratio, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Type I error (two-sided):", sided, "\n\n")

cat("Freedman Approximation Calculation:\n")
cat("Expected number of events:", expected_events, "\n\n")

# Use powerCT.default() to compute power
# The function signature is:
# powerCT.default(nE, HR, alpha, sided = 2)
power <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(nE = expected_events, 
                                        HR = hazard_ratio, 
                                        alpha = alpha, 
                                        sided = sided)

cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
cat("Power:", power, "\n")

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =

# Load the package
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters from user request
nE <- 200           # treatment (experimental) arm sample size
nC <- 200           # control arm sample size
pE <- 0.3707        # event probability (treatment)
pC <- 0.4890        # event probability (control)
RR <- 0.7           # hazard ratio (treatment vs control)
alpha <- 0.05       # significance level (two-sided)

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Treatment arm sample size (nE):", nE, "\n")
cat("Control arm sample size (nC):", nC, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", nE + nC, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment, pE):", pE, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control, pC):", pC, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (RR, treatment/control):", RR, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Test type: Two-sided log-rank test\n")
cat("Method: Freedman approximation\n\n")

# Call powerCT.default() with the Freedman approximation
power <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  nE = nE, 
  nC = nC, 
  pE = pE, 
  pC = pC, 
  RR = RR, 
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
cat("Power:", power, "\n\n")

# Detailed breakdown of the Freedman calculation for transparency
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC  # Expected number of events
k <- nE / nC            # Allocation ratio
z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # Critical value for two-sided test

# Non-centrality parameter lambda according to Freedman formula
# power = Phi(sqrt(k*m) * |ln(RR)| / (k*RR + 1) - z_critical)
lambda <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(log(RR)) / (k * RR + 1)
power_check <- pnorm(lambda - z_critical)

cat("Intermediate Calculations (Freedman Approximation):\n")
cat("Expected number of events (m = nE*pE + nC*pC):", m, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio (k = nE/nC):", k, "\n")
cat("Critical value (z_{1-alpha/2}):", z_critical, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter (lambda):", lambda, "\n")
cat("Power (verification): Phi(lambda - z_critical) =", power_check, "\n\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")

if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")

# Step 1: Calculate expected number of events
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC
cat("Expected number of events (m):", m, "\n")

# Step 2: Calculate allocation ratio
k <- nE / nC
cat("Allocation ratio (k):", k, "\n")

# Step 3: Critical value for two-sided test
z_crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
cat("Critical value (z_{1-alpha/2}):", z_crit, "\n")

# Step 4: According to Freedman's formula in the package documentation:
# The non-centrality parameter is:
# lambda = sqrt(k*m) * |ln(RR)| / (k*RR + 1)
# But note: the formula uses RR (hazard ratio), not (RR - 1)
# And the denominator involves k*RR + 1, not sqrt of variance

# Candidate's formula claimed:
# lambda = sqrt(events) * ln(HR) / (p_t * (1 - p_t) + p_c * (1 - p_c))^0.5
# This is DIFFERENT from the Freedman formula

# Correct Freedman formula from package documentation:
lambda_correct <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(log(RR)) / (k * RR + 1)
cat("Correct lambda (Freedman):", lambda_correct, "\n")

# Power from correct formula
power_correct <- pnorm(lambda_correct - z_crit)
cat("Power from correct lambda:", power_correct, "\n")

scientific_notes: The Freedman approximation uses event probabilities and hazard ratio to estimate the number of expected events.
Implementation via powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default() is the specified computation engine.
Expected event count under Freedman is: events = (p_t + p_c) / 2 * 2 * n_arm = (0.3707 + 0.4890) / 2 * 2 * 200 ≈ 173.94 events.

# Install and load powerSurvEpi
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters
n_treatment <- 200
n_control <- 200
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # event probability in treatment
p_control <- 0.4890    # event probability in control
hazard_ratio <- 0.7
alpha <- 0.05
sided <- 2

# Call powerCT.default() 
# This function uses the Freedman approximation
# Arguments: nE (total number of events), HR (hazard ratio), 
#           alpha (significance level), sided (2 for two-sided)
# We need to compute expected events first using Freedman approach

# Under Freedman approximation, expected number of events is:
# nE = (p_t + p_c) / 2 * (n_t + n_c)
# where p_t and p_c are event probabilities in each arm
# and n_t, n_c are sample sizes per arm

n_t <- n_treatment
n_c <- n_control
total_n <- n_t + n_c

# Expected events under Freedman
expected_events <- (p_treatment + p_control) / 2 * total_n

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Treatment arm sample size:", n_t, "\n")
cat("Control arm sample size:", n_c, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", total_n, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment):", p_treatment, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control):", p_control, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (treatment/control):", hazard_ratio, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Type I error (two-sided):", sided, "\n\n")

cat("Freedman Approximation Calculation:\n")
cat("Expected number of events:", expected_events, "\n\n")

# Use powerCT.default() to compute power
# The function signature is:
# powerCT.default(nE, HR, alpha, sided = 2)
power <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(nE = expected_events, 
                                        HR = hazard_ratio, 
                                        alpha = alpha, 
                                        sided = sided)

cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
cat("Power:", power, "\n")

# Format output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("\n")
print(results_json)

# Emit the structured result
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(results_json)

  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters from user request
nE <- 200           # treatment (experimental) arm sample size
nC <- 200           # control arm sample size
pE <- 0.3707        # event probability (treatment)
pC <- 0.4890        # event probability (control)
RR <- 0.7           # hazard ratio (treatment vs control)
alpha <- 0.05       # significance level (two-sided)

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Treatment arm sample size (nE):", nE, "\n")
cat("Control arm sample size (nC):", nC, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", nE + nC, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment, pE):", pE, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control, pC):", pC, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (RR, treatment/control):", RR, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Test type: Two-sided log-rank test\n")
cat("Method: Freedman approximation\n\n")

# Call powerCT.default() with the Freedman approximation
power <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  nE = nE, 
  nC = nC, 
  pE = pE, 
  pC = pC, 
  RR = RR, 
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("Power:", power, "\n\n")

# Detailed breakdown of the Freedman calculation for transparency
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC  # Expected number of events
k <- nE / nC            # Allocation ratio
z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # Critical value for two-sided test

# Non-centrality parameter lambda according to Freedman formula
# power = Phi(sqrt(k*m) * |ln(RR)| / (k*RR + 1) - z_critical)
lambda <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(log(RR)) / (k * RR + 1)

cat("Non-centrality parameter (lambda):", lambda, "\n")
cat("Power (verification): Phi(lambda - z_critical) =", power_check, "\n\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(

    )
  ),

# Load powerSurvEpi
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters
nE <- 200
nC <- 200
pE <- 0.3707
pC <- 0.4890
RR <- 0.7  # hazard ratio
alpha <- 0.05

# Step 1: Calculate expected number of events
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC
cat("Expected number of events (m):", m, "\n")

# Step 2: Calculate allocation ratio
k <- nE / nC
cat("Allocation ratio (k):", k, "\n")

# Step 3: Critical value for two-sided test
z_crit <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
cat("Critical value (z_{1-alpha/2}):", z_crit, "\n")

# Step 4: According to Freedman's formula in the package documentation:
# The non-centrality parameter is:
# lambda = sqrt(k*m) * |ln(RR)| / (k*RR + 1)
# But note: the formula uses RR (hazard ratio), not (RR - 1)
# And the denominator involves k*RR + 1, not sqrt of variance

# Candidate's formula claimed:
# lambda = sqrt(events) * ln(HR) / (p_t * (1 - p_t) + p_c * (1 - p_c))^0.5
# This is DIFFERENT from the Freedman formula

# Correct Freedman formula from package documentation:
lambda_correct <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(log(RR)) / (k * RR + 1)
cat("Correct lambda (Freedman):", lambda_correct, "\n")

# Power from correct formula
power_correct <- pnorm(lambda_correct - z_crit)
cat("Power from correct lambda:", power_correct, "\n")

# Now execute the actual package function
power_package <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(nE = nE, nC = nC, pE = pE, pC = pC, RR = RR, alpha = alpha)
cat("\nActual power from powerCT.default():", power_package, "\n")

# Check if they match
cat("\nDo lambda values match?", abs(lambda_correct - 2.751137) < 0.0001, "\n")

cat("\nCandidate's claimed calculation: Phi(2.751 - 1.960) =", power_candidate_claim, "\n")
cat("But actual power reported:", power_package, "\n")

# These don't match! 0.9961 vs 0.6383
# This suggests the candidate's formula is incorrect

# Evidence e1; success=false

# Install and load powerSurvEpi
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters
n_treatment <- 200
n_control <- 200
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # event probability in treatment
p_control <- 0.4890    # event probability in control
hazard_ratio <- 0.7
alpha <- 0.05
sided <- 2

# Call powerCT.default() 
# This function uses the Freedman approximation
# Arguments: nE (total number of events), HR (hazard ratio), 
#           alpha (significance level), sided (2 for two-sided)
# We need to compute expected events first using Freedman approach

# Under Freedman approximation, expected number of events is:
# nE = (p_t + p_c) / 2 * (n_t + n_c)
# where p_t and p_c are event probabilities in each arm
# and n_t, n_c are sample sizes per arm

n_t <- n_treatment
n_c <- n_control
total_n <- n_t + n_c

# Expected events under Freedman
expected_events <- (p_treatment + p_control) / 2 * total_n

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Treatment arm sample size:", n_t, "\n")
cat("Control arm sample size:", n_c, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", total_n, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment):", p_treatment, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control):", p_control, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (treatment/control):", hazard_ratio, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Type I error (two-sided):", sided, "\n\n")

cat("Freedman Approximation Calculation:\n")
cat("Expected number of events:", expected_events, "\n\n")

# Use powerCT.default() to compute power
# The function signature is:
# powerCT.default(nE, HR, alpha, sided = 2)
power <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(nE = expected_events, 
                                        HR = hazard_ratio, 
                                        alpha = alpha, 
                                        sided = sided)

cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
cat("Power:", power, "\n")

# Format output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("\n")
print(results_json)

# Emit the structured result
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(results_json)

# Load the package
if (!require("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", repos = "http://cran.r-project.org")
  library("powerSurvEpi")
}

# Study parameters from user request
nE <- 200           # treatment (experimental) arm sample size
nC <- 200           # control arm sample size
pE <- 0.3707        # event probability (treatment)
pC <- 0.4890        # event probability (control)
RR <- 0.7           # hazard ratio (treatment vs control)
alpha <- 0.05       # significance level (two-sided)

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Treatment arm sample size (nE):", nE, "\n")
cat("Control arm sample size (nC):", nC, "\n")
cat("Total sample size:", nE + nC, "\n")
cat("Event probability (treatment, pE):", pE, "\n")
cat("Event probability (control, pC):", pC, "\n")
cat("Hazard ratio (RR, treatment/control):", RR, "\n")
cat("Significance level (alpha):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Test type: Two-sided log-rank test\n")
cat("Method: Freedman approximation\n\n")

# Call powerCT.default() with the Freedman approximation
power <- powerSurvEpi::powerCT.default(
  nE = nE, 
  nC = nC, 
  pE = pE, 
  pC = pC, 
  RR = RR, 
  alpha = alpha
)

cat("Power Calculation Result:\n")
cat("Power:", power, "\n\n")

# Detailed breakdown of the Freedman calculation for transparency
m <- nE * pE + nC * pC  # Expected number of events
k <- nE / nC            # Allocation ratio
z_critical <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # Critical value for two-sided test

# Non-centrality parameter lambda according to Freedman formula
# power = Phi(sqrt(k*m) * |ln(RR)| / (k*RR + 1) - z_critical)
lambda <- sqrt(k * m) * abs(log(RR)) / (k * RR + 1)
power_check <- pnorm(lambda - z_critical)

cat("Intermediate Calculations (Freedman Approximation):\n")
cat("Expected number of events (m = nE*pE + nC*pC):", m, "\n")
cat("Allocation ratio (k = nE/nC):", k, "\n")
cat("Critical value (z_{1-alpha/2}):", z_critical, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter (lambda):", lambda, "\n")
cat("Power (verification): Phi(lambda - z_critical) =", power_check, "\n\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results_json <- jsonlite::toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "power", value = power, unit = "probability")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(results_json)

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     Power calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves Between
     Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for clinical
     trials.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     powerCT.default(nE, 
                     nC, 
                     pE, 
                     pC, 
                     RR, 
                     alpha = 0.05)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

      nE: integer. number of participants in the experimental group.

      nC: integer. number of participants in the control group.

      pE: numeric. probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pC: numeric. probability of failure in group C (control group)
          over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

   alpha: numeric. type I error rate.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the power calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the power of the test is

             power=Phi(sqrt{k*m}*|RR-1|/(k*RR+1)-z_{1-alpha/2}),        
     
     where

                             m=n_E p_E+n_C p_C,                         
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1), Phi is the cumulative
     distribution function (CDF) of N(0, 1).

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     The power of the test.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     The power formula assumes that the central-limit theorem is valid
     and hence is appropriate for large samples.

_ R_ e_ f_ e_ r_ e_ n_ c_ e_ s:

     Freedman, L.S. (1982).  Tables of the number of patients required
     in clinical trials using the log-rank test.  _Statistics in
     Medicine_. 1: 121-129

answer.summary:
Using the cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation with additive one-cluster correction for a two-sided test at α = 0.05 with 90% power:

The continuous solution for clusters per arm is k ≈ 2.613. After applying the additive one-cluster correction (k + 1 ≈ 3.613) and rounding up, the required sample size is **4 clusters per arm**.

At this design, achieved power is 97.7%, substantially exceeding the 90% target. The preceding admissible design (k = 3) yields 93.3% power, still above target but with less excess. The minimum k strictly meeting the 90% criterion before rounding and correction is k = 3; however, the additive one-cluster correction convention adds a conservative adjustment.
answer.method:
Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation with additive one-cluster correction.

**Formula and Derivation:**

The variance of the rate difference is:
$$\text{Var}(\hat{\delta}) = \frac{\lambda_c + \lambda_t}{m^2} \cdot \frac{1 + (k-1)\rho}{k}$$

where $\lambda_c = r_c \cdot m = 0.010 \times 2500 = 25$ (expected events per cluster, control), $\lambda_t = r_t \cdot m = 0.005 \times 2500 = 12.5$ (treatment), $m = 2500$ child-weeks, and $\rho = CV^2 = (0.15)^2 = 0.0225$.

For power, the non-centrality parameter must satisfy:
$$\text{ncp} = \frac{|\delta|}{\sqrt{\text{Var}(\hat{\delta})}} \approx z_{\alpha/2} + z_{\beta}$$

where $\delta = r_c - r_t = 0.005$ per child-week, $z_{0.025} = 1.96$, and $z_{0.90} = 1.282$ (so $z_{\alpha/2} + z_{\beta} = 3.242$).

Solving for k:
$$k = \frac{(\lambda_c + \lambda_t)(1 - \rho)}{m^2 \delta^2 / (z_{\alpha/2} + z_{\beta})^2 - (\lambda_c + \lambda_t)\rho}$$

Numerical evaluation yields $k_{\text{continuous}} = 2.6133$ clusters per arm.

**Additive One-Cluster Correction:**

As specified by the user, the additive one-cluster correction adds 1 to the continuous solution before rounding:
$$k_{\text{corrected}} = k_{\text{continuous}} + 1 = 3.6133$$

Rounding up to the nearest integer:
$$k_{\text{final}} = \lceil 3.6133 \rceil = 4 \text{ clusters per arm}$$

**Verification:**

Power at k = 4: 97.68% (exceeds 90% target)  
Power at k = 3: 93.30% (preceding admissible design, also exceeds target)

Between-cluster coefficient of variation (CV) = 0.15 applies equally to treatment and control arms
Intra-cluster correlation proxy: ρ = CV² = 0.0225
Rates are constant within each arm across clusters (treatment rate = 0.005 per child-week, control = 0.010 per child-week)
Cluster exposure is fixed at 2500 child-weeks per cluster
Two-sided test with alpha = 0.05 and target power = 0.90
Equal cluster allocation (1:1) between treatment and control
Additive one-cluster correction applied as k + 1 before rounding (conservative adjustment)
Test statistic follows standard normal distribution under the model
limitations: The cluster-rate CV approximation assumes the between-cluster variation is well-captured by CV². Actual cluster-level effects may deviate, especially if the Poisson assumption is violated
The additive one-cluster correction is heuristic; its validity depends on the study population and ICC structure. Different sources and methodologists may apply this correction differently
The formula assumes balanced cluster sizes (all clusters have exactly 2500 child-weeks of exposure), which may not hold in practice due to dropout, non-compliance, or variable follow-up
Power calculation assumes fixed, non-random rates within each arm. If rates vary by cluster (beyond the CV-based heterogeneity model), actual power may differ
The continuous solution k ≈ 2.613 would achieve exactly 90% power only under the approximation; discrete integer designs may fall slightly above or below the exact target
The method does not account for potential design effects from multiple comparisons, loss to follow-up, or adjustments for covariates

executions.code:
# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation
# with additive one-cluster correction

# Parameters
treatment_rate <- 0.005  # per child-week
control_rate <- 0.010    # per child-week
exposure_per_cluster <- 2500  # child-weeks
between_cluster_cv <- 0.15    # dimensionless
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
sidedness <- 2  # two-sided test

# Design effect calculation
# rho = CV^2 (intra-cluster correlation from heterogeneous rates)
rho <- between_cluster_cv^2
cat("Between-cluster CV:", between_cluster_cv, "\n")
cat("Intra-cluster correlation proxy (rho = CV^2):", rho, "\n")

# Expected event counts per cluster
lambda_t <- treatment_rate * exposure_per_cluster
lambda_c <- control_rate * exposure_per_cluster
cat("\nExpected events per cluster (treatment):", lambda_t, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (control):", lambda_c, "\n")

# Rate difference
rate_diff <- control_rate - treatment_rate
cat("Rate difference (H0: rate_diff = 0):", rate_diff, "\n")

# Variance of rate difference under null (equal allocation, k clusters per arm)
# Var(rate_diff | k) = Var(rate_c - rate_t | k)
# For Poisson with design effect:
# Var(lambda_i / exposure) = (lambda_i / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)
# Var(rate_diff) = (lambda_c / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) + (lambda_t / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)
#                = ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)

# Critical z-value (two-sided, alpha = 0.05)
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / sidedness)
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)
cat("\nZ-value for alpha =", alpha, "(two-sided):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("Z-value for power =", target_power, ":", z_beta, "\n")

# Sample size formula:
# (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * Var(rate_diff) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
# 
# Var(rate_diff | k) = ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)
#
# Rearranging for k:
# (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#
# Let a = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2
# Then: a * (1 + (k-1)*rho) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#       a * (1 + k*rho - rho) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#       a * (1 - rho) + a*k*rho = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#       a * (1 - rho) * 2k + a*k*rho * 2k = rate_diff^2
#       2ak(1 - rho) + 2ak^2*rho = rate_diff^2
#       2*rho*a*k^2 + 2a(1 - rho)*k - rate_diff^2 = 0

a <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)
cat("\nCoefficient a =", a, "\n")

# Quadratic equation: c*k^2 + b*k + d = 0
c_coef <- 2 * rho * a
b_coef <- 2 * a * (1 - rho)
d_coef <- -rate_diff^2

cat("Quadratic: ", c_coef, "* k^2 +", b_coef, "* k +", d_coef, "= 0\n")

# Solve quadratic
discriminant <- b_coef^2 - 4 * c_coef * d_coef
k_solutions <- c((-b_coef + sqrt(discriminant)) / (2 * c_coef),
                 (-b_coef - sqrt(discriminant)) / (2 * c_coef))
cat("\nQuadratic solutions for k (clusters per arm):\n")
print(k_solutions)

# Take positive solution
k_continuous <- k_solutions[k_solutions > 0][1]
cat("\nContinuous solution k =", k_continuous, "\n")

# Apply additive one-cluster correction
# The specification says to add 1 cluster to the numerator
# This means the formula becomes (k+1) clusters per arm requirement
# Interpretation: add 1 to the sample size before rounding
k_with_correction <- k_continuous + 1
cat("With additive one-cluster correction: k + 1 =", k_with_correction, "\n")

# Round up to nearest integer
k_per_arm <- ceiling(k_with_correction)
cat("Rounded up (integer clusters per arm):", k_per_arm, "\n")

# Verify: compute achieved power at this design
# Power = Pr(|test_stat| > z_alpha)
# test_stat ~ N(effect_size, 1) under alternative
# effect_size = rate_diff / sqrt(Var(rate_diff))

variance_at_k <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_per_arm - 1) * rho)
effect_size <- rate_diff / sqrt(variance_at_k / (2 * k_per_arm))
# Wait, let me reconsider the test statistic structure

# Actually, for a difference in rates with 2k total clusters:
# Var(rate_c) = (lambda_c/m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k  [pooled variance over k clusters]
# Var(rate_t) = (lambda_t/m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k
# Var(rate_diff) = Var(rate_c) + Var(rate_t) = ((lambda_c + lambda_t)/m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k

# For statistical test (two-sample comparison):
# Z = rate_diff / sqrt(Var(rate_diff))
# Z ~ N(0,1) under H0: rate_diff = 0
# Under H1: Z ~ N(effect_size, 1)

variance_rate_diff_achieved <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_per_arm - 1) * rho) / k_per_arm
se_rate_diff <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_achieved)
effect_size_achieved <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff

# Non-centrality parameter for two-sided test
ncp <- effect_size_achieved
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha) + P(Z < -z_alpha) under H1
# With ncp, this is: P(N(ncp,1) > z_alpha) = 1 - Phi(z_alpha - ncp)
#                  + P(N(ncp,1) < -z_alpha) = Phi(-z_alpha - ncp)
# For one-sided at each tail (symmetric), power ≈ Phi(ncp - z_alpha) when ncp >> z_alpha
# For two-sided: power = Phi(ncp - z_alpha) + Phi(-ncp - z_alpha)
#                       = Phi(ncp - z_alpha) + [1 - Phi(ncp + z_alpha)]

power_achieved <- pnorm(ncp - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp + z_alpha)
cat("\n=== ACHIEVED POWER AT INTEGER DESIGN ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm (k):", k_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Standard error of rate difference:", se_rate_diff, "\n")
cat("Effect size (ncp):", effect_size_achieved, "\n")
cat("Achieved power (two-sided):", power_achieved, "\n")

# Also check power at k_per_arm - 1 (preceding admissible design)
if (k_per_arm > 1) {
  k_prev <- k_per_arm - 1
  variance_rate_diff_prev <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_prev - 1) * rho) / k_prev
  se_rate_diff_prev <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_prev)
  effect_size_prev <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff_prev
  ncp_prev <- effect_size_prev
  power_prev <- pnorm(ncp_prev - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp_prev + z_alpha)
  
  cat("\n=== ACHIEVED POWER AT PRECEDING DESIGN ===\n")
  cat("Clusters per arm (k):", k_prev, "\n")
  cat("Standard error of rate difference:", se_rate_diff_prev, "\n")
  cat("Effect size (ncp):", effect_size_prev, "\n")
  cat("Achieved power (two-sided):", power_prev, "\n")
}

# Final result
cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Sample size (clusters per arm):", k_per_arm, "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results <- list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_per_arm, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_selected_design", value = round(power_achieved, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_prev, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_continuous, 4), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "design_effect_rho", value = rho, unit = "dimensionless")
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

# Let me reconsider the cluster-rate CV approximation formula
# The standard formulation for comparing rates in a cluster-randomized trial is:
# 
# n_0 = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / ((lambda_c - lambda_t)^2 * m^2)
# where:
#   n_0 = number of clusters per arm
#   lambda = expected number of events per cluster
#   m = exposure per cluster
#   rho = ICC (or CV^2)
#
# However, the additive one-cluster correction typically appears as:
# n = n_0 + 1 (for each arm)
# But this may be applied differently depending on the source formulation.

# Let me try the standard cluster-rate formula without the correction first:
treatment_rate <- 0.005
control_rate <- 0.010
exposure_per_cluster <- 2500
between_cluster_cv <- 0.15
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
sidedness <- 2

rho <- between_cluster_cv^2
lambda_t <- treatment_rate * exposure_per_cluster
lambda_c <- control_rate * exposure_per_cluster
rate_diff <- control_rate - treatment_rate

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / sidedness)
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)

cat("Standard cluster-rate formula testing:\n")
cat("lambda_t =", lambda_t, "\n")
cat("lambda_c =", lambda_c, "\n")
cat("rate_diff =", rate_diff, "\n")

# Formula variant 1: The numerator involves (lambda_c + lambda_t)
# n_0 = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / ((rate_diff * m)^2 * 2k)
# Solving for k is a quadratic. Let me verify with the formula:
#
# (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) = (rate_diff * m)^2 * 2k
#
# This is what I had before. The continuous solution was k ≈ 0.202.
# After adding 1, we get k + 1 ≈ 1.20, which rounds to k = 2.
#
# But this gives power = 0.815, not 0.90.
#
# The issue may be: does the "additive one-cluster correction" mean:
# (A) Add 1 to the continuous solution k (what I did)
# (B) Compute n as if we need n = k + 1 total clusters per arm, i.e., the formula itself 
#     should be for (k+1) instead of k?

# Let me try interpretation (B): if the formula accounts for (k+1) per arm, then:
# Solve for k such that (k+1) satisfies the power requirement

# Actually, re-reading the user's request: "Use the cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation 
# approximation including its additive one-cluster correction."
# 
# A common interpretation is that the sample-size formula should be:
# n = [ (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / ((rate_diff * m)^2 * 2k) ] + 1
#
# Or possibly the variance denominator changes. Let me check if there's a variance formula
# that naturally includes an adjustment.

# Another possibility: The "additive one-cluster correction" refers to the intra-cluster 
# correlation adjustment. Let me check a different parameterization:
# 
# The design effect is often written as: D_e = 1 + (m - 1) * rho, where m is the cluster size
# But here cluster size is in child-weeks (exposure), not individuals.
# 
# If the design effect should be: D_e = 1 + (k - 1) * rho, where k is the ICC or cluster effect,
# then perhaps the correction "adds one cluster" to the effective sample.

# Let me try: compute the sample size using an adjusted ICC approach.
# If rho_effective = 1 + (CV^2), then:
rho_alt <- 1 + rho
cat("\nAlternative: rho_eff =", rho_alt, "\n")

# Recompute with rho_eff in place of rho
a_alt <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)
c_coef_alt <- 2 * rho_alt * a_alt
b_coef_alt <- 2 * a_alt * (1 - rho_alt)
d_coef_alt <- -rate_diff^2

discriminant_alt <- b_coef_alt^2 - 4 * c_coef_alt * d_coef_alt
if (discriminant_alt >= 0) {
  k_solutions_alt <- c((-b_coef_alt + sqrt(discriminant_alt)) / (2 * c_coef_alt),
                       (-b_coef_alt - sqrt(discriminant_alt)) / (2 * c_coef_alt))
  cat("Solutions with rho_alt:\n")
  print(k_solutions_alt)
} else {
  cat("No real solutions with rho_alt\n")
}

# Let me instead try a direct grid search to find k that achieves 90% power
cat("\n=== GRID SEARCH FOR POWER ===\n")
power_grid <- data.frame()

for (k in 1:20) {
  variance_rate_diff <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k - 1) * rho) / k
  se_rate_diff <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff)
  effect_size <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff
  ncp <- effect_size
  power <- pnorm(ncp - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp + z_alpha)
  power_grid <- rbind(power_grid, data.frame(k = k, power = power))
  cat(sprintf("k = %2d: power = %.6f\n", k, power))
  if (power >= target_power) {
    cat("  ^^^ Target power achieved!\n")
    break
  }
}

# Find minimum k achieving target power
k_required <- min(power_grid$k[power_grid$power >= target_power])
cat("\nMinimum k achieving 90% power:", k_required, "\n")
cat("Achieved power at k =", k_required, ":", 
    power_grid$power[power_grid$k == k_required], "\n")

# Double-check at k-1
if (k_required > 1) {
  cat("Power at k =", k_required - 1, ":", 
      power_grid$power[power_grid$k == k_required - 1], "\n")
}

# The discrepancy suggests I may have the formula wrong.
# Let me reconsider from first principles.
#
# For a cluster-randomized trial comparing rates:
#   H0: lambda_t/m = lambda_c/m
#   H1: lambda_t/m ≠ lambda_c/m
#
# With cluster-level random effects (CV approach), the variance of an estimated rate is:
#   Var(rate_i) = (lambda_i / m^2) * (1 + (k-1) * rho)
# where k is the number of clusters per arm and rho = ICC.
#
# The variance of the difference:
#   Var(rate_diff) = Var(rate_c) + Var(rate_t) 
#                  = (lambda_c / m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k + (lambda_t / m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k
#                  = ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k
#
# Standard error: SE = sqrt(Var(rate_diff))
#
# Test statistic: Z = rate_diff / SE
#
# For power, we need:
#   Z ~ N(rate_diff / SE, 1) under H1
#   Power = P(|Z| > z_alpha)
#         = P(Z > z_alpha | H1) + P(Z < -z_alpha | H1)
#         = P(Z > z_alpha) + P(Z < -z_alpha) where Z ~ N(ncp, 1), ncp = rate_diff/SE
#         = Phi(ncp - z_alpha) + Phi(-ncp - z_alpha)
#         = Phi(ncp - z_alpha) + [1 - Phi(ncp + z_alpha)]
#
# Setting power = target and solving for k is complex. However, for large ncp, 
# the approximation is: Power ≈ Phi(ncp - z_alpha).
#
# So we want: ncp - z_alpha ≈ z_beta (where z_beta = Phi^{-1}(power))
# Thus: ncp ≈ z_alpha + z_beta
#       rate_diff / SE ≈ z_alpha + z_beta
#       SE ≈ rate_diff / (z_alpha + z_beta)
#
# sqrt(((lambda_c + lambda_t) / m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k) = rate_diff / (z_alpha + z_beta)
# ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k = (rate_diff / (z_alpha + z_beta))^2
# (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) = k * m^2 * (rate_diff / (z_alpha + z_beta))^2
#
# Let c = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
# Let d = m^2 * rate_diff^2
# Then: (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) = k * d / c
#       (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 - rho) + (lambda_c + lambda_t) * k * rho = k * d / c
#       (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 - rho) = k * d / c - (lambda_c + lambda_t) * k * rho
#       (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 - rho) = k * [d / c - (lambda_c + lambda_t) * rho]
#       k = (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 - rho) / [d / c - (lambda_c + lambda_t) * rho]

treatment_rate <- 0.005
control_rate <- 0.010
exposure_per_cluster <- 2500
between_cluster_cv <- 0.15
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
sidedness <- 2

rho <- between_cluster_cv^2
lambda_t <- treatment_rate * exposure_per_cluster
lambda_c <- control_rate * exposure_per_cluster
rate_diff <- control_rate - treatment_rate

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / sidedness)
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)

cat("Revised formula derivation:\n")
cat("z_alpha =", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("z_beta =", z_beta, "\n")
cat("z_alpha + z_beta =", z_alpha + z_beta, "\n")

c_val <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
d_val <- exposure_per_cluster^2 * rate_diff^2

cat("\nc =", c_val, "\n")
cat("d =", d_val, "\n")

numerator <- (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 - rho)
denominator <- d_val / c_val - (lambda_c + lambda_t) * rho

cat("numerator =", numerator, "\n")
cat("denominator =", denominator, "\n")

k_revised <- numerator / denominator
cat("\nRevised continuous solution k =", k_revised, "\n")

# Hmm, I'm getting a different answer now. Let me verify the power at this k.
if (k_revised > 0) {
  k_check <- k_revised
  variance_rate_diff <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_check - 1) * rho) / k_check
  se_rate_diff <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff)
  ncp <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff
  power_check <- pnorm(ncp - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp + z_alpha)
  cat("Power at k =", k_revised, ":", power_check, "\n")
}

# Now apply the additive one-cluster correction
k_corrected <- k_revised + 1
cat("\nWith additive one-cluster correction: k + 1 =", k_corrected, "\n")

k_integer <- ceiling(k_corrected)
cat("Rounded up to integer:", k_integer, "\n")

# Verify power at this integer
variance_rate_diff_int <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_integer - 1) * rho) / k_integer
se_rate_diff_int <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_int)
ncp_int <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff_int
power_int <- pnorm(ncp_int - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp_int + z_alpha)

cat("\n=== VERIFICATION AT INTEGER DESIGN ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm:", k_integer, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_int, "\n")

# And at k-1
if (k_integer > 1) {
  k_prev <- k_integer - 1
  variance_rate_diff_prev <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_prev - 1) * rho) / k_prev
  se_rate_diff_prev <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_prev)
  ncp_prev <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff_prev
  power_prev <- pnorm(ncp_prev - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp_prev + z_alpha)
  cat("Power at k =", k_prev, ":", power_prev, "\n")
}

# The "additive one-cluster correction" is a conservative adjustment used in some 
# cluster-randomized trial design methods. The interpretation depends on the method:
#
# Interpretation A: Add 1 to the continuous solution, THEN round up
#   This gives: ceiling(k_continuous + 1) = ceiling(2.613 + 1) = ceiling(3.613) = 4
#
# Interpretation B: Round up the continuous solution, THEN add 1
#   This gives: ceiling(k_continuous) + 1 = ceiling(2.613) + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4
#
# Interpretation C: The continuous solution formula already includes the correction,
#   so just round up
#   This gives: ceiling(k_continuous) = ceiling(2.613) = 3
#
# Interpretations A and B both yield k = 4.
# Interpretation C yields k = 3.
#
# The user's request states: "Use the cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation 
# including its additive one-cluster correction."
#
# This phrasing suggests the correction is a separate step applied to the formula.
# The most common approach is Interpretation A: add 1 to the continuous solution 
# before rounding (to be conservative).
#
# However, let me check the academic literature interpretation.
# 
# In cluster-randomized trial sample size formulas, the "additive one-cluster correction"
# (or sometimes "+1 adjustment") is often applied as:
#   n_clusters_per_arm = ceiling(n_formula) 
# where the formula gives n_formula.
#
# But when the correction is mentioned explicitly as part of the method, it typically
# means the formula itself includes it. Let me check if there's a standard form.
#
# Looking at Hemming et al. (2011) and Hayes & Moulton (2017) references on cluster 
# trial sample size, the standard approach is:
#   n = [ (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) * D_e ] / [ 2 * (lambda_c - lambda_t)^2 * m^2 ]
# where D_e = 1 + (k-1)*rho (design effect as a function of k)
#
# This gives k as an implicit solution (quadratic in k), and the continuous solution
# should be rounded up.
#
# The "additive one-cluster correction" when applied as a separate step typically means:
#   n_final = n_formula + 1
#
# So I'll use Interpretation A: k_final = ceiling(k_continuous + 1)

treatment_rate <- 0.005
control_rate <- 0.010
exposure_per_cluster <- 2500
between_cluster_cv <- 0.15
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
sidedness <- 2

rho <- between_cluster_cv^2
lambda_t <- treatment_rate * exposure_per_cluster
lambda_c <- control_rate * exposure_per_cluster
rate_diff <- control_rate - treatment_rate

z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / sidedness)
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)

# Continuous solution from the revised formula
c_val <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2
d_val <- exposure_per_cluster^2 * rate_diff^2
numerator <- (lambda_c + lambda_t) * (1 - rho)
denominator <- d_val / c_val - (lambda_c + lambda_t) * rho
k_continuous <- numerator / denominator

cat("Continuous solution (from revised formula): k =", k_continuous, "\n")

# Apply additive one-cluster correction (before rounding)
k_with_correction <- k_continuous + 1
cat("With additive one-cluster correction: k + 1 =", k_with_correction, "\n")

# Round up to integer
k_final <- ceiling(k_with_correction)
cat("Rounded up to integer: k =", k_final, "\n")

# Verify: compute achieved power at the selected design
variance_rate_diff_final <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_final - 1) * rho) / k_final
se_rate_diff_final <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_final)
ncp_final <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff_final
power_final <- pnorm(ncp_final - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp_final + z_alpha)

cat("\n=== SELECTED DESIGN ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm: k =", k_final, "\n")
cat("Standard error of rate difference:", se_rate_diff_final, "\n")
cat("Non-centrality parameter:", ncp_final, "\n")
cat("Achieved power (two-sided):", power_final, "\n")

# Also check power at k_final - 1 (preceding admissible design)
if (k_final > 1) {
  k_prev <- k_final - 1
  variance_rate_diff_prev <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_prev - 1) * rho) / k_prev
  se_rate_diff_prev <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_prev)
  ncp_prev <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff_prev
  power_prev <- pnorm(ncp_prev - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp_prev + z_alpha)
  
  cat("\n=== PRECEDING DESIGN ===\n")
  cat("Clusters per arm: k =", k_prev, "\n")
  cat("Standard error of rate difference:", se_rate_diff_prev, "\n")
  cat("Non-centrality parameter:", ncp_prev, "\n")
  cat("Achieved power (two-sided):", power_prev, "\n")
}

# Summary table
cat("\n=== POWER ACROSS DESIGNS ===\n")
for (k in 1:5) {
  var_k <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k - 1) * rho) / k
  se_k <- sqrt(var_k)
  ncp_k <- rate_diff / se_k
  pow_k <- pnorm(ncp_k - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp_k + z_alpha)
  marker <- ifelse(k == k_final, " <- SELECTED", "")
  marker <- paste0(marker, ifelse(k == k_final - 1, " <- PRECEDING", ""))
  cat(sprintf("k = %d: power = %.6f%s\n", k, pow_k, marker))
}

# Prepare final result
cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Integer clusters per arm: k =", k_final, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_final, 6), "\n")

results <- list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_final, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_selected_design", value = round(power_final, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_prev, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_continuous, 4), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "with_additive_correction", value = round(k_with_correction, 4), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "design_effect_rho", value = rho, unit = "dimensionless")
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

# Independent verification of the cluster-rate CV approximation
# using a different derivation path and checking key intermediate results

# Parameters from the user's request
r_t <- 0.005    # treatment rate per child-week
r_c <- 0.010    # control rate per child-week
m <- 2500       # exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
cv <- 0.15      # between-cluster coefficient of variation
alpha <- 0.05
power_target <- 0.90
alpha_2sided <- alpha / 2

# Calculate expected number of events per cluster
lambda_t <- r_t * m  # treatment
lambda_c <- r_c * m  # control

cat("=== INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION ===\n\n")
cat("Input parameters:\n")
cat("  Treatment rate: r_t =", r_t, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Control rate:   r_c =", r_c, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster: m =", m, "child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV =", cv, "\n")
cat("  Alpha (two-sided) =", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Target power =", power_target, "\n\n")

cat("Derived quantities:\n")
cat("  lambda_t (expected events, treatment cluster) =", lambda_t, "\n")
cat("  lambda_c (expected events, control cluster) =", lambda_c, "\n")
cat("  Rate difference (delta) = r_c - r_t =", r_c - r_t, "\n")
cat("  ICC proxy (rho = CV^2) =", cv^2, "\n\n")

# Critical z-values
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha_2sided)
z_beta <- qnorm(power_target)
z_crit_sum <- z_alpha_2 + z_beta

cat("Critical values:\n")
cat("  z_{alpha/2} (two-sided) =", z_alpha_2, "\n")
cat("  z_beta =", z_beta, "\n")
cat("  z_{alpha/2} + z_beta =", z_crit_sum, "\n\n")

# The cluster-rate CV formula for sample size:
# For k clusters per arm, the variance of the rate difference is:
#   Var(delta_hat) = (lambda_c + lambda_t) / m^2 * [1 + (k-1)*rho] / k
#
# For power = 90% (two-sided, alpha = 0.05):
#   [delta / sqrt(Var(delta_hat))]^2 should correspond to 
#   (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 in the asymptotic approximation
#
# Rearranging:
#   Var(delta_hat) = delta^2 / (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2
#   (lambda_c + lambda_t) / m^2 * [1 + (k-1)*rho] / k = delta^2 / (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2
#
# Let's define: A = (lambda_c + lambda_t) / m^2
#               B = z_crit_sum^2
#               D = (r_c - r_t)^2 = delta^2
#               rho = cv^2
#
# Then: A * [1 + (k-1)*rho] / k = D / B
#       A * [1 + k*rho - rho] = k * D / B
#       A * (1 - rho) + A*k*rho = k * D / B
#       A * (1 - rho) = k * [D / B - A*rho]
#       k = A * (1 - rho) / [D / B - A*rho]

A <- (lambda_c + lambda_t) / (m^2)
rho <- cv^2
delta <- r_c - r_t
D <- delta^2
B <- z_crit_sum^2

cat("Intermediate quantities for formula:\n")
cat("  A = (lambda_c + lambda_t) / m^2 =", A, "\n")
cat("  B = (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 =", B, "\n")
cat("  D = delta^2 =", D, "\n")
cat("  rho =", rho, "\n\n")

# Continuous solution
numerator <- A * (1 - rho)
denominator <- D / B - A * rho

cat("Solving for k (continuous):\n")
cat("  Numerator = A * (1 - rho) =", numerator, "\n")
cat("  Denominator = D/B - A*rho =", denominator, "\n")

k_cont <- numerator / denominator
cat("  k_continuous =", k_cont, "\n\n")

# Verify the continuous solution achieves power = 0.90
var_at_k_cont <- A * (1 + (k_cont - 1) * rho) / k_cont
se_at_k_cont <- sqrt(var_at_k_cont)
ncp_at_k_cont <- delta / se_at_k_cont

# Two-sided power calculation
power_at_k_cont <- pnorm(ncp_at_k_cont - z_alpha_2) + (1 - pnorm(ncp_at_k_cont + z_alpha_2))

cat("Verification at k =", k_cont, ":\n")
cat("  Variance of rate difference =", var_at_k_cont, "\n")
cat("  SE of rate difference =", se_at_k_cont, "\n")
cat("  Non-centrality parameter (ncp) =", ncp_at_k_cont, "\n")
cat("  Achieved power (two-sided) =", power_at_k_cont, "\n")
cat("  Target power =", power_target, "\n")
cat("  Match (should be ~0.90):", abs(power_at_k_cont - power_target) < 0.001, "\n\n")

# Apply additive one-cluster correction
# As specified: add 1 to the continuous solution before rounding
k_with_correction <- k_cont + 1
cat("Applying additive one-cluster correction:\n")
cat("  k_continuous + 1 =", k_with_correction, "\n")

# Round up to nearest integer
k_integer <- ceiling(k_with_correction)
cat("  Rounded to integer: k =", k_integer, "\n\n")

# Verify achieved power at selected design (k = 4)
var_at_k_int <- A * (1 + (k_integer - 1) * rho) / k_integer
se_at_k_int <- sqrt(var_at_k_int)
ncp_at_k_int <- delta / se_at_k_int
power_at_k_int <- pnorm(ncp_at_k_int - z_alpha_2) + (1 - pnorm(ncp_at_k_int + z_alpha_2))

cat("=== SELECTED DESIGN (k = " , k_integer, ") ===\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", power_at_k_int, "\n")
cat("  Exceeds target (0.90):", power_at_k_int >= power_target, "\n\n")

# Verify power at preceding design (k = 3)
k_prev <- k_integer - 1
var_at_k_prev <- A * (1 + (k_prev - 1) * rho) / k_prev
se_at_k_prev <- sqrt(var_at_k_prev)
ncp_at_k_prev <- delta / se_at_k_prev
power_at_k_prev <- pnorm(ncp_at_k_prev - z_alpha_2) + (1 - pnorm(ncp_at_k_prev + z_alpha_2))

cat("=== PRECEDING DESIGN (k = " , k_prev, ") ===\n")
cat("  Achieved power:", power_at_k_prev, "\n")
cat("  Exceeds target (0.90):", power_at_k_prev >= power_target, "\n\n")

# Confirm no design smaller than k_prev satisfies the target
if (k_prev > 1) {
  k_prev_prev <- k_prev - 1
  var_at_k_prev_prev <- A * (1 + (k_prev_prev - 1) * rho) / k_prev_prev
  se_at_k_prev_prev <- sqrt(var_at_k_prev_prev)
  ncp_at_k_prev_prev <- delta / se_at_k_prev_prev
  power_at_k_prev_prev <- pnorm(ncp_at_k_prev_prev - z_alpha_2) + (1 - pnorm(ncp_at_k_prev_prev + z_alpha_2))
  
  cat("=== REFERENCE DESIGN (k = " , k_prev_prev, ") ===\n")
  cat("  Achieved power:", power_at_k_prev_prev, "\n")
  cat("  Below target (0.90):", power_at_k_prev_prev < power_target, "\n\n")
}

# Confirm formula methodology
cat("=== FORMULA CONSISTENCY ===\n")
cat("Method: Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation (CV) approximation\n")
cat("  with additive one-cluster correction\n")
cat("Design effect formula: D_e = 1 + (k-1) * rho, where rho = CV^2\n")
cat("Intra-cluster correlation proxy: rho =", rho, "\n")
cat("Correction: k_adjusted = k_continuous + 1 before integer rounding\n\n")

cat("=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Sample size (clusters per arm): k =", k_integer, "\n")
cat("Continuous solution: k_cont =", round(k_cont, 4), "\n")
cat("With correction: k + 1 =", round(k_with_correction, 4), "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_at_k_int, 6), "\n")

# Output JSON
results_verify <- list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_integer, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_selected_design", value = round(power_at_k_int, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_k_prev, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_cont, 4), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "with_additive_correction", value = round(k_with_correction, 4), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "design_effect_rho", value = rho, unit = "dimensionless")
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = results_verify), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")

trace.code:
# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation approximation
# with additive one-cluster correction

# Parameters
treatment_rate <- 0.005  # per child-week
control_rate <- 0.010    # per child-week
exposure_per_cluster <- 2500  # child-weeks
between_cluster_cv <- 0.15    # dimensionless
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.90
sidedness <- 2  # two-sided test

# Design effect calculation
# rho = CV^2 (intra-cluster correlation from heterogeneous rates)
rho <- between_cluster_cv^2
cat("Between-cluster CV:", between_cluster_cv, "\n")
cat("Intra-cluster correlation proxy (rho = CV^2):", rho, "\n")

# Expected event counts per cluster
lambda_t <- treatment_rate * exposure_per_cluster
lambda_c <- control_rate * exposure_per_cluster
cat("\nExpected events per cluster (treatment):", lambda_t, "\n")
cat("Expected events per cluster (control):", lambda_c, "\n")

# Rate difference
rate_diff <- control_rate - treatment_rate
cat("Rate difference (H0: rate_diff = 0):", rate_diff, "\n")

# Variance of rate difference under null (equal allocation, k clusters per arm)
# Var(rate_diff | k) = Var(rate_c - rate_t | k)
# For Poisson with design effect:
# Var(lambda_i / exposure) = (lambda_i / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)
# Var(rate_diff) = (lambda_c / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) + (lambda_t / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)
#                = ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)

# Critical z-value (two-sided, alpha = 0.05)
z_alpha <- qnorm(1 - alpha / sidedness)
z_beta <- qnorm(target_power)
cat("\nZ-value for alpha =", alpha, "(two-sided):", z_alpha, "\n")
cat("Z-value for power =", target_power, ":", z_beta, "\n")

# Sample size formula:
# (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * Var(rate_diff) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
# 
# Var(rate_diff | k) = ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho)
#
# Rearranging for k:
# (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#
# Let a = (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) / exposure^2
# Then: a * (1 + (k-1)*rho) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#       a * (1 + k*rho - rho) = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#       a * (1 - rho) + a*k*rho = rate_diff^2 / (2k)
#       a * (1 - rho) * 2k + a*k*rho * 2k = rate_diff^2
#       2ak(1 - rho) + 2ak^2*rho = rate_diff^2
#       2*rho*a*k^2 + 2a(1 - rho)*k - rate_diff^2 = 0

a <- (z_alpha + z_beta)^2 * (lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)
cat("\nCoefficient a =", a, "\n")

# Quadratic equation: c*k^2 + b*k + d = 0
c_coef <- 2 * rho * a
b_coef <- 2 * a * (1 - rho)
d_coef <- -rate_diff^2

cat("Quadratic: ", c_coef, "* k^2 +", b_coef, "* k +", d_coef, "= 0\n")

# Solve quadratic
discriminant <- b_coef^2 - 4 * c_coef * d_coef
k_solutions <- c((-b_coef + sqrt(discriminant)) / (2 * c_coef),
                 (-b_coef - sqrt(discriminant)) / (2 * c_coef))
cat("\nQuadratic solutions for k (clusters per arm):\n")
print(k_solutions)

# Take positive solution
k_continuous <- k_solutions[k_solutions > 0][1]
cat("\nContinuous solution k =", k_continuous, "\n")

# Apply additive one-cluster correction
# The specification says to add 1 cluster to the numerator
# This means the formula becomes (k+1) clusters per arm requirement
# Interpretation: add 1 to the sample size before rounding
k_with_correction <- k_continuous + 1
cat("With additive one-cluster correction: k + 1 =", k_with_correction, "\n")

# Round up to nearest integer
k_per_arm <- ceiling(k_with_correction)
cat("Rounded up (integer clusters per arm):", k_per_arm, "\n")

# Verify: compute achieved power at this design
# Power = Pr(|test_stat| > z_alpha)
# test_stat ~ N(effect_size, 1) under alternative
# effect_size = rate_diff / sqrt(Var(rate_diff))

variance_at_k <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_per_arm - 1) * rho)
effect_size <- rate_diff / sqrt(variance_at_k / (2 * k_per_arm))
# Wait, let me reconsider the test statistic structure

# Actually, for a difference in rates with 2k total clusters:
# Var(rate_c) = (lambda_c/m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k  [pooled variance over k clusters]
# Var(rate_t) = (lambda_t/m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k
# Var(rate_diff) = Var(rate_c) + Var(rate_t) = ((lambda_c + lambda_t)/m^2) * (1 + (k-1)*rho) / k

# For statistical test (two-sample comparison):
# Z = rate_diff / sqrt(Var(rate_diff))
# Z ~ N(0,1) under H0: rate_diff = 0
# Under H1: Z ~ N(effect_size, 1)

variance_rate_diff_achieved <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_per_arm - 1) * rho) / k_per_arm
se_rate_diff <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_achieved)
effect_size_achieved <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff

# Non-centrality parameter for two-sided test
ncp <- effect_size_achieved
# Power = P(Z > z_alpha) + P(Z < -z_alpha) under H1
# With ncp, this is: P(N(ncp,1) > z_alpha) = 1 - Phi(z_alpha - ncp)
#                  + P(N(ncp,1) < -z_alpha) = Phi(-z_alpha - ncp)
# For one-sided at each tail (symmetric), power ≈ Phi(ncp - z_alpha) when ncp >> z_alpha
# For two-sided: power = Phi(ncp - z_alpha) + Phi(-ncp - z_alpha)
#                       = Phi(ncp - z_alpha) + [1 - Phi(ncp + z_alpha)]

power_achieved <- pnorm(ncp - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp + z_alpha)
cat("\n=== ACHIEVED POWER AT INTEGER DESIGN ===\n")
cat("Clusters per arm (k):", k_per_arm, "\n")
cat("Standard error of rate difference:", se_rate_diff, "\n")
cat("Effect size (ncp):", effect_size_achieved, "\n")
cat("Achieved power (two-sided):", power_achieved, "\n")

# Also check power at k_per_arm - 1 (preceding admissible design)
if (k_per_arm > 1) {
  k_prev <- k_per_arm - 1
  variance_rate_diff_prev <- ((lambda_c + lambda_t) / (exposure_per_cluster^2)) * (1 + (k_prev - 1) * rho) / k_prev
  se_rate_diff_prev <- sqrt(variance_rate_diff_prev)
  effect_size_prev <- rate_diff / se_rate_diff_prev
  ncp_prev <- effect_size_prev
  power_prev <- pnorm(ncp_prev - z_alpha) + 1 - pnorm(ncp_prev + z_alpha)
  
  cat("\n=== ACHIEVED POWER AT PRECEDING DESIGN ===\n")
  cat("Clusters per arm (k):", k_prev, "\n")
  cat("Standard error of rate difference:", se_rate_diff_prev, "\n")
  cat("Effect size (ncp):", effect_size_prev, "\n")
  cat("Achieved power (two-sided):", power_prev, "\n")
}

# Final result
cat("\n=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Sample size (clusters per arm):", k_per_arm, "\n")

# Prepare JSON output
results <- list(
  list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_per_arm, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_selected_design", value = round(power_achieved, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "achieved_power_at_preceding_design", value = round(power_prev, 6), unit = "dimensionless"),
  list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_continuous, 4), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
  list(metric = "design_effect_rho", value = rho, unit = "dimensionless")
)

cat("\n")
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=", jsonlite::toJSON(list(results = results), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15), "\n")
