# Final verification and detailed reporting of the cluster-rate CV calculation

library(jsonlite)

cat("=== CLUSTER-RATE COEFFICIENT-OF-VARIATION DESIGN ===\n")
cat("Sample Size Calculation for Cluster-Randomized Trial with Count Outcomes\n\n")

# ======== INPUT PARAMETERS ========
lambda_t <- 0.005     # treatment rate
lambda_c <- 0.010     # control rate
n_cluster <- 2500     # exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
cv <- 0.15            # between-cluster CV
power_target <- 0.90
alpha <- 0.05
allocation_ratio <- 1

cat("INPUT PARAMETERS:\n")
cat("  Control event rate (λ_c):", lambda_c, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Treatment event rate (λ_t):", lambda_t, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster:", n_cluster, "child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV (κ):", cv, "\n")
cat("  Target power (1 - β):", power_target, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (α, two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Allocation ratio (treatment:control):", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# ======== DERIVATION ========
cat("STATISTICAL MODEL:\n")
cat("  Outcome: Count of events per cluster, modeled as Poisson\n")
cat("  With between-cluster lognormal random variation (log-scale)\n")
cat("  Test: Two-sided comparison of log-rates\n\n")

z_alpha_half <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - power_target)

cat("CRITICAL VALUES:\n")
cat("  z_α/2 (two-sided, α=0.05):", round(z_alpha_half, 6), "\n")
cat("  z_β (power=0.90):", round(z_beta, 6), "\n")
cat("  z_α/2 - z_β:", round(z_alpha_half - z_beta, 6), "\n\n")

# Expected event counts
mu_t <- n_cluster * lambda_t
mu_c <- n_cluster * lambda_c

cat("EXPECTED EVENTS PER CLUSTER:\n")
cat("  Treatment (μ_t = λ_t × n):", mu_t, "\n")
cat("  Control (μ_c = λ_c × n):", mu_c, "\n\n")

# Effect size on log scale
log_rr <- log(lambda_c / lambda_t)  # log(control/treatment)

cat("EFFECT SIZE:\n")
cat("  Rate ratio (control/treatment):", lambda_c / lambda_t, "\n")
cat("  Log rate ratio:", round(log_rr, 6), "\n\n")

# Variance formula for difference in log-rates
# Var(ln(λ_t)) = CV² + 1/μ_t   [between-cluster + within-cluster]
# Var(ln(λ_c)) = CV² + 1/μ_c
# Var(ln(λ_c) - ln(λ_t)) = CV² + 1/μ_c + CV² + 1/μ_t
#                         = 2·CV² + (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c)

var_within <- 1/mu_t + 1/mu_c
var_between <- 2 * cv^2
var_total_per_cluster <- var_within + var_between

cat("VARIANCE OF LOG-RATE DIFFERENCE (per cluster):\n")
cat("  Within-cluster (Poisson):\n")
cat("    1/μ_t + 1/μ_c =", 1/mu_t, "+", 1/mu_c, "=", var_within, "\n")
cat("  Between-cluster (CV effect):\n")
cat("    2·CV² = 2 ×", cv^2, "=", var_between, "\n")
cat("  Total per cluster:", var_total_per_cluster, "\n\n")

# Sample size formula (continuous solution)
# k = (z_α/2 - z_β)² × [variance per cluster] / (effect)²
k_continuous_base <- (z_alpha_half - z_beta)^2 * var_total_per_cluster / (log_rr)^2

cat("CONTINUOUS SAMPLE SIZE (base, no correction):\n")
cat("  k = (z_α/2 - z_β)² × V / (log_RR)²\n")
cat("  k = (", round(z_alpha_half, 4), "–", round(z_beta, 4), ")² ×", 
    round(var_total_per_cluster, 6), "/ (", round(log_rr, 6), ")²\n")
cat("  k =", round(k_continuous_base, 6), "clusters per arm\n\n")

# One-cluster additive correction
# The correction adjusts for finite-sample properties
# Corrected k satisfies: k_adj = k_base × (k_adj - 1) / (k_adj - 2)
# or equivalently, apply iteratively

k_corrected <- k_continuous_base
for (iter in 1:50) {
  k_old <- k_corrected
  if (k_corrected > 2) {
    correction <- (k_corrected - 1) / (k_corrected - 2)
    k_corrected <- k_continuous_base * correction
  }
  if (abs(k_corrected - k_old) < 1e-12) break
}

cat("ONE-CLUSTER ADDITIVE CORRECTION:\n")
cat("  Applied iteratively: k_adj = k_base × (k_adj - 1)/(k_adj - 2)\n")
cat("  Corrected k =", round(k_corrected, 6), "clusters per arm\n\n")

# Integer rounding
k_floor <- floor(k_corrected)
k_ceil <- ceiling(k_corrected)

cat("INTEGER ROUNDING:\n")
cat("  floor(k) =", k_floor, "\n")
cat("  ceil(k) =", k_ceil, "\n\n")

# Power function for verification
power_at_k <- function(k) {
  if (k < 1) return(NA)
  var_mean <- var_total_per_cluster / k
  if (k > 2) {
    var_mean <- var_mean * (k - 1) / (k - 2)
  }
  z_test <- abs(log_rr) / sqrt(var_mean)
  power <- pnorm(z_test - z_alpha_half)
  return(power)
}

# Calculate power at candidate designs
power_floor <- power_at_k(k_floor)
power_ceil <- power_at_k(k_ceil)

cat("POWER VERIFICATION:\n")
cat("  Power at k =", k_floor, ":", round(power_floor, 6), "\n")
cat("  Power at k =", k_ceil, ":", round(power_ceil, 6), "\n\n")

# Select minimum k meeting target power
if (power_floor >= power_target) {
  k_selected <- k_floor
  power_selected <- power_floor
} else {
  k_selected <- k_ceil
  power_selected <- power_ceil
}

cat("=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Minimum clusters per arm (target power", power_target, "):", k_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_selected, 6), "\n")
cat("Total clusters:", k_selected * 2, "(both arms)\n")
cat("Total child-weeks:", k_selected * 2 * n_cluster, "\n\n")

# Preceding design
k_preceding <- k_selected - 1
power_preceding <- power_at_k(k_preceding)

cat("Preceding design (k =", k_preceding, "):\n")
cat("  Power:", round(power_preceding, 6), "\n\n")

# Summary of calculations
cat("SUMMARY:\n")
cat("  Method: Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation with one-cluster additive correction\n")
cat("  Outcome: Poisson count with between-cluster lognormal variation\n")
cat("  Test: Two-sided Wald test on log-rate difference\n")
cat("  Power requirement:", power_target, "at α=", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Minimum sample size: k =", k_selected, "clusters per arm\n")
cat("  Achieved power: ", round(power_selected, 6), "\n\n")

# JSON output
results_json <- toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_selected, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_selected, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_corrected, 15), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "total_clusters", value = k_selected * 2, unit = "clusters"),
      list(metric = "total_person_time", value = k_selected * 2 * n_cluster, unit = "child_weeks")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(results_json)

One-cluster additive correction is applied to the denominator
Normal approximation is adequate for the test statistic
scientific_notes: The cluster-rate CV method adjusts for between-cluster heterogeneity via the inflation factor (1 + CV²(k-1))/k, where k = exposure-adjusted cluster count

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation design with one-cluster additive correction
# Treatment rate: λ_t = 0.005 per child-week
# Control rate: λ_c = 0.010 per child-week
# Exposure per cluster: n = 2500 child-weeks
# Between-cluster CV: κ = 0.15
# Power: 1-β = 0.90, so β = 0.10, z_β = qnorm(0.10) = 1.282
# Significance level: α = 0.05 (two-sided), z_α/2 = qnorm(0.975) = 1.96
# Allocation: 1:1 (treatment:control)

library(jsonlite)

# Input parameters
lambda_t <- 0.005  # treatment rate
lambda_c <- 0.010  # control rate
n_cluster <- 2500  # child-weeks per cluster
cv <- 0.15         # between-cluster CV
power_target <- 0.90
alpha <- 0.05
allocation_ratio <- 1

# Z-values
z_alpha_half <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided: 1.96
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - power_target)    # 0.10 tail: 1.282

cat("Z-values:\n")
cat("  z_α/2 (two-sided, α=0.05):", z_alpha_half, "\n")
cat("  z_β (power=0.90):", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Effect size: log hazard ratio (or log rate ratio)
log_rr <- log(lambda_t / lambda_c)
cat("Effect size (log rate ratio):", log_rr, "\n")
cat("Rate ratio:", lambda_t / lambda_c, "\n\n")

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu_t <- n_cluster * lambda_t
mu_c <- n_cluster * lambda_c
cat("Expected events per cluster:\n")
cat("  Treatment:", mu_t, "\n")
cat("  Control:", mu_c, "\n\n")

# Variance of log-rate difference under Poisson-based approximation
# For cluster-level rates with CV adjustment:
# Var(log λ) ≈ (CV² + 1/μ) for sparse events in a cluster
# Here we use the standard approximation for Poisson with between-cluster variation:
# The inflation factor is (1 + CV²(k-1))/k where k is the effective cluster size in terms of events.
# For the cluster-rate method, k is related to the minimum expected count.

# Standard approach: variance of difference in log-rates is approximately
# σ² = (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c) * (1 + CV²) [assuming CV affects both marginal variances]
# With additive one-cluster correction, we adjust the variance by (k-1)/(k-2)

# Simplified formulation (common in literature):
# Sample size formula: k = (z_α/2 + z_β)² × [var_per_cluster] / (effect_size)²
# where var_per_cluster includes the CV inflation and one-cluster correction

# Using the cluster-rate CV formula:
# var_difference = (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c) × (1 + CV²(effective_k - 1)) / effective_k
# 
# For the one-cluster correction in denominator:
# k_clusters = ((z_α/2 + z_β)² / (log(λ_t/λ_c))²) × 
#              [(1/μ_t + 1/μ_c) × (1 + CV²)] × (k-1)/(k-2)
# 
# This requires iteration. Use simpler closed form first:

# Basic variance (Poisson, ignoring CV temporarily):
var_basic <- (1/mu_t + 1/mu_c)
cat("Basic variance (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c):", var_basic, "\n")

# Inflation factor due to between-cluster CV (assumes k >> 1 initially)
# When between-cluster CV = 0.15, the design effect is (1 + CV²) for large k
inflation_cv <- 1 + cv^2
cat("CV inflation factor (1 + CV²):", inflation_cv, "\n\n")

# Approximate cluster count (continuous solution) WITHOUT one-cluster correction
k_continuous_unadjusted <- ((z_alpha_half + z_beta)^2 / (log_rr)^2) * var_basic * inflation_cv

cat("Continuous solution (before one-cluster correction):\n")
cat("  k =", k_continuous_unadjusted, "clusters\n\n")

# Apply one-cluster additive correction:
# The correction modifies the variance inflation by (k-1)/(k-2)
# Or equivalently, we solve: k = base_formula * (k-1)/(k-2)
# This is a fixed-point equation.

# Fixed-point iteration:
k_corrected <- k_continuous_unadjusted
for (iter in 1:20) {
  k_old <- k_corrected
  # Variance term with one-cluster correction
  correction_factor <- (k_old - 1) / (k_old - 2)
  k_corrected <- k_continuous_unadjusted * correction_factor
  if (abs(k_corrected - k_old) < 1e-6) break
}

cat("Corrected solution (with one-cluster additive correction):\n")
cat("  Iteration converged\n")
cat("  k =", k_corrected, "clusters per arm\n\n")

# Round to integers and check both directions
k_floor <- floor(k_corrected)
k_ceil <- ceiling(k_corrected)

cat("Integer candidates:\n")
cat("  k_floor =", k_floor, "\n")
cat("  k_ceil =", k_ceil, "\n\n")

# Function to compute power at a given k
compute_power <- function(k) {
  correction_factor <- (k - 1) / (k - 2)
  variance_adjusted <- var_basic * inflation_cv * correction_factor
  z_test <- abs(log_rr) / sqrt(variance_adjusted)
  power <- 2 * pnorm(-z_test + z_alpha_half) 
  # Two-sided: P(|Z| > z_α/2) under alternative
  power_alt <- pnorm(z_test - z_alpha_half) + pnorm(-z_test - z_alpha_half)
  # Better: 1 - Φ(z_α/2 - z_test)
  power_correct <- 1 - pnorm(z_alpha_half - z_test)
  return(list(z_test = z_test, power = power_correct, variance = variance_adjusted))
}

result_floor <- compute_power(k_floor)
result_ceil <- compute_power(k_ceil)

cat("Power at k =", k_floor, ":\n")
cat("  Test statistic z =", result_floor$z_test, "\n")
cat("  Power =", result_floor$power, "\n")
cat("  Variance (adjusted) =", result_floor$variance, "\n\n")

cat("Power at k =", k_ceil, ":\n")
cat("  Test statistic z =", result_ceil$z_test, "\n")
cat("  Power =", result_ceil$power, "\n")
cat("  Variance (adjusted) =", result_ceil$variance, "\n\n")

# Select the minimum k meeting target power
if (result_floor$power >= power_target) {
  k_selected <- k_floor
  power_selected <- result_floor$power
} else {
  k_selected <- k_ceil
  power_selected <- result_ceil$power
}

cat("RESULT:\n")
cat("Minimum integer clusters per arm:", k_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_selected, "\n\n")

# Also report the preceding admissible design
if (k_selected == k_floor) {
  k_preceding <- k_floor - 1
  result_preceding <- compute_power(k_preceding)
  power_preceding <- result_preceding$power
} else {
  k_preceding <- k_floor
  power_preceding <- result_floor$power
}

cat("Preceding admissible design:\n")
cat("  Clusters per arm:", k_preceding, "\n")
cat("  Power:", power_preceding, "\n\n")

# Prepare output
results_list <- list(
  sample_size = k_selected,
  power_achieved = round(power_selected, 15),
  power_preceding = round(power_preceding, 15),
  clusters_preceding = k_preceding,
  continuous_solution = round(k_corrected, 15),
  k_floor = k_floor,
  k_ceil = k_ceil
)

cat("\n--- POWER_AGENT_RESULT ---\n")
cat(toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_selected, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_selected, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_corrected, 15), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
))

# Re-examine the cluster-rate CV methodology
# 
# The cluster-rate method is designed for count data (events) in clusters.
# Standard reference: Hayes & Moulton (2009), and Eldridge & Kerry (2012)
#
# For cluster randomized trials with count outcomes:
# - Cluster-level event rate follows a distribution with between-cluster variation
# - The design effect incorporates both the within-cluster correlation and CV
#
# Key formulas:
# λ_i ~ Gamma or lognormal with mean λ and CV κ
# E[Events in cluster i] = λ × n_i (where n_i is person-time)
# 
# For comparing two cluster-level rates λ_t vs λ_c,
# the test statistic variance includes:
# 1. Poisson variance: 1/μ_t + 1/μ_c where μ = λ × n
# 2. Between-cluster inflation: multiplied by (1 + CV²(k-1))/k for k clusters per arm
# 3. One-cluster additive correction: (k-1)/(k-2) adjustment
#
# However, the continuous solution of k ≈ 0.057 is suspiciously small.
# This is likely because the effect size is VERY LARGE:
# - Rate ratio = 0.5 (50% reduction)
# - Expected events per cluster: 25 (control) and 12.5 (treatment)
# - This is a strong signal with large expected counts
#
# Let me reconsider: perhaps the problem intends a DIFFERENT interpretation.
# 
# Alternative: the user may be asking for power at a specific sample size,
# or there may be a different parameterization for the cluster-rate CV method.
#
# Let me check: Hayes & Moulton cluster-rate formula typically written as:
# For comparing cluster means (or rates) in a CRT:
# 
# n = (z_α/2 + z_β)² × [Var_between + Var_within] / Δ²
#
# where Var_between = σ_b² (between-cluster variance)
# and Var_within depends on the outcome type
#
# For Poisson with lognormal random effects:
# The log-rate has variance approximately CV² + 1/E[count]
#
# Let me re-parameterize using a clearer statement:

library(jsonlite)

# Input parameters
lambda_t <- 0.005     # treatment: events per child-week
lambda_c <- 0.010     # control: events per child-week
n_cluster <- 2500     # child-weeks per cluster (exposure)
cv <- 0.15            # between-cluster CV (log-scale or rate-scale?)
power_target <- 0.90
alpha <- 0.05
allocation_ratio <- 1

# Z-values
z_alpha_half <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - power_target)

cat("=== CLUSTER-RATE CV DESIGN CALCULATION ===\n\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat("  Treatment rate (λ_t):", lambda_t, "events per child-week\n")
cat("  Control rate (λ_c):", lambda_c, "events per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster (n):", n_cluster, "child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV (κ):", cv, "\n")
cat("  Target power:", power_target, "\n")
cat("  α (two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Allocation: 1:1\n\n")

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu_t <- n_cluster * lambda_t
mu_c <- n_cluster * lambda_c
cat("Expected events per cluster:\n")
cat("  Treatment (μ_t):", mu_t, "\n")
cat("  Control (μ_c):", mu_c, "\n\n")

# Log rate ratio (effect size on log scale)
log_rr <- log(lambda_c / lambda_t)  # Control/Treatment, so positive for benefit
cat("Log rate ratio (control/treatment):", log_rr, "\n")
cat("Rate ratio:", lambda_c / lambda_t, "\n\n")

# Cluster-rate CV variance formula (from Hayes & Moulton and similar sources):
# For Poisson counts with between-cluster lognormal random variation:
# Var(ln(rate_i)) = Var_between + Var_within
# where:
#   Var_between ≈ CV² (assumed)
#   Var_within ≈ 1/μ (Poisson component)
#
# Variance of the difference in log-rates (assuming independence between arms):
# Var(ln(λ_t) - ln(λ_c)) = Var(ln(λ_t)) + Var(ln(λ_c))
#                         = [CV² + 1/μ_t] + [CV² + 1/μ_c]
#                         = 2·CV² + (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c)
#
# This assumes each cluster provides an independent estimate.
# With k clusters per arm:
# Var(mean_log_rate_t - mean_log_rate_c) = [2·CV² + (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c)] / k
#
# Sample size formula:
# k = (z_α/2 + z_β)² · [2·CV² + (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c)] / (log_rr)²
#
# One-cluster additive correction: multiply by (k-1)/(k-2) or add 1 to numerator

var_within <- 1/mu_t + 1/mu_c
var_between <- 2 * cv^2

cat("Variance components:\n")
cat("  Within-cluster (Poisson): 1/μ_t + 1/μ_c =", var_within, "\n")
cat("  Between-cluster (CV² effect): 2·CV² =", var_between, "\n")
cat("  Total per cluster:", var_within + var_between, "\n\n")

# Continuous sample size (clusters per arm)
k_continuous_base <- (z_alpha_half - z_beta)^2 * (var_within + var_between) / (log_rr)^2

cat("Continuous solution (base, no correction):\n")
cat("  k =", k_continuous_base, "clusters per arm\n\n")

# Apply one-cluster additive correction iteratively
# The correction modifies: k → k · (k-1) / (k-2)
k_corrected <- k_continuous_base
for (iter in 1:30) {
  k_old <- k_corrected
  if (k_corrected <= 2) {
    # Cannot apply correction for k ≤ 2; just use base
    k_corrected <- k_continuous_base
    break
  }
  correction <- (k_corrected - 1) / (k_corrected - 2)
  k_corrected <- k_continuous_base * correction
  if (abs(k_corrected - k_old) < 1e-9) break
}

cat("Continuous solution (with one-cluster correction):\n")
cat("  k =", k_corrected, "clusters per arm\n\n")

# Integer candidates
k_floor <- floor(k_corrected)
k_ceil <- ceiling(k_corrected)

# Ensure k_floor >= 1 for power calculation
if (k_floor < 1) k_floor <- 1

cat("Integer candidates:\n")
cat("  floor:", k_floor, "\n")
cat("  ceiling:", k_ceil, "\n\n")

# Function to compute achieved power
compute_power_at_k <- function(k) {
  if (k < 1) return(NA)
  
  # Variance at k clusters per arm
  # Total variance includes within-cluster and between-cluster components
  # Divided by k (averaging over k clusters)
  var_total_per_cluster <- var_within + var_between
  var_mean <- var_total_per_cluster / k
  
  # Apply one-cluster correction if k > 2
  if (k > 2) {
    correction <- (k - 1) / (k - 2)
    var_mean <- var_mean * correction
  }
  
  # Test statistic
  z_test <- abs(log_rr) / sqrt(var_mean)
  
  # Power (two-sided test at α = 0.05)
  # Under null: Z ~ N(0,1)
  # Under alt: Z ~ N(z_test, 1)
  # Power = P(|Z| > z_α/2 | alt) = P(Z > z_α/2) + P(Z < -z_α/2)
  #       = Φ(-z_α/2 + z_test) + Φ(-z_α/2 - z_test)
  #       = Φ(z_test - z_α/2)  [second term negligible for large z_test]
  power <- pnorm(z_test - z_alpha_half)
  
  return(list(
    k = k,
    var_mean = var_mean,
    z_test = z_test,
    power = power
  ))
}

# Compute power for candidate integers
res_floor <- compute_power_at_k(k_floor)
res_ceil <- compute_power_at_k(k_ceil)

cat("Power calculations:\n\n")
cat("At k =", k_floor, ":\n")
cat("  Variance (mean):", res_floor$var_mean, "\n")
cat("  z_test:", res_floor$z_test, "\n")
cat("  Power:", res_floor$power, "\n\n")

cat("At k =", k_ceil, ":\n")
cat("  Variance (mean):", res_ceil$var_mean, "\n")
cat("  z_test:", res_ceil$z_test, "\n")
cat("  Power:", res_ceil$power, "\n\n")

# Select minimum k meeting target power
if (res_floor$power >= power_target) {
  k_selected <- k_floor
  power_selected <- res_floor$power
} else if (res_ceil$power >= power_target) {
  k_selected <- k_ceil
  power_selected <- res_ceil$power
} else {
  # Need to search higher
  k_search <- k_ceil + 1
  while (k_search <= 10000) {
    res_search <- compute_power_at_k(k_search)
    if (res_search$power >= power_target) {
      k_selected <- k_search
      power_selected <- res_search$power
      break
    }
    k_search <- k_search + 1
  }
  if (k_search > 10000) {
    k_selected <- NA
    power_selected <- NA
  }
}

cat("=== RESULT ===\n")
cat("Minimum integer clusters per arm:", k_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_selected, "\n\n")

# Preceding design
k_preceding <- k_selected - 1
res_preceding <- compute_power_at_k(k_preceding)
power_preceding <- res_preceding$power

cat("Preceding design (k =", k_preceding, "):\n")
cat("  Power:", power_preceding, "\n\n")

# Output JSON
cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_selected, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_selected, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_corrected, 15), unit = "clusters_per_arm")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
))

# Final verification and detailed reporting of the cluster-rate CV calculation

library(jsonlite)

cat("=== CLUSTER-RATE COEFFICIENT-OF-VARIATION DESIGN ===\n")
cat("Sample Size Calculation for Cluster-Randomized Trial with Count Outcomes\n\n")

# ======== INPUT PARAMETERS ========
lambda_t <- 0.005     # treatment rate
lambda_c <- 0.010     # control rate
n_cluster <- 2500     # exposure per cluster (child-weeks)
cv <- 0.15            # between-cluster CV
power_target <- 0.90
alpha <- 0.05
allocation_ratio <- 1

cat("INPUT PARAMETERS:\n")
cat("  Control event rate (λ_c):", lambda_c, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Treatment event rate (λ_t):", lambda_t, "per child-week\n")
cat("  Exposure per cluster:", n_cluster, "child-weeks\n")
cat("  Between-cluster CV (κ):", cv, "\n")
cat("  Target power (1 - β):", power_target, "\n")
cat("  Significance level (α, two-sided):", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Allocation ratio (treatment:control):", allocation_ratio, ":1\n\n")

# ======== DERIVATION ========
cat("STATISTICAL MODEL:\n")
cat("  Outcome: Count of events per cluster, modeled as Poisson\n")
cat("  With between-cluster lognormal random variation (log-scale)\n")
cat("  Test: Two-sided comparison of log-rates\n\n")

z_alpha_half <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - power_target)

cat("CRITICAL VALUES:\n")
cat("  z_α/2 (two-sided, α=0.05):", round(z_alpha_half, 6), "\n")
cat("  z_β (power=0.90):", round(z_beta, 6), "\n")
cat("  z_α/2 - z_β:", round(z_alpha_half - z_beta, 6), "\n\n")

# Expected event counts
mu_t <- n_cluster * lambda_t
mu_c <- n_cluster * lambda_c

cat("EXPECTED EVENTS PER CLUSTER:\n")
cat("  Treatment (μ_t = λ_t × n):", mu_t, "\n")
cat("  Control (μ_c = λ_c × n):", mu_c, "\n\n")

# Effect size on log scale
log_rr <- log(lambda_c / lambda_t)  # log(control/treatment)

cat("EFFECT SIZE:\n")
cat("  Rate ratio (control/treatment):", lambda_c / lambda_t, "\n")
cat("  Log rate ratio:", round(log_rr, 6), "\n\n")

# Variance formula for difference in log-rates
# Var(ln(λ_t)) = CV² + 1/μ_t   [between-cluster + within-cluster]
# Var(ln(λ_c)) = CV² + 1/μ_c
# Var(ln(λ_c) - ln(λ_t)) = CV² + 1/μ_c + CV² + 1/μ_t
#                         = 2·CV² + (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c)

var_within <- 1/mu_t + 1/mu_c
var_between <- 2 * cv^2
var_total_per_cluster <- var_within + var_between

cat("VARIANCE OF LOG-RATE DIFFERENCE (per cluster):\n")
cat("  Within-cluster (Poisson):\n")
cat("    1/μ_t + 1/μ_c =", 1/mu_t, "+", 1/mu_c, "=", var_within, "\n")
cat("  Between-cluster (CV effect):\n")
cat("    2·CV² = 2 ×", cv^2, "=", var_between, "\n")
cat("  Total per cluster:", var_total_per_cluster, "\n\n")

# Sample size formula (continuous solution)
# k = (z_α/2 - z_β)² × [variance per cluster] / (effect)²
k_continuous_base <- (z_alpha_half - z_beta)^2 * var_total_per_cluster / (log_rr)^2

cat("CONTINUOUS SAMPLE SIZE (base, no correction):\n")
cat("  k = (z_α/2 - z_β)² × V / (log_RR)²\n")
cat("  k = (", round(z_alpha_half, 4), "–", round(z_beta, 4), ")² ×", 
    round(var_total_per_cluster, 6), "/ (", round(log_rr, 6), ")²\n")
cat("  k =", round(k_continuous_base, 6), "clusters per arm\n\n")

# One-cluster additive correction
# The correction adjusts for finite-sample properties
# Corrected k satisfies: k_adj = k_base × (k_adj - 1) / (k_adj - 2)
# or equivalently, apply iteratively

k_corrected <- k_continuous_base
for (iter in 1:50) {
  k_old <- k_corrected
  if (k_corrected > 2) {
    correction <- (k_corrected - 1) / (k_corrected - 2)
    k_corrected <- k_continuous_base * correction
  }
  if (abs(k_corrected - k_old) < 1e-12) break
}

cat("ONE-CLUSTER ADDITIVE CORRECTION:\n")
cat("  Applied iteratively: k_adj = k_base × (k_adj - 1)/(k_adj - 2)\n")
cat("  Corrected k =", round(k_corrected, 6), "clusters per arm\n\n")

# Integer rounding
k_floor <- floor(k_corrected)
k_ceil <- ceiling(k_corrected)

cat("INTEGER ROUNDING:\n")
cat("  floor(k) =", k_floor, "\n")
cat("  ceil(k) =", k_ceil, "\n\n")

# Power function for verification
power_at_k <- function(k) {
  if (k < 1) return(NA)
  var_mean <- var_total_per_cluster / k
  if (k > 2) {
    var_mean <- var_mean * (k - 1) / (k - 2)
  }
  z_test <- abs(log_rr) / sqrt(var_mean)
  power <- pnorm(z_test - z_alpha_half)
  return(power)
}

# Calculate power at candidate designs
power_floor <- power_at_k(k_floor)
power_ceil <- power_at_k(k_ceil)

cat("POWER VERIFICATION:\n")
cat("  Power at k =", k_floor, ":", round(power_floor, 6), "\n")
cat("  Power at k =", k_ceil, ":", round(power_ceil, 6), "\n\n")

# Select minimum k meeting target power
if (power_floor >= power_target) {
  k_selected <- k_floor
  power_selected <- power_floor
} else {
  k_selected <- k_ceil
  power_selected <- power_ceil
}

cat("=== FINAL ANSWER ===\n")
cat("Minimum clusters per arm (target power", power_target, "):", k_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", round(power_selected, 6), "\n")
cat("Total clusters:", k_selected * 2, "(both arms)\n")
cat("Total child-weeks:", k_selected * 2 * n_cluster, "\n\n")

# Preceding design
k_preceding <- k_selected - 1
power_preceding <- power_at_k(k_preceding)

cat("Preceding design (k =", k_preceding, "):\n")
cat("  Power:", round(power_preceding, 6), "\n\n")

# Summary of calculations
cat("SUMMARY:\n")
cat("  Method: Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation with one-cluster additive correction\n")
cat("  Outcome: Poisson count with between-cluster lognormal variation\n")
cat("  Test: Two-sided Wald test on log-rate difference\n")
cat("  Power requirement:", power_target, "at α=", alpha, "\n")
cat("  Minimum sample size: k =", k_selected, "clusters per arm\n")
cat("  Achieved power: ", round(power_selected, 6), "\n\n")

# JSON output
results_json <- toJSON(
  list(
    results = list(
      list(metric = "sample_size", value = k_selected, unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_selected, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_preceding, 15), unit = "probability"),
      list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(k_corrected, 15), unit = "clusters_per_arm"),
      list(metric = "total_clusters", value = k_selected * 2, unit = "clusters"),
      list(metric = "total_person_time", value = k_selected * 2 * n_cluster, unit = "child_weeks")
    )
  ),
  auto_unbox = TRUE,
  digits = 15
)

cat("POWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(results_json)

# Evidence e1; success=true

# Cluster-rate coefficient-of-variation design with one-cluster additive correction
# Treatment rate: λ_t = 0.005 per child-week
# Control rate: λ_c = 0.010 per child-week
# Exposure per cluster: n = 2500 child-weeks
# Between-cluster CV: κ = 0.15
# Power: 1-β = 0.90, so β = 0.10, z_β = qnorm(0.10) = 1.282
# Significance level: α = 0.05 (two-sided), z_α/2 = qnorm(0.975) = 1.96
# Allocation: 1:1 (treatment:control)

library(jsonlite)

# Input parameters
lambda_t <- 0.005  # treatment rate
lambda_c <- 0.010  # control rate
n_cluster <- 2500  # child-weeks per cluster
cv <- 0.15         # between-cluster CV
power_target <- 0.90
alpha <- 0.05
allocation_ratio <- 1

# Z-values
z_alpha_half <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided: 1.96
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - power_target)    # 0.10 tail: 1.282

cat("Z-values:\n")
cat("  z_α/2 (two-sided, α=0.05):", z_alpha_half, "\n")
cat("  z_β (power=0.90):", z_beta, "\n\n")

# Effect size: log hazard ratio (or log rate ratio)
log_rr <- log(lambda_t / lambda_c)
cat("Effect size (log rate ratio):", log_rr, "\n")
cat("Rate ratio:", lambda_t / lambda_c, "\n\n")

# Expected event counts per cluster
mu_t <- n_cluster * lambda_t
mu_c <- n_cluster * lambda_c
cat("Expected events per cluster:\n")
cat("  Treatment:", mu_t, "\n")
cat("  Control:", mu_c, "\n\n")

# Variance of log-rate difference under Poisson-based approximation
# For cluster-level rates with CV adjustment:
# Var(log λ) ≈ (CV² + 1/μ) for sparse events in a cluster
# Here we use the standard approximation for Poisson with between-cluster variation:
# The inflation factor is (1 + CV²(k-1))/k where k is the effective cluster size in terms of events.
# For the cluster-rate method, k is related to the minimum expected count.

# Standard approach: variance of difference in log-rates is approximately
# σ² = (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c) * (1 + CV²) [assuming CV affects both marginal variances]
# With additive one-cluster correction, we adjust the variance by (k-1)/(k-2)

# Simplified formulation (common in literature):
# Sample size formula: k = (z_α/2 + z_β)² × [var_per_cluster] / (effect_size)²
# where var_per_cluster includes the CV inflation and one-cluster correction

# Using the cluster-rate CV formula:
# var_difference = (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c) × (1 + CV²(effective_k - 1)) / effective_k
# 
# For the one-cluster correction in denominator:
# k_clusters = ((z_α/2 + z_β)² / (log(λ_t/λ_c))²) × 
#              [(1/μ_t + 1/μ_c) × (1 + CV²)] × (k-1)/(k-2)
# 
# This requires iteration. Use simpler closed form first:

# Basic variance (Poisson, ignoring CV temporarily):
var_basic <- (1/mu_t + 1/mu_c)
cat("Basic variance (1/μ_t + 1/μ_c):", var_basic, "\n")

# Inflation factor due to between-cluster CV (assumes k >> 1 initially)
# When between-cluster CV = 0.15, the design effect is (1 + CV²) for large k
inflation_cv <- 1 + cv^2
cat("CV inflation factor (1 + CV²):", inflation_cv, "\n\n")

# Approximate cluster count (continuous solution) WITHOUT one-cluster correction
k_continuous_unadjusted <- ((z_alpha_half + z_beta)^2 / (log_rr)^2) * var_basic * inflation_cv

cat("Continuous solution (before one-cluster correction):\n")
cat("  k =", k_continuous_unadjusted, "clusters\n\n")

# Apply one-cluster additive correction:
# The correction modifies the variance inflation by (k-1)/(k-2)
# Or equivalently, we solve: k = base_formula * (k-1)/(k-2)
# This is a fixed-point equation.

# Fixed-point iteration:
k_corrected <- k_continuous_unadjusted
for (iter in 1:20) {
  k_old <- k_corrected
  # Variance term with one-cluster correction
  correction_factor <- (k_old - 1) / (k_old - 2)
  k_corrected <- k_continuous_unadjusted * correction_factor
  if (abs(k_corrected - k_old) < 1e-6) break
}

cat("Corrected solution (with one-cluster additive correction):\n")
cat("  Iteration converged\n")
cat("  k =", k_corrected, "clusters per arm\n\n")

# Round to integers and check both directions
k_floor <- floor(k_corrected)
k_ceil <- ceiling(k_corrected)

cat("Integer candidates:\n")
cat("  k_floor =", k_floor, "\n")
cat("  k_ceil =", k_ceil, "\n\n")

# Function to compute power at a given k
compute_power <- function(k) {
  correction_factor <- (k - 1) / (k - 2)
  variance_adjusted <- var_basic * inflation_cv * correction_factor
  z_test <- abs(log_rr) / sqrt(variance_adjusted)
  power <- 2 * pnorm(-z_test + z_alpha_half) 
  # Two-sided: P(|Z| > z_α/2) under alternative
  power_alt <- pnorm(z_test - z_alpha_half) + pnorm(-z_test - z_alpha_half)
  # Better: 1 - Φ(z_α/2 - z_test)
  power_correct <- 1 - pnorm(z_alpha_half - z_test)
  return(list(z_test = z_test, power = power_correct, variance = variance_adjusted))
}

result_floor <- compute_power(k_floor)
result_ceil <- compute_power(k_ceil)

cat("Power at k =", k_floor, ":\n")
cat("  Test statistic z =", result_floor$z_test, "\n")
cat("  Power =", result_floor$power, "\n")
cat("  Variance (adjusted) =", result_floor$variance, "\n\n")

cat("Power at k =", k_ceil, ":\n")
cat("  Test statistic z =", result_ceil$z_test, "\n")
cat("  Power =", result_ceil$power, "\n")
cat("  Variance (adjusted) =", result_ceil$variance, "\n\n")

# Select the minimum k meeting target power
if (result_floor$power >= power_target) {
  k_selected <- k_floor
  power_selected <- result_floor$power
} else {
  k_selected <- k_ceil
  power_selected <- result_ceil$power
}

cat("RESULT:\n")
cat("Minimum integer clusters per arm:", k_selected, "\n")
cat("Achieved power:", power_selected, "\n\n")

# Also report the preceding admissible design
if (k_selected == k_floor) {
  k_preceding <- k_floor - 1
  result_preceding <- compute_power(k_preceding)

scientific_notes: The Freedman approximation uses the observed event probabilities and hazard ratio to estimate the number of events required, then divides by the average event probability to obtain total sample size.

answer.summary: Using the Freedman approximation for a two-sided log-rank test with α = 0.05, target power 80%, hazard ratio 0.7, event probabilities 0.3707 (treatment) and 0.4890 (control), and equal allocation (1:1), the required integer sample size is **294 participants per group** (588 total). This result was obtained using powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default and verified against the underlying Freedman formula: m = 252.04 events required, yielding n_E = n_C = 294 after ceiling rounding.
answer.method: Freedman approximation for log-rank test sample size calculation (powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default). The method estimates the number of events m required under the Freedman formula, then divides by the weighted average event probability to obtain total sample size, with equal allocation yielding equal per-group sizes. Formula: n_E = (m × k)/(k × p_E + p_C), where m = (1/k) × [(k·RR + 1)/(RR − 1)]² × (z_{1−α/2} + z_{1−β})², and RR is the hazard ratio, p_E and p_C are event probabilities, k is the allocation ratio, and z values are critical points from the standard normal distribution.
assumptions: Two independent treatment groups with 1:1 equal allocation
Two-sided log-rank test with significance level α = 0.05
Hazard ratio (treatment vs. control) = 0.7 under the alternative hypothesis
Event probabilities: treatment = 0.3707, control = 0.4890 over the study period
Target power = 80% (type II error β = 0.2)
Central limit theorem valid for large samples
Cox proportional hazards model applies
No post-hoc adjustments for multiple comparisons or interim analyses
limitations: The Freedman approximation is based on normal approximation and is suitable for large sample sizes; it does not account for small-sample adjustments
No inflation for loss to follow-up, non-adherence, or other practical complications is included
Event probabilities are treated as fixed; uncertainty in their specification is not propagated
The calculation assumes fixed follow-up time with the stated cumulative event rates; variation in follow-up duration is not considered
Rounding to the nearest integer may slightly alter the achieved power

# Load the powerSurvEpi package for survival study sample size calculation
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Set parameters according to user specification
alpha <- 0.05           # Two-sided significance level
beta <- 0.2             # Type II error (1 - power = 1 - 0.8 = 0.2)
hr <- 0.7               # Hazard ratio (treatment vs. control)
p_event_trt <- 0.3707   # Event probability in treatment group
p_event_ctrl <- 0.4890  # Event probability in control group
allocation <- 1         # Equal allocation (1:1)

# Use powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default for log-rank test sample size
# This function implements the Freedman approximation
result <- powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default(
  alpha = alpha,
  beta = beta,
  hr = hr,
  p_trt = p_event_trt,
  p_ctrl = p_event_ctrl,
  allocation_ratio = allocation
)

# Extract sample size per group (convert to integer by ceiling)
n_per_group <- ceiling(result)

# Display results
cat("=== Freedman Approximation for Log-Rank Test ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Alpha (two-sided): %g\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target Power: %g\n", 1 - beta))
cat(sprintf("Hazard Ratio (treatment vs. control): %g\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (treatment): %g\n", p_event_trt))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (control): %g\n", p_event_ctrl))
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio: %g:1\n", allocation))
cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("Calculated sample size per group (from formula): %.2f\n", result))
cat(sprintf("Integer sample size per group (ceiling): %d\n", n_per_group))
cat("\n")

# Output for structured reporting
output <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_per_group,
  unit = "participants_per_group"
)

print(output)

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     Sample size calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves
     Between Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for
     clinical trials.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     ssizeCT.default(power, 
                     k, 
                     pE, 
                     pC, 
                     RR, 
                     alpha = 0.05)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

   power: numeric. power to detect the magnitude of the hazard ratio as
          small as that specified by ‘RR’.

       k: numeric. ratio of participants in group E (experimental
          group) compared to group C (control group).

      pE: numeric. probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pC: numeric. probability of failure in group C (control group)
          over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

   alpha: numeric. type I error rate.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the sample size calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the number of participants needed in each group to
     achieve a power of 1-beta is

           n_E=\frac{m k}{k p_E + p_C}, n_C=\frac{m}{k p_E + p_C}       
     
     where

     m=\frac{1}{k}<=ft(\frac{k RR + 1}{RR - 1}\right)^2<=ft(
     z_{1-alpha/2}+z_{1-beta}
     \right)^2,
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1).

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     A two-element vector. The first element is n_E and the second
     element is n_C.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     (1) The sample size formula assumes that the central-limit theorem
     is valid and hence is appropriate for large samples. (2) n_E and
     n_C will be rounded up to integers.

# Verify the Freedman approximation calculation step-by-step
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Input parameters
power <- 0.8
k <- 1                    # Allocation ratio
pE <- 0.3707              # Event probability in treatment
pC <- 0.4890              # Event probability in control
RR <- 0.7                 # Hazard ratio
alpha <- 0.05             # Two-sided significance level
beta <- 1 - power         # Type II error rate

# Critical values from standard normal distribution
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)      # Two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - beta)              # Power-related critical value

cat("=== Freedman Approximation Formula Verification ===\n\n")
cat(sprintf("Input Parameters:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  power (1 - beta):           %.4f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  beta (type II error):       %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("  alpha (two-sided):          %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio k:         %.1f\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  Event prob. in treatment:   %.4f\n", pE))
cat(sprintf("  Event prob. in control:     %.4f\n", pC))
cat(sprintf("  Hazard ratio (RR):          %.4f\n\n", RR))

cat(sprintf("Critical Values from Standard Normal:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-alpha/2) [two-sided]:  %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-beta):                 %.6f\n\n", z_beta))

# Freedman formula components
# m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2
numerator_fraction <- (k * RR + 1) / (RR - 1)
z_sum <- z_alpha_2 + z_beta
m <- (1 / k) * (numerator_fraction ^ 2) * (z_sum ^ 2)

cat(sprintf("Freedman Formula Calculation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  (k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1) = (1*0.7 + 1)/(0.7 - 1) = %.6f\n", numerator_fraction))
cat(sprintf("  ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 = %.6f\n", numerator_fraction ^ 2))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-alpha/2) + z_(1-beta) = %.6f + %.6f = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2, z_beta, z_sum))
cat(sprintf("  (z_(1-alpha/2) + z_(1-beta))^2 = %.6f\n", z_sum ^ 2))
cat(sprintf("  m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 = %.6f\n\n", m))

# Total events and per-group sample sizes
# n_E = (m * k) / (k * pE + pC)
# n_C = m / (k * pE + pC)
denom <- k * pE + pC
n_E <- (m * k) / denom
n_C <- m / denom

cat(sprintf("Sample Size Calculation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator (k*pE + pC):   %.6f\n", denom))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = (m*k) / (k*pE + pC) = (%.6f * %.1f) / %.6f = %.2f → %d\n", 
            m, k, denom, n_E, ceiling(n_E)))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = m / (k*pE + pC)      = %.6f / %.6f = %.2f → %d\n", 
            m, denom, n_C, ceiling(n_C)))
cat("\n")

# Total events under the design
total_events <- ceiling(n_E) * pE + ceiling(n_C) * pC
cat(sprintf("Expected Events:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Events in treatment group:  %.2f\n", ceiling(n_E) * pE))
cat(sprintf("  Events in control group:    %.2f\n", ceiling(n_C) * pC))
cat(sprintf("  Total expected events:      %.2f\n\n", total_events))

# Confirm with ssizeCT.default
result <- ssizeCT.default(power = power, k = k, pE = pE, pC = pC, RR = RR, alpha = alpha)
cat(sprintf("Confirmation from ssizeCT.default:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E (treatment):  %d participants\n", result[1]))
cat(sprintf("  n_C (control):    %d participants\n", result[2]))

plan.estimand: Number of participants per group in a two-arm survival study with log-rank test
plan.hypothesis: Null: hazard ratio = 1 vs. Alternative: hazard ratio ≠ 1
assumptions: Two independent treatment groups with equal allocation (1:1)
Survival times follow an exponential or other distribution where event probabilities are interpreted as cumulative event rates over the study period
Log-rank test with two-sided type-I error rate α = 0.05
Freedman normal approximation formula for sample size calculation
No loss to follow-up or administrative censoring beyond the event probabilities specified
scientific_notes: The Freedman approximation uses the observed event probabilities and hazard ratio to estimate the number of events required, then divides by the average event probability to obtain total sample size.
This approach is referenced in powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default and is suitable when planning studies with survival endpoints.
The result will be an integer sample size per group achieved by rounding up to the nearest whole participant.

# Load the powerSurvEpi package for survival study sample size calculation
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Set parameters according to user specification
alpha <- 0.05           # Two-sided significance level
beta <- 0.2             # Type II error (1 - power = 1 - 0.8 = 0.2)
hr <- 0.7               # Hazard ratio (treatment vs. control)
p_event_trt <- 0.3707   # Event probability in treatment group
p_event_ctrl <- 0.4890  # Event probability in control group
allocation <- 1         # Equal allocation (1:1)

# Use powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default for log-rank test sample size
# This function implements the Freedman approximation
result <- powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default(
  alpha = alpha,
  beta = beta,
  hr = hr,
  p_trt = p_event_trt,
  p_ctrl = p_event_ctrl,
  allocation_ratio = allocation
)

# Extract sample size per group (convert to integer by ceiling)
n_per_group <- ceiling(result)

# Display results
cat("=== Freedman Approximation for Log-Rank Test ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Alpha (two-sided): %g\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target Power: %g\n", 1 - beta))
cat(sprintf("Hazard Ratio (treatment vs. control): %g\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (treatment): %g\n", p_event_trt))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (control): %g\n", p_event_ctrl))
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio: %g:1\n", allocation))
cat("\n")
cat(sprintf("Calculated sample size per group (from formula): %.2f\n", result))
cat(sprintf("Integer sample size per group (ceiling): %d\n", n_per_group))
cat("\n")

# Output for structured reporting
output <- data.frame(
  metric = "sample_size",
  value = n_per_group,
  unit = "participants_per_group"
)

print(output)

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     Sample size calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves
     Between Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for
     clinical trials.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     ssizeCT.default(power, 
                     k, 
                     pE, 
                     pC, 
                     RR, 
                     alpha = 0.05)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

   power: numeric. power to detect the magnitude of the hazard ratio as
          small as that specified by ‘RR’.

       k: numeric. ratio of participants in group E (experimental
          group) compared to group C (control group).

      pE: numeric. probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pC: numeric. probability of failure in group C (control group)
          over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

   alpha: numeric. type I error rate.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the sample size calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the number of participants needed in each group to
     achieve a power of 1-beta is

           n_E=\frac{m k}{k p_E + p_C}, n_C=\frac{m}{k p_E + p_C}       
     
     where

     m=\frac{1}{k}<=ft(\frac{k RR + 1}{RR - 1}\right)^2<=ft(
     z_{1-alpha/2}+z_{1-beta}
     \right)^2,
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1).

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     A two-element vector. The first element is n_E and the second
     element is n_C.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     (1) The sample size formula assumes that the central-limit theorem
     is valid and hence is appropriate for large samples. (2) n_E and
     n_C will be rounded up to integers.

_ R_ e_ f_ e_ r_ e_ n_ c_ e_ s:

     Freedman, L.S. (1982).  Tables of the number of patients required
     in clinical trials using the log-rank test.  _Statistics in
     Medicine_. 1: 121-129

# Verify the Freedman approximation calculation step-by-step
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Input parameters
power <- 0.8
k <- 1                    # Allocation ratio
pE <- 0.3707              # Event probability in treatment
pC <- 0.4890              # Event probability in control
RR <- 0.7                 # Hazard ratio
alpha <- 0.05             # Two-sided significance level
beta <- 1 - power         # Type II error rate

# Critical values from standard normal distribution
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha / 2)      # Two-sided critical value
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - beta)              # Power-related critical value

cat("=== Freedman Approximation Formula Verification ===\n\n")
cat(sprintf("Input Parameters:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  power (1 - beta):           %.4f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  beta (type II error):       %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("  alpha (two-sided):          %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio k:         %.1f\n", k))
cat(sprintf("  Event prob. in treatment:   %.4f\n", pE))
cat(sprintf("  Event prob. in control:     %.4f\n", pC))
cat(sprintf("  Hazard ratio (RR):          %.4f\n\n", RR))

cat(sprintf("Critical Values from Standard Normal:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-alpha/2) [two-sided]:  %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-beta):                 %.6f\n\n", z_beta))

# Freedman formula components
# m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2
numerator_fraction <- (k * RR + 1) / (RR - 1)
z_sum <- z_alpha_2 + z_beta
m <- (1 / k) * (numerator_fraction ^ 2) * (z_sum ^ 2)

cat(sprintf("Freedman Formula Calculation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  (k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1) = (1*0.7 + 1)/(0.7 - 1) = %.6f\n", numerator_fraction))
cat(sprintf("  ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 = %.6f\n", numerator_fraction ^ 2))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-alpha/2) + z_(1-beta) = %.6f + %.6f = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2, z_beta, z_sum))
cat(sprintf("  (z_(1-alpha/2) + z_(1-beta))^2 = %.6f\n", z_sum ^ 2))
cat(sprintf("  m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 = %.6f\n\n", m))

# Total events and per-group sample sizes
# n_E = (m * k) / (k * pE + pC)
# n_C = m / (k * pE + pC)
denom <- k * pE + pC
n_E <- (m * k) / denom
n_C <- m / denom

cat(sprintf("Sample Size Calculation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator (k*pE + pC):   %.6f\n", denom))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = (m*k) / (k*pE + pC) = (%.6f * %.1f) / %.6f = %.2f → %d\n", 
            m, k, denom, n_E, ceiling(n_E)))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = m / (k*pE + pC)      = %.6f / %.6f = %.2f → %d\n", 
            m, denom, n_C, ceiling(n_C)))
cat("\n")

# Total events under the design
total_events <- ceiling(n_E) * pE + ceiling(n_C) * pC
cat(sprintf("Expected Events:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Events in treatment group:  %.2f\n", ceiling(n_E) * pE))
cat(sprintf("  Events in control group:    %.2f\n", ceiling(n_C) * pC))
cat(sprintf("  Total expected events:      %.2f\n\n", total_events))

# Confirm with ssizeCT.default
result <- ssizeCT.default(power = power, k = k, pE = pE, pC = pC, RR = RR, alpha = alpha)
cat(sprintf("Confirmation from ssizeCT.default:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E (treatment):  %d participants\n", result[1]))
cat(sprintf("  n_C (control):    %d participants\n", result[2]))

cat(sprintf("  z_(1-alpha/2) [two-sided]:  %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-beta):                 %.6f\n\n", z_beta))

# Freedman formula components
# m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2
numerator_fraction <- (k * RR + 1) / (RR - 1)
z_sum <- z_alpha_2 + z_beta
m <- (1 / k) * (numerator_fraction ^ 2) * (z_sum ^ 2)

cat(sprintf("Freedman Formula Calculation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  (k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1) = (1*0.7 + 1)/(0.7 - 1) = %.6f\n", numerator_fraction))
cat(sprintf("  ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 = %.6f\n", numerator_fraction ^ 2))
cat(sprintf("  z_(1-alpha/2) + z_(1-beta) = %.6f + %.6f = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2, z_beta, z_sum))
cat(sprintf("  (z_(1-alpha/2) + z_(1-beta))^2 = %.6f\n", z_sum ^ 2))
cat(sprintf("  m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_alpha/2 + z_beta)^2 = %.6f\n\n", m))

# Total events and per-group sample sizes
# n_E = (m * k) / (k * pE + pC)
# n_C = m / (k * pE + pC)
denom <- k * pE + pC
n_E <- (m * k) / denom
n_C <- m / denom

cat(sprintf("Sample Size Calculation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator (k*pE + pC):   %.6f\n", denom))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = (m*k) / (k*pE + pC) = (%.6f * %.1f) / %.6f = %.2f → %d\n", 
            m, k, denom, n_E, ceiling(n_E)))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = m / (k*pE + pC)      = %.6f / %.6f = %.2f → %d\n", 
            m, denom, n_C, ceiling(n_C)))
cat("\n")

# Total events under the design
total_events <- ceiling(n_E) * pE + ceiling(n_C) * pC
cat(sprintf("Expected Events:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Events in treatment group:  %.2f\n", ceiling(n_E) * pE))
cat(sprintf("  Events in control group:    %.2f\n", ceiling(n_C) * pC))
cat(sprintf("  Total expected events:      %.2f\n\n", total_events))

# Confirm with ssizeCT.default
result <- ssizeCT.default(power = power, k = k, pE = pE, pC = pC, RR = RR, alpha = alpha)
cat(sprintf("Confirmation from ssizeCT.default:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E (treatment):  %d participants\n", result[1]))
cat(sprintf("  n_C (control):    %d participants\n", result[2]))

Independent observations

answer.summary: Using the Freedman (1982) approximation for two-sided log-rank test with a hazard ratio of 0.7, event probabilities of 0.3707 (treatment) and 0.4890 (control), two-sided alpha=0.05, target power=0.80, and equal allocation (1:1), the required sample size is 294 participants per group (588 total). The continuous solution (293.17) was rounded up to the nearest integer following standard sample size convention.
answer.method: Freedman approximation (Freedman, 1982) implemented via powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default. The method calculates the required number of events using m = (1/k)·[(k·HR+1)/(HR-1)]²·(z₁₋α/₂+z₁₋β)², then converts to participant sample size using n = m·k/(k·pE+pC) and n = m/(k·pE+pC). Sample sizes are rounded up to integers.
assumptions: Two-sided log-rank test testing H₀: HR=1 vs H₁: HR≠1
Equal allocation ratio (1:1)
Event probabilities represent cumulative incidence over study period
Proportional hazards assumption holds
No censoring mechanism other than study-defined administrative censoring
Independent observations
Large-sample validity of central limit theorem approximation
No competing risks
limitations: Freedman approximation relies on large-sample asymptotics; validity depends on adequate event counts (>20-30 per group recommended)
Method assumes proportional hazards which may not hold in practice
Does not account for potential protocol violations, non-adherence, or irregular follow-up patterns
Sample size is deterministic under specified parameters; actual trial power may vary with realized event probabilities
No adjustment for multiple comparisons if planned
Assumes event probabilities are accurately specified a priori

# Install and load powerSurvEpi for verification
if (!requireNamespace("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", quiet = TRUE)
}
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Define parameters
alpha <- 0.05  # two-sided significance level
power <- 0.80  # target power
hr <- 0.7      # hazard ratio (alternative)
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # event probability in treatment group
p_control <- 0.4890    # event probability in control group
allocation_ratio <- 1  # equal allocation

# Calculate using powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default
# This function uses Freedman approximation
# ssizeCT.default computes sample size per group for two-sample survival test

result <- ssizeCT.default(
  alpha = alpha,
  power = power,
  hazardRatio = hr,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  p2 = p_control
)

# Extract sample size per group
n_per_group_continuous <- result$n

# Standard ceiling rounding for sample size
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("=== Freedman Approximation for Log-Rank Test ===\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (two-sided): %g\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power: %g\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  Hazard ratio: %g\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("  Event probability (treatment): %g\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("  Event probability (control): %g\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio: %g\n", allocation_ratio))
cat("\nResults:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Continuous sample size per group: %.4f\n", n_per_group_continuous))
cat(sprintf("  Integer sample size per group (ceiling): %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d\n", 2 * n_per_group))

# Verification: compute power at the rounded sample size
# Use powerSurvEpi::powerSurvEpi for power verification
power_check <- powerSurvEpi(
  N = 2 * n_per_group,  # total sample size
  hazardRatio = hr,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  p2 = p_control,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat(sprintf("\nVerification - Achieved power at n=%d per group: %.6f\n", 
            n_per_group, power_check$power)

# Also check power at ceiling - 1
n_lower <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_lower > 0) {
  power_lower <- powerSurvEpi(
    N = 2 * n_lower,
    hazardRatio = hr,
    p1 = p_treatment,
    p2 = p_control,
    alpha = alpha
  )
  cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d per group: %.6f\n", n_lower, power_lower$power))
}

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_list <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = 2 * n_per_group, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_check$power, 6), unit = "proportion")
  )
)

cat("\n=== Output for Structured Reporting ===\n")
cat("Primary metric: sample_size = ", n_per_group, " participants_per_group\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_check$power, 6), "\n")

# Return as JSON
library(jsonlite)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(result_list, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Verify the Freedman approximation manually
# Formula from the documentation:
# n_E = m*k / (k*pE + pC)
# n_C = m / (k*pE + pC)
# where m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
power <- 0.80
beta <- 1 - power  # 0.20
hr <- 0.7  # This is RR in the formula (hazard ratio)
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # pE (experimental)
p_control <- 0.4890    # pC (control)
k <- 1  # allocation ratio

# Critical values from standard normal distribution
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - beta)  # one-sided for power

cat("=== Manual Verification of Freedman Approximation ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Input parameters:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  alpha (two-sided): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  beta (1 - power): %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("  power: %.4f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  HR (RR): %.1f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("  pE (treatment): %.4f\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("  pC (control): %.4f\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("  k (allocation ratio): %.1f\n\n", k))

cat(sprintf("Critical values:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  z_{1-alpha/2} (two-sided): %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_{1-beta} (power): %.6f\n\n", z_beta))

# Compute m using the formula
numerator_ratio <- (k * hr + 1) / (hr - 1)
cat(sprintf("Formula components:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  (k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1) = (%.1f*%.1f + 1)/(%.1f - 1) = %.6f\n", 
            k, hr, hr, numerator_ratio))

ratio_squared <- numerator_ratio^2
cat(sprintf("  Squared ratio: %.6f\n", ratio_squared))

z_sum <- z_alpha_2 + z_beta
z_sum_squared <- z_sum^2
cat(sprintf("  (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2 = (%.6f + %.6f)^2 = %.6f\n\n",
            z_alpha_2, z_beta, z_sum_squared))

m <- (1/k) * ratio_squared * z_sum_squared
cat(sprintf("m = (1/k) * ((k*RR + 1)/(RR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-alpha/2} + z_{1-beta})^2\n"))
cat(sprintf("m = (1/%.1f) * %.6f * %.6f\n", k, ratio_squared, z_sum_squared))
cat(sprintf("m = %.6f\n\n", m))

# Compute sample sizes
denominator <- k * p_treatment + p_control
cat(sprintf("Denominator: k*pE + pC = %.1f*%.4f + %.4f = %.6f\n\n", 
            k, p_treatment, p_control, denominator))

n_E <- m * k / denominator
n_C <- m / denominator

cat(sprintf("Sample sizes (continuous):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = m*k / (k*pE + pC) = %.6f * %.1f / %.6f = %.6f\n", 
            m, k, denominator, n_E))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = m / (k*pE + pC) = %.6f / %.6f = %.6f\n\n", 
            m, denominator, n_C))

# Round up to integers
n_E_int <- ceiling(n_E)
n_C_int <- ceiling(n_C)

cat(sprintf("Sample sizes (rounded up to integers):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = %d (from %.6f)\n", n_E_int, n_E))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = %d (from %.6f)\n", n_C_int, n_C))
cat(sprintf("  Total: %d\n\n", n_E_int + n_C_int))

# Compare with ssizeCT.default result
library(powerSurvEpi)
result_ssizeCT <- ssizeCT.default(
  power = power,
  k = k,
  pE = p_treatment,
  pC = p_control,
  RR = hr,

)

            result_ssizeCT[1], result_ssizeCT[2]))
cat(sprintf("  Match: %s\n", 
            if (n_E_int == result_ssizeCT[1] & n_C_int == result_ssizeCT[2]) "✓ YES" else "✗ NO"))

# Summary for structured reporting
cat(sprintf("\n=== Summary ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Method: Freedman approximation (1982) for log-rank test\n"))
cat(sprintf("Study design: Two-sided log-rank test\n"))
cat(sprintf("Hypothesis: H0: HR = 1 vs H1: HR ≠ 1\n"))
cat(sprintf("Significance level: %.4f (two-sided)\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("Effect size (HR): %.1f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (treatment): %.4f\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("Event probability (control): %.4f\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("Allocation ratio: %.1f:1\n\n", k))
cat(sprintf("PRIMARY RESULT:\n"))
cat(sprintf("Sample size per group: %d participants\n", n_E_int))
cat(sprintf("Total sample size: %d participants\n", n_E_int + n_C_int))

# Independent verification using direct formula implementation
# without relying on powerSurvEpi package

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
power <- 0.80
beta <- 1 - power
hr <- 0.7
p_E <- 0.3707   # experimental/treatment
p_C <- 0.4890   # control
k <- 1          # allocation ratio

# Step 1: Compute critical values
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - beta)

cat("=== Independent Verification of Freedman Approximation ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Input parameters:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  α (two-sided): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Power: %.2f, β: %.4f\n", power, beta))
cat(sprintf("  HR: %.1f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("  p_E (treatment): %.4f\n", p_E))
cat(sprintf("  p_C (control): %.4f\n", p_C))
cat(sprintf("  k (ratio E:C): %.1f\n\n", k))

# Step 2: Compute m (number of events)
# Formula: m = (1/k) * ((k*HR + 1)/(HR - 1))^2 * (z_{1-α/2} + z_{1-β})^2

numerator_term <- (k * hr + 1) / (hr - 1)
m <- (1/k) * (numerator_term^2) * ((z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2)

cat(sprintf("Critical values:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  z_{1-α/2} = %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_{1-β} = %.6f\n", z_beta))
cat(sprintf("  Sum: %.6f, Squared: %.6f\n\n", z_alpha_2 + z_beta, (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2))

cat(sprintf("Event number calculation:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  (k*HR + 1)/(HR - 1) = (%.1f × %.1f + 1)/(%.1f - 1) = %.6f\n", 
            k, hr, hr, numerator_term))
cat(sprintf("  m = (1/k) × [ratio]^2 × [z-sum]^2\n"))
cat(sprintf("  m = (1/%.1f) × %.6f × %.6f = %.6f\n\n", 
            k, numerator_term^2, (z_alpha_2 + z_beta)^2, m))

# Step 3: Convert events to sample size
# n_E = m*k / (k*p_E + p_C)
# n_C = m / (k*p_E + p_C)

denominator <- k * p_E + p_C
n_E_continuous <- m * k / denominator
n_C_continuous <- m / denominator

cat(sprintf("Sample size conversion (continuous):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  Denominator: k×p_E + p_C = %.1f × %.4f + %.4f = %.6f\n",
            k, p_E, p_C, denominator))
cat(sprintf("  n_E = m×k / denominator = %.6f × %.1f / %.6f = %.6f\n", 
            m, k, denominator, n_E_continuous))
cat(sprintf("  n_C = m / denominator = %.6f / %.6f = %.6f\n\n", 
            m, denominator, n_C_continuous))

# Step 4: Round to integers
n_E_int <- ceiling(n_E_continuous)
n_C_int <- ceiling(n_C_continuous)

cat(sprintf("Rounded to integers (ceiling convention):\n"))
cat(sprintf("  n_E: %.6f → %d\n", n_E_continuous, n_E_int))
cat(sprintf("  n_C: %.6f → %d\n", n_E_continuous, n_C_int))
cat(sprintf("  Total: %d\n\n", n_E_int + n_C_int))

# Step 5: Verify with powerSurvEpi package
library(powerSurvEpi)
result_pkg <- ssizeCT.default(
  power = power,
  k = k,
  pE = p_E,
  pC = p_C,
  RR = hr,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat(sprintf("=== Comparison with powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Package result: n_E = %d, n_C = %d\n", result_pkg[1], result_pkg[2]))
cat(sprintf("Manual calculation: n_E = %d, n_C = %d\n", n_E_int, n_C_int))
cat(sprintf("Match: %s\n\n", 
    if(all(c(n_E_int, n_C_int) == result_pkg)) "✓ VERIFIED" else "✗ MISMATCH"))

# Step 6: Additional checks
cat(sprintf("=== Sanity Checks ===\n"))

# Event count at rounded sample size
total_n <- n_E_int + n_C_int
expected_events <- n_E_int * p_E + n_C_int * p_C
cat(sprintf("Expected number of events at n=%d per group:\n", n_E_int))
cat(sprintf("  n_E × p_E + n_C × p_C = %d × %.4f + %d × %.4f = %.2f events\n",
            n_E_int, p_E, n_C_int, p_C, expected_events))
cat(sprintf("  Calculated m (required events): %.2f\n", m))
cat(sprintf("  Ratio achieved/required: %.4f\n\n", expected_events / m))

# Power calculation at rounded design
# We can estimate power using the Freedman formula inverted:
# power = Φ(√m × (HR-1)/(k×HR+1) × √(denominator/m) - z_{1-α/2})

# More directly: when we have n participants, we have approximately
# E[# events] = n_E × p_E + n_C × p_C events
# The test statistic follows approximately N(0,1) under H0
# and shifts by √m(HR-1)/(k×HR+1) under HA with expected events m

# For quick validation: achieved power should be >= target if n is correctly chosen
cat(sprintf("=== Design Specification Summary ===\n"))
cat(sprintf("Method: Freedman (1982) approximation\n"))
cat(sprintf("Hypothesis: Two-sided log-rank test, H0: HR=1 vs H1: HR≠1\n"))
cat(sprintf("Significance level: α = %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("Effect size: HR = %.1f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("Event probabilities: p_E = %.4f, p_C = %.4f\n", p_E, p_C))
cat(sprintf("Allocation: 1:1 (equal arms)\n\n"))
cat(sprintf("PRIMARY RESULT:\n"))
cat(sprintf("Sample size per group: %d\n", n_E_int))
cat(sprintf("Total sample size: %d\n", total_n))
cat(sprintf("Expected events: %.1f\n", expected_events))

# JSON output
library(jsonlite)
results_json <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_E_int, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = total_n, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "expected_events", value = round(expected_events, 1), unit = "count"),
    list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(n_E_continuous, 6), unit = "participants")
  )
)

cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(results_json, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

library(powerSurvEpi)

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
hr <- 0.7
p_E <- 0.3707
p_C <- 0.4890
target_power <- 0.80

# Test sample sizes around the continuous solution (293.17)
test_ns <- c(292, 293, 294, 295)

cat("=== Power Verification at Boundary Sample Sizes ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Testing n per group near continuous solution (293.17)\n"))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n\n", target_power))

power_results <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = integer(),
  total_n = integer(),
  achieved_power = numeric(),
  meets_target = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (n in test_ns) {
  total_n <- 2 * n
  
  # Calculate power using powerSurvEpi::powerSurvEpi function
  power_obj <- powerSurvEpi(
    N = total_n,
    hazardRatio = hr,
    p1 = p_E,
    p2 = p_C,
    alpha = alpha
  )
  
  power_achieved <- power_obj$power
  meets <- if (power_achieved >= target_power) "✓ YES" else "✗ NO"
  
  power_results <- rbind(power_results, data.frame(
    n_per_group = n,
    total_n = total_n,
    achieved_power = power_achieved,
    meets_target = meets
  ))
  
  cat(sprintf("n = %d per group (N = %d total): Power = %.6f %s\n",
              n, total_n, power_achieved, meets))
}

cat("\n=== Minimum Admissible Design ===\n")

min_admissible <- power_results$n_per_group[
  power_results$achieved_power >= target_power][1]

library(powerSurvEpi)

# Parameters
alpha <- 0.05
hr <- 0.7
p_E <- 0.3707
p_C <- 0.4890
k <- 1  # equal allocation
target_power <- 0.80

# Test sample sizes around the continuous solution (293.17)
test_ns <- c(292, 293, 294, 295)

cat("=== Power Verification at Boundary Sample Sizes ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Testing n per group near continuous solution (293.167674)\n"))
cat(sprintf("Target power: %.2f\n\n", target_power))

power_results <- data.frame(
  n_per_group = integer(),
  total_n = integer(),
  achieved_power = numeric(),
  meets_target = character(),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

for (n in test_ns) {
  total_n <- 2 * n
  
  # Calculate power using powerCT.default
  # powerCT.default(power, k, pE, pC, RR, alpha)
  # But we need to invert: given n, what is the power?
  # Looking at the documentation, we may need powerCT.default0 or compute it differently
  
  # Actually, the package provides ssizeCT which inverts for sample size
  # For power given sample size, we need to iterate or use the formula
  
  # Using the Freedman formula directly to compute power
  # Given n, number of events m = (k*pE + pC) * n / (k + 1) for equal allocation (k=1)
  # For k=1: m = (pE + pC) * n
  m_achieved <- (k * p_E + p_C) * n
  
  # Z-statistic under alternative: 
  # z = sqrt(m) * (hr - 1) / (k*hr + 1) - z_{alpha/2}
  # Power = Phi(z)
  
  z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)
  z_stat <- sqrt(m_achieved) * (hr - 1) / (k * hr + 1)
  power_achieved <- pnorm(z_stat - z_alpha_2)
  
  meets <- if (power_achieved >= target_power) "✓ YES" else "✗ NO"
  
  power_results <- rbind(power_results, data.frame(
    n_per_group = n,
    total_n = total_n,
    achieved_power = power_achieved,
    meets_target = meets
  ))
  
  cat(sprintf("n = %d per group (N = %d total): Power = %.6f %s\n",
              n, total_n, power_achieved, meets))
}

cat("\n=== Minimum Admissible Design ===\n")
# Find minimum n that meets target
min_admissible <- power_results$n_per_group[
  power_results$achieved_power >= target_power][1]

cat(sprintf("Minimum n per group meeting target power %.2f: %d\n",
            target_power, min_admissible))

# Verify the continuous vs integer rounding
continuous_solution <- 293.167674
cat(sprintf("\nContinuous solution: %.6f\n", continuous_solution))
cat(sprintf("Floor: %d\n", floor(continuous_solution)))
cat(sprintf("Ceiling: %d\n", ceiling(continuous_solution)))

# Show power at floor(continuous)
floor_n <- floor(continuous_solution)
floor_power <- power_results$achieved_power[power_results$n_per_group == floor_n]
cat(sprintf("\nPower at floor (%d): %.6f %s target\n", 
    floor_n, floor_power, 
    if (floor_power >= target_power) ">=" else "<"))

ceiling_n <- ceiling(continuous_solution)
ceiling_power <- power_results$achieved_power[power_results$n_per_group == ceiling_n]
cat(sprintf("Power at ceiling (%d): %.6f %s target\n", 
    ceiling_n, ceiling_power,
    if (ceiling_power >= target_power) ">=" else "<"))

cat(sprintf("Rounded (ceiling): %d\n", ceiling_n))
cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d: %.6f\n", floor_n, floor_power))

cat(sprintf("✓ Achieves power: %.6f (≥ target: %.2f)\n", ceiling_power, target_power))

plan.estimand: Sample size per arm for survival study comparing two groups via log-rank test
plan.hypothesis: Null: hazard ratio = 1; Alternative: hazard ratio ≠ 1
assumptions: Two-sided log-rank test with Freedman approximation
Equal allocation (1:1 ratio)
Event probabilities represent cumulative incidence over study period
Proportional hazards assumption holds
No censoring other than administrative censoring
Independent observations
scientific_notes: Freedman approximation uses event probabilities (p1, p2) and log hazard ratio to calculate required number of events
The formula accounts for the imbalance in event probabilities between arms under the alternative hypothesis
Integer rounding follows standard ceiling convention for sample size per group
Result will be verified against powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default implementation

# Install and load powerSurvEpi for verification
if (!requireNamespace("powerSurvEpi", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("powerSurvEpi", quiet = TRUE)
}
library(powerSurvEpi)

# Define parameters
alpha <- 0.05  # two-sided significance level
power <- 0.80  # target power
hr <- 0.7      # hazard ratio (alternative)
p_treatment <- 0.3707  # event probability in treatment group
p_control <- 0.4890    # event probability in control group
allocation_ratio <- 1  # equal allocation

# Calculate using powerSurvEpi::ssizeCT.default
# This function uses Freedman approximation
# ssizeCT.default computes sample size per group for two-sample survival test

result <- ssizeCT.default(
  alpha = alpha,
  power = power,
  hazardRatio = hr,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  p2 = p_control
)

# Extract sample size per group
n_per_group_continuous <- result$n

# Standard ceiling rounding for sample size
n_per_group <- ceiling(n_per_group_continuous)

cat("=== Freedman Approximation for Log-Rank Test ===\n")
cat("Parameters:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Significance level (two-sided): %g\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  Target power: %g\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  Hazard ratio: %g\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("  Event probability (treatment): %g\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("  Event probability (control): %g\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("  Allocation ratio: %g\n", allocation_ratio))
cat("\nResults:\n")
cat(sprintf("  Continuous sample size per group: %.4f\n", n_per_group_continuous))
cat(sprintf("  Integer sample size per group (ceiling): %d\n", n_per_group))
cat(sprintf("  Total sample size: %d\n", 2 * n_per_group))

# Verification: compute power at the rounded sample size
# Use powerSurvEpi::powerSurvEpi for power verification
power_check <- powerSurvEpi(
  N = 2 * n_per_group,  # total sample size
  hazardRatio = hr,
  p1 = p_treatment,
  p2 = p_control,
  alpha = alpha
)

cat(sprintf("\nVerification - Achieved power at n=%d per group: %.6f\n", 
            n_per_group, power_check$power)

# Also check power at ceiling - 1
n_lower <- n_per_group - 1
if (n_lower > 0) {
  power_lower <- powerSurvEpi(
    N = 2 * n_lower,
    hazardRatio = hr,
    p1 = p_treatment,
    p2 = p_control,
    alpha = alpha
  )
  cat(sprintf("Power at n=%d per group: %.6f\n", n_lower, power_lower$power))
}

# Output for POWER_AGENT_RESULT
result_list <- list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = n_per_group, unit = "participants_per_group"),
    list(metric = "total_sample_size", value = 2 * n_per_group, unit = "participants"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_check$power, 6), unit = "proportion")
  )
)

cat("\n=== Output for Structured Reporting ===\n")
cat("Primary metric: sample_size = ", n_per_group, " participants_per_group\n")
cat("Achieved power: ", round(power_check$power, 6), "\n")

# Return as JSON
library(jsonlite)
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(result_list, auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     Sample size calculation for the Comparison of Survival Curves
     Between Two Groups under the Cox Proportional-Hazards Model for
     clinical trials.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     ssizeCT.default(power, 
                     k, 
                     pE, 
                     pC, 
                     RR, 
                     alpha = 0.05)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

   power: numeric. power to detect the magnitude of the hazard ratio as
          small as that specified by ‘RR’.

       k: numeric. ratio of participants in group E (experimental
          group) compared to group C (control group).

      pE: numeric. probability of failure in group E (experimental
          group) over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      pC: numeric. probability of failure in group C (control group)
          over the maximum time period of the study (t years).

      RR: numeric. postulated hazard ratio.

   alpha: numeric. type I error rate.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     This is an implementation of the sample size calculation method
     described in Section 14.12 (page 807) of Rosner (2006). The method
     was proposed by Freedman (1982).

     Suppose we want to compare the survival curves between an
     experimental group (E) and a control group (C) in a clinical trial
     with a maximum follow-up of t years.  The Cox proportional hazards
     regression model is assumed to have the form:

                      h(t|X_1)=h_0(t)\exp(beta_1 X_1).                  
     
     Let n_E be the number of participants in the E group and n_C be
     the number of participants in the C group.  We wish to test the
     hypothesis H0: RR=1 versus H1: RR not equal to 1, where
     RR=\exp(beta_1)=underlying hazard ratio for the E group versus the
     C group. Let RR be the postulated hazard ratio, alpha be the
     significance level. Assume that the test is a two-sided test. If
     the ratio of participants in group E compared to group C =
     n_E/n_C=k, then the number of participants needed in each group to
     achieve a power of 1-beta is

           n_E=\frac{m k}{k p_E + p_C}, n_C=\frac{m}{k p_E + p_C}       
     
     where

     m=\frac{1}{k}<=ft(\frac{k RR + 1}{RR - 1}\right)^2<=ft(
     z_{1-alpha/2}+z_{1-beta}
     \right)^2,
     
     and z_{1-alpha/2} is the 100 (1-alpha/2)-th percentile of the
     standard normal distribution N(0, 1).

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     A two-element vector. The first element is n_E and the second
     element is n_C.

_ N_ o_ t_ e:

     (1) The sample size formula assumes that the central-limit theorem
     is valid and hence is appropriate for large samples. (2) n_E and
     n_C will be rounded up to integers.

_ R_ e_ f_ e_ r_ e_ n_ c_ e_ s:

     Freedman, L.S. (1982).  Tables of the number of patients required
     in clinical trials using the log-rank test.  _Statistics in

# n_C = m / (k*pE + pC)

k <- 1  # allocation ratio

# Critical values from standard normal distribution
z_alpha_2 <- qnorm(1 - alpha/2)  # two-sided
z_beta <- qnorm(1 - beta)  # one-sided for power

cat("=== Manual Verification of Freedman Approximation ===\n")
cat(sprintf("Input parameters:\n"))
cat(sprintf("  alpha (two-sided): %.4f\n", alpha))
cat(sprintf("  beta (1 - power): %.4f\n", beta))
cat(sprintf("  power: %.4f\n", power))
cat(sprintf("  HR (RR): %.1f\n", hr))
cat(sprintf("  pE (treatment): %.4f\n", p_treatment))
cat(sprintf("  pC (control): %.4f\n", p_control))
cat(sprintf("  k (allocation ratio): %.1f\n\n", k))

cat(sprintf("  z_{1-alpha/2} (two-sided): %.6f\n", z_alpha_2))
cat(sprintf("  z_{1-beta} (power): %.6f\n\n", z_beta))

# Compute m using the formula
numerator_ratio <- (k * hr + 1) / (hr - 1)

            k, hr, hr, numerator_ratio))

ratio_squared <- numerator_ratio^2
cat(sprintf("  Squared ratio: %.6f\n", ratio_squared))

z_sum <- z_alpha_2 + z_beta
